The t-SNE visualizations show clear separation between dataset sources, suggesting systemic differences (e.g., image resolutions) may be exploited rather than attack-style semantics. The too-good-to-be-true results in Table 3 should be treated with suspicion without ruling out dataset-level confounds.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of incremental novelty (MAFE is largely text extension over existing CLIP fusion methods) and suspicious evaluation results suggesting dataset confounds rather than genuine method performance, not because the defense problem itself is unimportant.

paper_title: Manipulation Concept: Towards Deriving Generalizable and Physics-informed Manipulation Knowledge of Articulated Objects

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Incremental contributions over prior works, reliance on hand-crafted templates, and complex pipeline design

main_rejection_cause.reason: The most relevant prior work SAGE (ICLR 2024 Workshop) also incorporates a VLM and Grounded-SAM for actionable part categories without clarifying the novelty of the current approach or providing direct performance comparison. The manipulation concepts rely on hand-crafted templates which can be labor-intensive when scaling to additional object categories.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: No clear secondary rejection cause is supported by the reviews.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of incremental novelty over prior work like SAGE and reliance on hand-crafted templates, not because the experiments are insufficiently validated.

paper_title: Feature Learning for the High Dimensional Stationary Sch\"odinger Equation with Deep Ritz Method

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Highly restrictive assumptions (squared ReLU activation, specific PDE, lack of boundary conditions) limit practical relevance, and experiments are not compared to alternative PDE training objectives

main_rejection_cause.reason: The analysis relies on very restrictive settings: squared ReLU activation without justification that is difficult to extend to other link functions; specific stationary Schrodinger equation with Neumann boundary conditions not incorporated into algorithmic framework; convergence guarantee in agnostic case is constant-factor to best-in-class rather than globally optimal; and two-neuron analysis relies on aligned first feature assumption.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: The paper lacks head-to-head comparisons against alternative PDE training objectives (e.g., residual-based PINNs) on more challenging benchmarks. Numerical experiments rely on simplifications (d → ∞) and do not provide experiments for finite-dimensional problems to give insight into practical relevance.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of overly restrictive assumptions (squared ReLU, specific PDE, lack of boundary analysis) that limit practical relevance and insufficient experiment completeness (no comparison to PINNs or realistic settings), not because the theoretical framework is poorly presented.

paper_title: PhysicsMinions: Winning Gold Medals in the Latest Physics Olympiads with a Coevolutionary Multimodal Multi-Agent System

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The paper lacks novelty as its multi-agent architecture (visual/logic/review studios with iterative feedback) is insufficiently differentiated from prior actor-critic multi-agent frameworks and contemporaneous work on physics reasoning, despite strong experimental results.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The design motivation is unclear beyond existing actor-critic-style multi-agent models. Reviewers consistently note that key components (image understanding with expert tools, self-refinement/verification loops) have been shown in prior work including Physics-Supernova, Best-of-N methods, and self-refinement approaches. The visual studio also does not participate in the refinement process, and the approach lacks heterogeneity in deployed LLMs.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Computational budget comparisons are insufficient. Reviewers note the paper does not disclose hardware configurations, runtime, GPU usage, or token costs. Given that the method is multi-stage with iterative generation-and-verification, the claim of efficiency is unsubstantiated without fair token/time comparisons to baselines.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because its multi-agent architecture is incrementally building on established actor-critic frameworks without sufficient differentiation in novelty, not because the experiments lack rigor or the problem is unimportant.

paper_title: A Bit of Freedom Goes a Long Way: Classical and Quantum Algorithms for Reinforcement Learning under a Generative Model

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The paper overstates novelty in the infinite-horizon quantum setting by omitting prior closely related work and the hybrid RL model (exploration-generative phases) is insufficiently justified and undermines the core exploration-exploitation challenge of online RL.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The paper omits prior closely related work (e.g., 'Quantum Speedups in Regret Analysis of Infinite Horizon Average-Reward Markov Decision Processes,' ICML 2025) that already reports exponential quantum improvements for average-reward MDPs. The paper therefore does not correctly position its main claimed contribution, and the hybrid exploration-generative RL model remains insufficiently justified with reviewers noting it undermines the core exploration-exploitation challenge.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: No clear secondary rejection cause is supported by the reviews.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of novelty concerns (omitting prior quantum RL work and poorly justified hybrid model), not because of experimental or soundness issues.

paper_title: Voyager: Real-Time Splatting City-Scale 3D Gaussians on Resource-Constrained Devices

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The paper lacks comprehensive ablation studies to separately evaluate the contribution of each component (temporal-aware LoD search and alpha-filtering), leaving the effectiveness of individual design choices unclear.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The ablation study is insufficient. Reviewers consistently note that Table 2 shows the combined effect boosting FPS from 22 to 42, but individual contributions of each component (LoD tree partitioning, fully-streaming traversal, temporal-aware search, alpha-filtering, LUT-based alpha-filtering) are not analyzed. The base model is also not clearly defined.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Limited comparison with latest CUDA-level optimizations like FlashGS. Some reviewer concerns about potentially lowered baseline results (e.g., Octree-GS on HierarchicalGS UrbanScene3D contradicts original paper). Missing references to key LoD-related work.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of incomplete experiments (missing comprehensive ablation studies), not because of fundamental method issues.

paper_title: Perturbations Matter: Sensitivity-Guided Hallucination Detection in LLMs

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The paper's contribution is limited as its theoretical oracle bounds (99% separability) do not translate to practice (75% AUROC), raising questions about scalability and real-world feasibility of per-sample prompt optimization.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The method requires oracle-style per-sample prompt optimization, raising questions about scalability and real-world feasibility. The theoretical claim of near-perfect separability (~99%) is merely an oracle lower bound that does not translate to practice where AUROC is only ~75%. The comparison in Figure 1 was also questioned as potentially unfair (K-means unsupervised vs supervised perturbation sensitivity).

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: The idea of sensitivity-guided detection overlaps with well-known approaches in adversarial robustness and influence functions, and related work on perturbation-based methods (e.g., SPUQ) is not adequately addressed. The paper's novelty claim is overstated given existing work showing good separation using internal representations directly.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because the proposed sensitivity-based approach has questionable feasibility (per-sample prompt optimization) and the theoretical bounds do not translate to practice, not because the experimental evaluation is weak.

paper_title: OPV: Outcome-based Process Verifier for Efficient Long Chain-of-Thought Verification

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The paper's efficiency claims are unsubstantiated (zero computational cost measurements provided) and experimental comparisons are unfair (comparing supervised training with massive expert data against zero-shot baselines).

main_rejection_cause.reason: The paper claims 'efficient' repeatedly but provides ZERO computational cost measurements: no latency, FLOPs, or token counts. Total cost (671B DeepSeek-V3 summarization + 32B OPV verification) makes the claims of efficiency dubious compared to vanilla PV approaches.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Unfair experimental comparisons. Baselines (Qwen3-Max, R1, etc.) use zero-shot prompting while OPV uses 40k expert annotations plus iterative training plus RL. This compares supervised training vs no training, not verification paradigms. Missing critical ablations including training full-CoT PV with the same 40k data.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of unsubstantiated efficiency claims and unfair experimental comparisons (massive annotation budget vs zero-shot baselines), not because the underlying approach (summarize then verify CoTs) lacks merit.

paper_title: DPsurv: Dual-Prototype Evidential Fusion for Uncertainty-Aware and Interpretable Whole Slide Image Survival Prediction

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The paper combines multiple complex modules (GMM, dual-prototype structure, evidential fusion with GRFNs) without sufficient ablation studies to justify the complexity, and the λ hyperparameter selection issue undermines the calibration claims.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The λ hyperparameter for converting interval-valued survival bounds to a single value is set to 0.1, but reviewer analysis shows that performance (IBS, IBLL) significantly improves when λ is moved away from this value, indicating suboptimal calibration and a post-hoc justification that undermines the paper's claims of well-calibrated uncertainty estimates.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: The absence of ablation studies to isolate the contribution of each component (dual-prototype structure, evidential fusion, regularization terms R1 and R2) makes it impossible to assess whether the model's success stems from its intricate design or if simpler alternatives could achieve comparable results.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of methodological soundness issues with hyperparameter selection for calibration, not because the research problem of interpretable uncertainty-aware survival prediction is unimportant.

paper_title: FM-IRL: Flow-Matching for Reward Modeling and Policy Regularization in Reinforcement Learning

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The paper combines existing ideas (FM reward, distillation, AIL) without sufficient novelty and shows only marginal performance improvements over baselines.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The paper largely follows the GAIL recipe and borrows heavily from prior work including DRAIL and Flow Q-Learning. The main algorithmic novelty is limited to using flow-matching loss as rewards, which is not substantially different from diffusion-based reward methods given that flow matching and diffusion models are closely related.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Performance improvements are marginal on several benchmarks, the mode-averaging concern due to regularization in the student policy is not adequately addressed, and comparisons to FM-based baselines may be unfair due to different reward structures.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because it lacks novelty as an incremental A+B+C combination, not because the problem of improving flow-matching-based imitation learning is unimportant.

paper_title: AdaMuon: Adaptive Muon Optimizer

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The paper lacks sufficient baseline comparisons, has weak conceptual justification for its modifications, and scalability to larger models is untested.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The paper only compares against AdamW and Muon, excluding other relevant adaptive or second-order optimizers like Shampoo, Adafactor, or Sophia. Additionally, the ablation studies and sensitivity analyses are insufficient to justify the complex combination of sign stabilization, second-moment accumulation, and RMS alignment.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: The conceptual arguments for the two modifications (sign operation before orthogonalization and element-wise normalization) feel hand-wavy and lack strong empirical support or mathematical grounding. The justification that second-moment serves as a diagonal proxy to local curvature is disputed and not well-supported.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of incomplete experiments with insufficient baseline comparisons, not because the goal of improving Muon optimizer efficiency is unimportant.

paper_title: SparseSSM: Efficient Selective Structured State Space Models Can Be Pruned in One-Shot

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The paper focuses on pruning SSM parameters which constitute a small fraction of total parameters, yielding minimal practical speedup (~1.05x for parallel scan) while the dominant projection layers remain unpruned due to significant performance degradation.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The practical impact of the method is fundamentally limited because SSM parameters constitute only ~5% of total Mamba parameters, and most parameters reside in projection layers. In the common parallel scan deployment regime, the speedup is only ~1.05x, which does not justify the practical relevance claimed by the paper.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: No clear secondary rejection cause is supported by the reviews. While recurrent mode shows better speedups (1.7-2x), this represents a less common deployment scenario and reviewers still questioned the practical motivation.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because the practical feasibility of SSM pruning is limited by minimal speedup gains in common deployment scenarios, not because the theoretical contribution of adapting OBS to SSMs is weak.

paper_title: SteinDiff: Resolving the Contractivity Trap via Reference-free Stein Regularization

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The paper has serious mathematical flaws in its theoretical justification, including applying fixed-point theory to time-varying operators and incorrect application of Stein's lemma, without providing convergence guarantees to the correct distribution.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The paper incorrectly applies Krasnosel'skii-Mann theorem which requires a fixed map, but the method applies it to time-varying operators. Additionally, the correctness of using Stein's lemma is questionable since the algorithm does not preserve correct marginals, and no formal convergence proof to the correct distribution is provided.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: The premise of the 'contractivity trap' is flawed as numerical discretization of ODEs does not require Lipschitz constant < 1; convergence holds for bounded Lipschitz constants albeit with exponential factors. The end goal is weak convergence to the distribution, not pointwise trajectory convergence.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of serious mathematical soundness issues in its theoretical framework, not because the empirical results showing improved FID at low NFE are weak.

paper_title: AlphaVAE: Unified End-to-End RGBA Image Reconstruction and Generation with Alpha-Aware Representation Learning

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Unresolved concerns about evaluation metric validity (LPIPS under alpha blending) and insufficient justification for the patch discriminator design

main_rejection_cause.reason: LPIPS validity under alpha blending remains unresolved after rebuttal - the feature-domain mismatch concern is not fully settled, and the backbone network trained on standard RGB images may produce unreliable measurements on alpha-composited images

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Patch discriminator justification is insufficient - no quantitative benchmarking such as sharpness/NIQE or discriminator variants was provided, leaving the design choice inadequately validated

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of unresolved concerns about evaluation metric soundness (LPIPS under alpha blending) and insufficient patch discriminator justification, not because the core RGBA VAE framework lacks merit.

paper_title: On Rademacher Complexity-based Generalization Bounds for the Transformer Architecture

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Multiple critical soundness issues including missing/unstated assumptions, internal inconsistencies, undefined notation, unclear approximations, and absence of clearly stated theorems that undermine trust in the core theoretical results

main_rejection_cause.reason: Serious soundness issues pervade the paper: missing/unstated assumptions (stability assumption at L319), internal inconsistencies (equation at L328 invalid according to L310), undefined notation (symbol ~ not defined), and unclear approximations undermine trust in the core results

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Presentation lacks rigor required for a theory paper - missing theorem statements, no equation numbers, lack of formal mathematical structure (definition, lemma, theorem, proofs), and vague experimental descriptions hinder understanding and reproducibility

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of serious methodological soundness issues (missing assumptions, internal inconsistencies, undefined notation) and lack of rigor, not because the general topic of Rademacher complexity bounds for transformers is unimportant.

paper_title: Handling Tabular Data under Coupled Shifts of Feature Missingness and Distributional Change

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Missing critical experimental components including naturally-occurring missingness evaluation, cross-domain evaluation, imputation quality assessment, and comparisons to LLM-based imputation methods, combined with incomplete ablation coverage

main_rejection_cause.reason: Missing critical components: naturally-occurring missingness scenarios, realistic settings without prior knowledge of missing columns, cross-domain evaluation, imputation quality assessment against baselines (mean, k-NN, MICE, GAIN), and comparisons with LLM-based imputation methods

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: The observation that coupled shifts exceed additive effects may not consistently hold across all datasets, and the assumption that entire columns are missing does not reflect real-world partial missingness scenarios

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of incomplete experiments (missing natural missingness, cross-domain evaluation, imputation baselines), not because the problem formulation or method design is fundamentally flawed.

paper_title: Agentic 3D Scene Generation with Spatially Contextualized VLMs

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Limited algorithmic novelty (primarily system-level composition), insufficient 3D evaluation (relies on 2D metrics without quantitative 3D accuracy, geometry consistency, or spatial relation correctness), and heavy reliance on external generators that confounds attribution of quality

main_rejection_cause.reason: Evaluation relies on 2D rendered metrics (CLIP, BLIP, LPIPS) without quantitative validation of 3D accuracy, geometry consistency, or spatial relation correctness - critical aspects for a 3D generation paper

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: The contribution is largely system-level composition rather than algorithmic breakthrough - scene graphs, point-cloud restoration, ergonomic layout optimization build directly on existing methods (ATISS, Point-M2AE, Fast3R), and quality heavily depends on external APIs (Meshy.ai) making it difficult to disentangle the contribution of the spatial context mechanism

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of insufficient 3D-specific evaluation and limited algorithmic novelty, not because the high-level concept of spatially contextualized VLMs for 3D generation is uninteresting.

paper_title: Growing with Your Embodied Agent: A Human-in-the-Loop Lifelong Code Generation Framework for Long-Horizon Manipulation Skills

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Limited technical novelty (system primarily integrates existing ideas), missing strong baseline comparisons (VLA models, hierarchical/lifelong RL methods), and insufficient human subjects study specification for core HITL contribution

main_rejection_cause.reason: Limited technical novelty - the system primarily integrates existing ideas (HITL, RAG, code generation) rather than introducing new algorithmic contributions; the core contribution is conceptual integration rather than novel algorithmic design

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Missing or weak comparisons to strong baselines (VLA models like OpenVLA and π0, hierarchical/lifelong RL methods like HiLLa, BOSS, Text2Reward), and insufficient specification of human subjects study (no information on user demographics, expertise, or inter-user variability)

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of limited technical novelty (integration of existing ideas) and missing strong baseline comparisons, not because the long-horizon manipulation demonstration is unimpressive.

paper_title: FU-DWS: Effective Federated Domain Unlearning via Domain-aware Weight Surgery

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The method relies on heuristic thresholds and assumes channel-wise independence without principled criteria, limiting its theoretical soundness and practical applicability. Additionally, the motivation for federated domain unlearning (FDU) as distinct from conventional federated unlearning is not well-justified.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The method design relies on heuristic thresholds tau_p and tau_f that are selected empirically without principled criteria, and assumes channel-wise independence ignoring potential inter-channel correlations, which could cause partial forgetting or unintentional degradation of domain-invariant features.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: The motivation for focusing on federated domain unlearning (FDU) is not well-justified, as the distinction from conventional federated unlearning is unconvincing and prior work already demonstrates handling of non-IID data.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of method soundness concerns including heuristic threshold tuning and channel independence assumptions, not because of experiment issues.

paper_title: Integer-Centric Neural Video Compression

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The quantization method significantly reduces performance, especially at higher bitrates, and the paper fails to cite or compare with closely related prior works on cross-platform integer networks for data compression, making it impossible to position the contribution.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The paper omits key related work citations (particularly ICLR 2019 Integer Networks for Data Compression) and fails to compare with previous cross-platform neural codec techniques, making it impossible to position the contribution relative to prior art.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: The multiply-twice integerization lacks strong theoretical foundation, and the primary performance gain appears to come from the memory model (standard LSTM), not the quantization method itself, which reduces performance significantly.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of missing comparisons with closely related prior works and performance degradation from quantization, not because the core integer training concept lacks merit.

paper_title: Can LLMs Alleviate Catastrophic Forgetting in Graph Continual Learning? A Systematic Study

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The paper identifies evaluation protocol flaws (task ID leakage) but fails to clearly establish how these diagnosis issues necessitate or motivate the specific architectural choices in SimGCL (graph prompts, LoRA, prototypes), creating a conceptual gap between the stated problem and proposed solution.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The paper's introduction positions the main contribution as correcting unfair GCL evaluation protocols (task ID leakage), yet the proposed method SimGCL operates at the architectural/representation level without a clear conceptual link explaining how protocol flaws necessitate the design of graph-prompt verbalization, one-time LoRA tuning, and prototype classifier.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: The paper lacks theoretical grounding for why the combination of graph prompts, LoRA fine-tuning, and prototype-based classification alleviates forgetting. The mechanism behind its robustness is not formally analyzed, and the approach is largely empirical.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of the misalignment between the stated motivation (correcting evaluation protocols) and the proposed method (architectural solution), not because the experiments lack coverage.

paper_title: UniMMVSR: A Unified Multi-Modal Framework for Cascaded Video Super-Resolution

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The paper combines existing techniques (channel/token concatenation, RoPE, cascaded modeling) without substantial architectural novelty, and the evaluation relies on no-reference metrics (MUSIQ, DOVER) known for biases toward their training data, with insufficient user study validation.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The core contributions (channel concatenation for LR video, token-wise concatenation for references, separate conditional RoPE) are standard practices in the field rather than fundamental innovations. The improvements upon existing components like conditioning strategy, degradation pipeline, and training order are incremental.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: The evaluation relies heavily on no-reference metrics (MUSIQ, DOVER) known for biases, and while a user study with 20 participants was provided in rebuttal, the scale is insufficient for rigorous validation of the method's performance.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of limited architectural novelty and reliance on biased evaluation metrics, not because the unified multi-modal framework lacks practical value.

paper_title: TGPO: Temporal Grounded Policy Optimization for Signal Temporal Logic Tasks

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The method can only handle a restricted fragment of STL (no disjunctions, no liveness properties like G(F...)), yet claims to solve general STL tasks, overstating its scope. The exponential growth of temporal assignment search space with subgoal count remains a significant scalability limitation.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The paper overclaims what types of STL it can handle. It cannot process disjunctions or liveness properties (G(F...)), which are important in maintenance tasks or repeated periodic tasks. The current fragment supported needs to be formally defined and clearly distinguished from STL forms the method cannot handle.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: The number of different time-variable assignments can grow exponentially with the number of subgoals, and this is further complicated for nested and/or disjunctive formulas. The formal connection between dense rewards and STL satisfaction is not rigorously established.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of overclaiming its STL scope and scalability concerns with exponential time-variable assignment growth, not because the empirical results are weak.

paper_title: SSD: Spatial-Semantic Head Decoupling for Efficient Autoregressive Image Generation

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The paper lacks comprehensive evaluation: experiments only on Janus-Pro without full evaluation on second model, missing FID metrics for lossy compression, and unexplained anomalous baseline throughput.

main_rejection_cause.reason: All experiments conducted on single model family (Janus-Pro). Authors added analysis on LlamaGen-XL but failed to provide full performance evaluation on second model, as explicitly requested by multiple reviewers. This leaves the central claim of generalizability unsubstantiated.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Missing FID metrics for a lossy compression technique. After promising to provide FID results during rebuttal, authors failed to deliver them. Additionally, baseline throughput anomaly (decreasing with increased batch size) was never addressed, casting doubt on the claimed 6.6x speedup.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of insufficient and incomplete experiments (single model evaluation, missing FID metrics, unexplained baseline anomaly), not because of method issues (the head decoupling approach is novel and well-motivated).

paper_title: Investigating Advanced Reasoning of Large Language Models via Black-Box Interaction

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The paper lacks sufficient analysis of why models fail and insufficient validation of the automated dataset generation framework.

main_rejection_cause.reason: Paper identifies that LLMs lack efficient exploration strategies but does not deeply investigate why. The analysis shows that the deficiency exists but lacks exploration into contributing factors (long-context reasoning, feedback utilization, planning capabilities). The authors did not provide metrics on token/turn efficiency to understand if better models achieve success through superior strategy or more computation.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: No clear secondary rejection cause is supported by the reviews.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of insufficient experiments (lacking 'why' analysis of model failures), not because the black-box interaction paradigm lacks novelty or significance.

paper_title: QuantDemoire: Quantization with Outlier Aware for Image Demoiréing

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The paper has insufficient novelty and questionable soundness of the sampling-based activation quantization method.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The sampling-based activation quantization has high variance - subsampling entries does not change the underlying distribution and extreme outliers may or may not be captured. Reviewers demonstrated theoretically and empirically that even multiple runs cannot adequately address this variance issue. The method offers no advantage over robust estimators like 99.99% percentile.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Components of the method resemble existing approaches: smoothing/clipping approach resembles OmniQuant, preserving outliers in FP resembles LLM-int8, and frequency-aware calibration shows marginal effect in ablations. The method lacks substantial novel contributions beyond combining existing techniques.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of method soundness issues (high-variance sampling for activation quantization) and limited novelty (components resemble existing methods), not because the demoireing application is insignificant.

paper_title: Revisiting Theory of Contrastive Learning for Domain Generalization

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The paper has insufficient empirical grounding to support its theoretical claims and limited practical utility.

main_rejection_cause.reason: Despite rebuttal adding empirical section, the analysis remains too limited. Reviewers explicitly requested experiments on standard DG benchmarks (DomainBed), reproducing Saunshi et al. core experiments, and validating the predicted role of intra-class variance. The paper does not demonstrate whether minimizing theoretical quantities leads to better downstream performance.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Presentation issues undermine evaluation: missing definitions for key notations (W^mu, R, Re_S(F)), idealized assumptions (latent class means, uniform downstream sampling) not validated, and abstract promises guarantees for new downstream classes but no theorem accounts for unseen classes. The gap from CL to DG is studied extensively in prior work.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of insufficient experiments (limited empirical grounding after rebuttal) and presentation issues (missing definitions, idealized assumptions), not because the theoretical framework lacks soundness.

paper_title: P$^3$-SAM: Native 3D Part Segmentation

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The paper's performance gains are primarily attributed to dataset scale and pretrained models rather than novel architectural contributions.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The architectural design closely follows 2D SAM with only minor modifications (exchanging feature extractor with Sonata). Reviewers questioned whether the core contribution is the dataset rather than the model. The multi-head predictor, claimed as a key architectural insight, was not analyzed in depth to explain why it leads to better performance. Similar attempts to extend SAM to 3D exist (e.g., PointSAM).

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Dataset curation process lacks quantitative validation. The automatic part annotation via geometric heuristics (merging small parts, adjacency rules) may introduce bias, and no error analysis of annotations was provided. Reviewers requested ablation on data quality and scale curves but received insufficient analysis to determine if improvements stem from model architecture or simply larger training data.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of limited method novelty (architecture closely follows SAM with minor changes), not because the dataset contribution or experimental results are weak.

paper_title: Fairness for the People, by the People: Minority Collective Action

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The paper's method has significant soundness issues related to unrealistic assumptions about user capabilities (label flipping vs feature manipulation) and feasibility concerns about firm-side counteraction, combined with incomplete experiments missing key baselines

main_rejection_cause.reason: The paper assumes users can flip labels but cannot change features, which is unrealistic in practical settings like hiring where users can manipulate both. Additionally, firms could counteract the collective action by detecting accuracy drops.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Missing key pre-processing baselines like AIF360 methods, and limited dataset variety that doesn't fully demonstrate the ACA framing's practical utility.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because the method's assumptions about user-side label manipulation are unrealistic and the experiments lack key baseline comparisons, not because the underlying motivation for user-driven fairness is uninteresting.

paper_title: DCPO: Dynamic Clipping Policy Optimization

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The paper lacks sufficient experimental support for its proposed method, particularly demonstrating benefits only on a single model family and failing to compare against directly relevant entropy-aware methods

main_rejection_cause.reason: The method was only validated on Qwen family models, and experiments with LLaMA-based methods showed performance degradation. Additionally, comparisons with directly relevant entropy-aware methods (beyond GRPO variants) were missing initially, and performance gains are marginal.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: The baseline DAPO performance differs from the original paper's reported results, raising questions about whether comparisons are fair. No code or models are available for reproducibility.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because the experiments demonstrate the method only on one model family and lack crucial comparisons with related entropy-aware methods, not because the underlying ideas of dynamic clipping and advantage standardization lack merit.

paper_title: Adaptive Symmetrization of the KL Divergence

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The paper has theoretical issues in its mathematical derivation (entropy of data distribution ignored in empirical dual problem) and weak experiments limited to low-dimensional synthetic data with poor FID scores

main_rejection_cause.reason: The transition from the idealized problem to the empirical dual problem ignores the entropy of the data distribution, which invalidates the claimed equivalence. The paper also lacks discussion on why symmetrizing KL divergence offers statistical advantages.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Experiments are primarily on low-dimensional synthetic 2D datasets, and the high-dimensional CelebA FID scores are too poor to demonstrate practical utility. Missing comparisons with diffusion models and other state-of-the-art generative models.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of theoretical flaws in the optimization derivation and experiments limited to low-dimensional synthetic data with poor high-dimensional results, not because the core idea of using proxy models for Jeffreys divergence is conceptually uninteresting.

paper_title: Struct2Real: A Systematic Framework for Accurate and Efficient Structure-Grounded Object Image Generation

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The paper presents a heavily engineered system with limited conceptual novelty, demonstrating effectiveness only on simple geometric objects while lacking comprehensive evaluation and details on computational costs

main_rejection_cause.reason: The proposed system follows the same recipe as existing works on part-based 3D generation using MLLMs with feedback loops, representing primarily an engineering integration rather than fundamentally new algorithmic contribution.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Experiments focus on simple geometric objects; limited evaluation on complex shapes or articulated/deformable objects. The limited dataset (30 categories, 3000 samples) and primitive library restrict demonstrated applicability.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because the technical novelty is limited and the system is primarily an engineering integration of existing techniques, not because the StructMap representation and structure-grounded generation task lack merit.

paper_title: One-for-All Model Initialization with Frequency-Domain Knowledge

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The paper lacks rigorous theoretical justification for applying DCT to non-spatial weight tensors, with reviewers finding the connection between weight-space frequency and function-space smoothness unconvincing despite empirical evidence

main_rejection_cause.reason: The application of DCT directly to weight tensors lacks theoretical justification. Unlike images, weights lack inherent spatial structure, and the assumption of continuity in weight space is not theoretically grounded. The paper's cited work (Rahaman et al. 2019) addresses function space, not weight space.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: No clear secondary rejection cause is supported by the reviews.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because the theoretical justification for applying DCT to weight space is insufficient, not because the empirical results or practical utility of the method are lacking.

paper_title: Language Models as Noisy Experts for Sequential Causal Discovery

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The paper lacks sufficient methodological novelty - its core components (PAG estimation and Bayesian approach) are not original contributions - and relies on restrictive assumptions (linear Gaussian SEM, stationarity, single confounder) that limit applicability to real-world scenarios.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The core components of BLANCE - PAG estimation via FCI and Bayesian integration of LLM priors - are not novel contributions. The PAG structure is a standard and mature theoretical tool, and converting LLM knowledge to priors is a direct application of existing Bayesian causal discovery ideas.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: The method relies on restrictive assumptions including linear Gaussian SEM for parameter estimation (limiting applicability to nonlinear real-world systems), stationarity of causal structure across batches (violated in many streaming scenarios), and single confounder identification heuristic (no theoretical guarantee).

paper_title: AIGID-RFT: Reinforcement Fine-Tuning Multimodal LLMs for AI-Generated Image Detection

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The paper's method is not feasible at realistic inference speeds (0.284 FPS compared to 15 FPS of alternatives), and the Cross Layer Forensic Adapter lacks novelty as it is merely an MLP-based feature fusion module with standard Up/Down-projection and LayerNorm techniques.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The proposed method runs at only 0.284 FPS, which is impractically slow compared to existing methods that can run at 15 FPS. This severe computational bottleneck makes the approach unrealistic for real-world AI-generated image detection.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: The Cross Layer Forensic Adapter (CLFA) is essentially an MLP-based feature fusion module using standard techniques (Up/Down-projection, LayerNorm) that lack sufficient innovation tailored to the AIGC detection task. Additionally, the reinforcement learning training directly adopts GRPO without modifications.

paper_title: InfVSR: Breaking Length Limits of Generic Video Super-Resolution

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The experiments are incomplete and lack video results necessary to evaluate temporal consistency, which is the paper's main claimed contribution. Without visual demonstrations, it is impossible to assess whether long-term semantic and pixel-level consistency is maintained as claimed.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The paper lacks video results in the supplementary material, making it extremely challenging to evaluate temporal consistency which is the main claimed advantage of the method. The supplementary visualizations showing text images not faithful to ground truth suggest generative instability issues.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: The training uses only 1K clips from REDS dataset, whereas previous VSR methods typically use 100K-1M video clips. This raises questions about generalizability. Additionally, the training data focuses on objects (cars, cats) rather than human faces, limiting effectiveness on Deepfake/face-swap detection.

paper_title: CondiQuant: Condition Number Based Low-Bit Quantization for Image Super-Resolution

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The experiments are incomplete and limited to a single architecture (SwinIR-light), with insufficient demonstration of generalization to other SR networks or low-level vision tasks. The authors' rebuttal only provided EDSR results, not addressing the requested evaluations on arbitrary-scale backbones or larger SwinIR variants.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The evaluation is limited to a single architecture (SwinIR-light) without demonstrating generalization to other SR networks like SwinIR-B, MambaIRv2-light, RCAN, or EDSR. The method's claim of being architecture-agnostic is not empirically validated. Additionally, testing on other low-level tasks (denoising, deblurring) is missing.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Implementation details are insufficiently described, including which layers get processed/skipped, numerical stability for large SVDs, and integration details with 2DQuant. The configuration in table2(d) lacks explanation, and comparison with other quantization methods that also enable weight optimization is missing.

paper_title: LLM-IQA: Standard-guided MLLM for Mix-grained Image Quality Assessment

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The paper lacks methodological innovation as it is primarily an application of sophisticated prompt engineering rather than a novel IQA framework. The claimed segmentation and masking approach contradicts the ablation study results showing masks perform poorly while bounding boxes work well.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The proposed method combines segmentation, discrete-level prompting, and score aggregation - this is an application of prompt engineering rather than a novel IQA framework. The strategy of prompting MLLMs with predefined standards and averaging local patch scores has been employed in prior work (e.g., Wen et al. for video quality assessment, Q-Bench). The contribution is tied to the specific MLLM (mPLUG-Owl3) used.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: There is a critical internal contradiction: Section 3 describes segmentation and masks, but the ablation study (Table 3, Exp 5) shows masks perform poorly (SRCC 0.632 on SPAQ) while bounding boxes perform well. The paper even claims on page 8 that bounding boxes are necessary. This fundamental conflict between methodological description and experimental validation undermines reliability.

paper_title: Harnessing Model Uncertainty for Adaptive Causal Debiasing in Visual Question Answering

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The method fundamentally misrepresents itself as a counterfactual approach when it is actually a feature ablation technique; causal claims are overstated, and mathematical formulations contain errors and internal inconsistencies.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The method is presented as a counterfactual reasoning system but is actually a feature ablation using contrastive residual, making causal semantics overstated. Reviewer jNhM identifies that counterfactuals require formal do-calculus (abduction, action, prediction), but the method uses only contrastive residual. Mathematical formulations contain errors: Figure 1 contradicts the math (suggests cutting question path but math replaces vision paths with constant), potential error in gating mechanism with hyperparameter gamma, and ambiguity in defining constant C.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Experiments rely heavily on older VQA backbones and lack tests on modern Transformer-based or VLM architectures. Missing computational overhead analysis (FLOPs, memory, latency) for ensemble uncertainty and multi-head designs. Baseline CF-VQA not included in Tables 4 and 6. The method performs worse than TPCL and even worse than BLIP on VQAv2 in Table 4.

paper_title: Mixture of Neuron Experts

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The paper does not convincingly establish fundamentally new conceptual contribution beyond applying top-k pruning to GLU-style experts, with performance gains being modest and dependent on specific architectural choices.

main_rejection_cause.reason: Multiple reviewers expressed concerns that the core idea of neuron-level sparsification is conceptually close to existing approaches such as Product-Key Memory and Ultra-Sparse Memory Networks. Reviewer REoY notes the concept was already introduced in earlier work and scaling attempts were made. The paper does not convincingly establish a fundamentally new conceptual contribution; it is a nesting of MoE and Product-Key Models without discussing this relationship.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: No clear secondary rejection cause is supported by the reviews.

paper_title: Stealing and Defending the Ends of LLMs

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Experiments are conducted under small-scale models and datasets without sufficient evidence that the approach scales to larger, realistic settings, and the authors did not provide adequate large-scale experiments during rebuttal.

main_rejection_cause.reason: Almost all reviewers point out that experiments are conducted under small-scale models and datasets. Reviewer n4Zu states it is hard to measure actual usefulness without realistic size models like Llama3-7B and realistic tasks/datasets. The baseline comparison (LLM with random SP initialization) is not convincing; performance of base LLM without soft prompt should be included. Experiments with comparison to other PEFT methods like LoRA are missing.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Evidence for generation tasks like summarization is weak or inconsistent. Generation metrics (ROUGE/BERTScore) and CAP-on vs CAP-off comparisons are needed. Extension to large VLMs remains unexplored. The authors did not provide sufficient experiments on large-scale models during the rebuttal, leaving concerns unresolved.

paper_title: Neuro-MoBRE: Exploring Multi-subject Multi-task Intracranial Decoding via Explicit Heterogeneity Resolving

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The paper lacks experiments on publicly available benchmarks, overclaims zero-shot generalization (actually cross-subject), and does not compare unseen subject performance against strong baselines.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The model is evaluated solely on one private iEEG dataset with no verification on any public iEEG benchmarks. Reviewers note the paper should either include experiments on low-SNR modalities like EEG/MEG to test robustness or clearly reframe the motivation. The claim about 'zero-shot generalization' is overclaimed - the scenario involves unseen subjects within the same dataset, which should be characterized as cross-subject generalization, not zero-shot. The paper doesn't compare unseen subject decoding performance against other baselines.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: The paper claims to address low-SNR conditions but evaluates exclusively on high-SNR intracranial data, which doesn't demonstrate robustness to low-SNR or applicability to non-invasive modalities. The paper identifies low SNR as a main challenge in the introduction but the current experiments do not address or validate performance under low-SNR conditions.

paper_title: Disentangling Content from Style to Overcome Shortcut Learning: A Hybrid Generative-Discriminative Learning Framework

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The paper combines existing techniques without sufficient theoretical insight into why this particular combination succeeds; the orthogonality assumption lacks formal justification, and three of four reviewers fundamentally misunderstood the work indicating severe presentation failures.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The framework primarily combines existing techniques without sufficient theoretical insight. The proposed 'Invariance Pre-training Principle' closely parallels established concepts: domain randomization (keep sample invariant to style in supervised learning) and denoising autoencoders (self-supervised approach). Both techniques already aim to improve generalization through invariance. The claim of being the first to operationalize this principle is not convincing. Authors argue their work differs from prior art because it addresses representation learning rather than style transfer, but both share the fundamental motivation of separating style and content representations.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Three of four reviewers fundamentally misunderstood the work, indicating systemic communication issues rather than isolated misreadings. Baseline methods in Figure 1 remain difficult to interpret. The evaluation protocol is not clearly specified. The paper fails to clearly articulate: (1) the guiding intuition behind the design, (2) what meaningfully differentiates it from prior work, and (3) why the approach should succeed theoretically. Reviewers note the orthogonality assumption remains philosophically questionable - content and style are not simply orthogonal; sometimes content itself becomes part of the style.

paper_title: StageVAR: Stage-Aware Acceleration for Visual Autoregressive Models

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The paper received mixed reviews (3x 4, 1x 6) with key concerns about novelty and experimental completeness. Reviewers found that the three-stage decomposition largely refines FastVAR's two-stage insight, and the CFG elimination technique is more heuristic than academic discovery. Critical experimental concerns include missing standard metrics (FID/IS) and insufficient comparisons with FastVAR and SkipVAR. While the rebuttal addressed some concerns, key limitations on novelty and technical soundness remained unresolved.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The three-stage decomposition largely refines FastVAR's two-stage insight, and at least 50% of the acceleration effect comes from CFG elimination, which is closer to a simple heuristic than an academic discovery. The core contributions are incremental over prior work.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Results are not evaluated on standard image evaluation metrics (FID/IS), and comparisons with prior research (FastVAR, SkipVAR) are insufficient. The GenEval and DPG benchmarks do not precisely capture image quality degradation.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of limited novelty (incremental over FastVAR with heuristic CFG elimination), not because it fails to address the acceleration problem.

paper_title: Better know nothing than half-know anything: A Precise and Efficient Dataset for Scientific Reasoning in Language Models

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The paper received scores of 4/6/4 with positive agreement on motivation and empirical results, but persistent concerns about implementation transparency, decontamination verification, model-based filtering bias, and limited methodological novelty. While the rebuttal addressed reproducibility gaps and provided scaling evidence, core concerns remained unresolved.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The pipeline combines standard techniques (LLM extraction, MinHash deduplication, answer distillation) without introducing new algorithms or theoretical insights. The methodological novelty is limited beyond careful engineering and filtering.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Model-based filtering may bias the dataset toward problems current models can already solve, contradicting the goal of creating challenging training data for improving model capabilities.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of limited methodological novelty (standard curation techniques without new algorithms), not because the empirical results are weak.

paper_title: SRDiffusion: Accelerate Diffusion Inference via Sketching-Rendering Cooperation

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The paper received mixed reviews (6/4/6/2) with concerns about limited novelty, reliance on questionable VBench metrics, and practical deployment challenges. While the rebuttal addressed some concerns with user studies and clearer motivation, the core novelty concerns persisted, and the method was seen as incrementally building on existing techniques like SDXL-refiner and Wan2.2.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The core concept of using different models for different noise levels is not novel - similar approaches have been used in SDXL-refiner and Wan2.2 (MoE with high/low denoise models). The technical contribution remains a heuristic switching strategy between two pre-existing models.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: The paper's motivation relies on VBench scores claiming Wan 14B and 1.3B have similar quality, but VBench may not capture the perceptual gap that is apparent to human eyes. This undermines the foundational premise.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of limited novelty (concept already used in SDXL-refiner and Wan2.2), not because it fails to achieve acceleration.

paper_title: TRACE: Transcoder-based Concept Editing

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The paper received mixed reviews with concerns about positioning vs. closely related SAE-style concept editing and whether the evaluation supports the strongest claims. While the rebuttal added many experiments and improved coverage, remaining questions about architectural dependency (TRACE only works with models having post-text-encoder bottleneck layers) and robustness methodology (attacks tuned on SD1.4 may not transfer to newer architectures) made the contribution feel less settled for acceptance.

main_rejection_cause.reason: For models without a clear post-text-encoder bottleneck (like SD1.4), the 'insert an identity block' workaround is fragile and easy to bypass, weakening the core persistence/tamper-resistance claim in adversarial settings.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Robustness results rely on attacks originally tuned for SD1.4, which may not transfer to SD3.5 or FLUX without model-specific optimization, making it harder to fully trust the robustness claims.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of architectural dependency concerns (TRACE only naturally works with specific model architectures), not because the transcoder idea itself lacks merit.

paper_title: VoxSet: Sparse Voxel Set Tokenizer for 3D Shape Generation

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The paper received scores of 4/2/4/8/4 with widespread criticism for limited novelty (incremental hybridization), incomplete experimental comparisons (missing Spark3D/HiTem3D), and insufficient generation evaluation (primarily qualitative). The rebuttal did not fully address these concerns.

main_rejection_cause.reason: VoxSet directly combines two existing SOTA approaches (sparse voxels and vector set) without introducing new architectural or theoretical insights. The contribution is largely pragmatic hybridization with heavy emphasis on engineering over novel ideas.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Generation evaluation is primarily qualitative with Figure 4 showing alignment issues. Key baselines (Spark3D, HiTem3D) are missing from comparisons. The paper only shows geometry generation without material generation, and quantitative comparison for image-to-3D is absent.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of limited novelty (incremental combination of existing approaches), not because the hybrid tokenizer lacks practical value.

paper_title: MANGO: Natural Multi-speaker 3D Talking Head Generation via 2D-Lifted Enhancement

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Weak conceptual novelty and limited visual quality compared to 2D SOTA

main_rejection_cause.reason: The framework is perceived as a simple combination of existing modules (diffusion and dual-audio processing) rather than a fundamental breakthrough. The '2D-Lifted Enhancement' is viewed as a specialized fix for noisy pseudo-3D training data rather than a general conceptual advance.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Missing key 2D SOTA comparisons (VASA-1, OmniHuman-1, HALLO3) and industry-grade 3D pipeline comparisons (NVIDIA Audio2Face). Visual quality gap remains substantial compared to SOTA pixel generators.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because the method provides weak conceptual novelty as an incremental combination of existing approaches and fails to compare against current 2D SOTA visual quality, not because the core dual-speaker modeling idea lacks merit.

paper_title: Holistic protean block for long-range DNA sequence modeling

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Insufficient novelty and marginal, non-significant performance improvements

main_rejection_cause.reason: Most architectural components are incremental improvements of established techniques (multi-scale convolutions, gated convolutions, dual-axis feature gating). The frequency-domain DNA analysis is novel but obscured by excessive packaging of incremental designs with unclear, non-standard terminology.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Performance improvements on NT benchmark are within margins of error relative to standard deviations. Missing comparisons with strong local motif extractors. Different pre-trained models used for different downstream tasks, contradicting foundation model concept.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because the method offers limited architectural novelty with incremental improvements over existing techniques, not because the frequency-domain DNA modeling idea lacks significance.

paper_title: Draft-and-Target Sampling for Video Generation Policy

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Limited technical novelty as primarily an application of speculative decoding to video generation

main_rejection_cause.reason: The core contribution applies speculative decoding to video generation with straightforward modifications (large-step-size-ODE draft model, progressive acceptance, token chunking). Lacks fundamentally new algorithmic contribution beyond adaptation to a new domain.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Only tests on robotic environment datasets (iTHOR, Meta-World, LIBERO) with no experiments on diverse video data like Kinetics-700. Limited speedup (~2x) with unclear if it outweighs added complexity.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because the method provides limited technical novelty as a straightforward application of speculative decoding to video generation, not because the problem of efficient video generation for robotics lacks importance.

paper_title: Rate-Distortion Optimization for Transformer Inference

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Limited experimental validation and presentation clarity issues

main_rejection_cause.reason: Limited baseline comparisons - only compares against Deflate for lossless compression without state-of-the-art methods like zstd or tensor quantization. No end-to-end evaluation in real multi-GPU or cross-machine setup.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Presentation issues including imprecise terminology ('differentiable quantization'), contradictory language, and unclear related work positioning. Theoretical bounds lack actionable insights.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because the experiments lack comprehensive baseline comparisons and real-world evaluation, not because the theoretical V-entropy framework lacks merit.

paper_title: Spectral-inspired Operator Learning with Limited Data and Unknown Physics

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Unfair experimental setup that gives SINO structural advantages not adequately disentangled from architectural contributions

main_rejection_cause.reason: Training setup unfairness: SINO trained on fine temporal grid (POL) with RK4 integration while baselines trained on coarse grid (DOL) with single-step rollouts. This gives SINO 100-1000x more effective training samples and better stability, not attributable to architecture alone. No released code for verification.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: SINO inference time is comparable to numerical spectral solvers, undermining practical value of neural operator for acceleration. This defeats the core purpose of neural surrogate models for PDEs.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because the experiments use an unfair training setup where SINO has structural advantages from fine temporal grid and RK4 stepping not properly disentangled from architectural contributions, not because the spectral-inspired neural operator concept lacks merit.

paper_title: Reframing Dense Action Detection (RefDense): A New Perspective on Problem Solving and a Novel Optimization Strategy

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The paper lacks sufficient novelty distinction from two-stream methods and has unresolved benchmarking fairness concerns that undermine the validity of performance claims.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The paper does not sufficiently distinguish its decomposition approach from established two-stream networks and recent related work (e.g., CVPR 2024 dual DETR, CVPR 2023 decomposed cross-modal distillation), making the novelty claims unconvincing.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Unresolved concerns about baseline parity, hyperparameter fairness, and corrected tables (Tables 3 and 5) undermine confidence in the reported performance improvements.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of insufficient novelty distinction from prior two-stream methods, not because the problem of temporal dense action detection is unimportant.

paper_title: Connecting Where You Look With What You Understand: Trajectory-Driven Localized Understanding for Interactive Vision-Language Models

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The paper fails to properly distinguish from highly related prior work (NAACL 2024) and lacks critical ablation studies while presenting unfair backbone comparisons.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The paper does not cite or compare with a highly related prior publication (NAACL 2024 on Interactive Regional Understanding in LVLMs) that shares nearly identical motivation and overlapping tasks, making the contribution appear incremental.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Unfair backbone comparisons (TraceVLM vs. other region-understanding methods under different backbones) and inconsistent benchmark results without explanation undermine the validity of claimed improvements.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because it insufficiently distinguishes from prior work and has unresolved evaluation fairness concerns, not because trajectory-aware video understanding is uninteresting.

paper_title: Which Heads Matter for Reasoning? RL-Guided KV Cache Compression

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The concept of 'reasoning heads' is weakly justified and critical ablation studies are missing, while the expensive RL training phase lacks cost analysis.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The concept of 'reasoning heads' lacks sufficient justification compared to established 'retrieval heads' work; the paper does not provide multi-level analyses to support its existence, and some claims contain technical inaccuracies.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Missing critical analyses including end-to-end speedups, head stability under different prompts, ablation on training pipeline stages, and bidirectional design components that would validate the core claims.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because the reasoning heads concept is weakly justified and key ablation studies are missing, not because KV cache compression for reasoning models is unimportant.

paper_title: VeriWeb: Verifiable Long-Chain Web Benchmark for Agentic Information-Seeking

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The benchmark has correctness issues with overly strict ground truth annotations and lacks sufficient distinction from prior subtask evaluation methods like AgentCompany.

main_rejection_cause.reason: Ground truth annotations appear overly strict (e.g., 39M vs 38.64M without precision instructions, multiple valid answers treated as single ground truth), potentially leading to unreliable benchmark evaluation.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Subtask-level evaluation features are similar to AgentCompany's checkpoint-based evaluation, reducing novelty despite different task domains.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of benchmark annotation correctness concerns, not because long-chain web agent evaluation is unimportant.

paper_title: Activation with Intrinsic-Extrinsic Consensus

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The paper lacks theoretical justification for the consensus-based gating mechanism and the 1.4% improvement from the consensus mechanism does not justify the added complexity.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The consensus-based gating strategy lacks formal justification; the choice of hard intersection over other gating approaches has no information-theoretic or optimization-based rationale, and non-differentiable gating raises training stability concerns.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: No clear secondary rejection cause is supported by the reviews.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because the consensus gating mechanism lacks theoretical justification and the modest improvement does not justify the complexity, not because the problem of channel relevance is uninteresting.

paper_title: Contrastive Semi-Supervised Domain Adaptation with von Mises-Fisher for Class Imbalance Mitigation

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The paper suffers from insufficient novelty (vMF distribution has been explored in UDA), unconvincing methodology with unclear notations and explanations, and insufficient experimentation with only two benchmarks and no comparisons to recent 2024-2025 methods.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The application of von Mises-Fisher contrast has become common in domain adaptation research, and this work merely extends it to the semi-supervised setting. The novelty is limited to incremental modifications rather than introducing new mechanisms.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Only two benchmarks (Office-Home and DomainNet) with ResNet-34 are used, which is insufficient. No comparisons with recent 2024-2025 methods are provided, and the reported performance fails to surpass baseline methods.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of insufficient novelty and incomplete experimentation, not because the problem domain (semi-supervised domain adaptation) is unimportant.

paper_title: Expanding Computation Spaces of LLMs at Inference Time

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The paper presents an empirical study with inconsistent results across different models and token types, failing to provide actionable insights or meaningful contributions to the community.

main_rejection_cause.reason: Results are inconsistent across different model types and sizes, and patterns do not generalize well. The explanations for different models contradict each other (larger models benefit from filler tokens vs. smaller models effectively utilize additional tokens).

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: The study does not provide clear practical value. Direct insertion of filler tokens leads to inconsistent performance fluctuations without clear guidance, and the approach appears to add random manipulation rather than serving as a beneficial algorithm.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of inconsistent experimental results and lack of clear patterns, not because the research question about computational space expansion is inherently uninteresting.

paper_title: Flow-Matching Guided Deep Unfolding for Hyperspectral Image Reconstruction

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The paper's technical novelty is incremental—the core architecture closely follows LADE-DUN (ECCV 2024), and replacing latent diffusion with flow matching is a component-level modification rather than a conceptual breakthrough.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The framework heavily derives from LADE-DUN architecture including GAP unfolding scheme, Trident Transformer, and two-stage training pipeline. The simple replacement of latent diffusion prior with flow matching is deemed an incremental refinement rather than a fundamental innovation.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Main quantitative results are only reported on an optical-filter-based HSI system instead of the dominant CASSI benchmark. Qualitative CASSI results are insufficient, and comparison methods are tested under different standards.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of limited technical novelty and incremental contribution, not because flow matching integration with deep unfolding is theoretically unsound.

paper_title: UniVerse-1: Unified Audio-Video Generation via Stitching of Experts

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Despite some strengths in the Stitching of Experts paradigm and dataset contribution, the paper suffers from disappointing qualitative results, insufficient comparisons to prior work, and concerns about reproducibility of the data annotation pipeline.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The paper omits necessary comparisons to key prior works (JavisDiT, MM-LDM, AV-DiT), is only evaluated on the newly proposed Verse-Bench without established public benchmarks, and lacks FVD/FAD quality metrics.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: The online data annotation pipeline is described in the appendix rather than main paper with insufficient details (e.g., audio activity detection parameters, captioning prompts). The noise sampling strategy explanation was inadequate and raised concerns among reviewers.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of incomplete comparisons and reproducibility concerns, not because the Stitching of Experts paradigm is conceptually flawed.

paper_title: Uncertainty Quantification for Regression Using Proper Scoring Rules

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The paper largely repackages existing concepts (proper scoring rules, Bayes risk decompositions, Gaussian ensembles) without introducing fundamentally new theory. The empirical section is extensive but inconclusive, with promised practical recommendations missing or buried.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The paper largely restates known results (CRPS, log score, Bayes risk, total/excess risk) and rederives them under Gaussian assumptions. The theoretical contributions beyond repackaging existing ideas are unclear, with Tables 2-3 seen as summaries rather than new findings.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: The empirical evaluation shows many near-ties, saturated OOD benchmarks, and modest active learning gains with limited discriminative power. Practical recommendations promised in the abstract are missing or buried, making actionable guidance elusive.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of limited theoretical novelty and lack of practical takeaways, not because the proper scoring rule framework for regression is conceptually weak.

paper_title: Convergence Theory of Decentralized Diffusion Models via Pseudo-Non-Markov Analysis

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The necessity of the pseudo-non-Markovian framework was successfully challenged by a reviewer who provided a sketch showing existing methods (conditional distributions and chain rule for TV distance) could achieve similar results without the new machinery. The authors did not convincingly refute this, casting doubt on the core theoretical contribution. Additionally, critical assumptions were dismissed as 'typos', reducing confidence in rigor.

main_rejection_cause.reason: Reviewer H4tx challenged the necessity of the pseudo-non-Markov framework, providing a sketch using standard conditional distributions and chain rule for TV distance that could achieve similar results without the proposed new analysis machinery. The authors did not convincingly refute this. This undermines the paper's primary theoretical contribution.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Critical assumptions (such as uniform lower bound on classifier probabilities) were initially presented as necessary but later dismissed as 'typos', reducing confidence in the rigor of the manuscript.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because its core contribution—the pseudo-non-Markovian analysis framework—was challenged as potentially unnecessary given simpler existing methods, not because the problem of decentralized DPM convergence lacks importance.

paper_title: CoPatch: Zero-Shot Referring Image Segmentation by Leveraging Untapped Spatial Knowledge in CLIP

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The design choices (negation, clustering threshold, selection logic) are insufficiently justified and appear heuristic rather than principled. Ablation studies suggest the majority of improvement comes from the negation and clustering steps, which were previously explored in CLIP Surgery, raising questions about the true novelty and contribution of the proposed approach.

main_rejection_cause.reason: Design choices (negation trick, clustering threshold, selection logic) are heuristic rather than principled. The negation step, which appears to be the main performance contributor, was previously explored in CLIP Surgery. Without comparison to CLIP Surgery or justification for the heuristic choices, the true novelty contribution is unclear.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: The ablation study reveals that the proposed global-local formulation and context token design contribute marginally compared to negation and clustering. Architectural generalizability remains unsupported beyond ViT-based CLIP models; no CNN-based experiments were provided despite reviewer requests.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because the design choices are insufficiently justified and appear heuristic, not because the problem of zero-shot referring image segmentation lacks importance.

paper_title: Rao Differential Privacy

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: While conceptually interesting, the paper does not demonstrate clear operational or practical advantages over existing privacy frameworks. For standard mechanisms, results largely recover known guarantees under reparameterization, and the benefits of a distance-based definition remain insufficiently justified from an ML or deployment perspective.

main_rejection_cause.reason: Multiple reviewers noted that the proposed Rao DP largely recovers known guarantees under reparameterization for standard mechanisms (especially Gaussian DP). The existence of Gaussian DP, which exhibits similar composition behavior and characterization of the Gaussian mechanism, weakens the case for Rao DP as a distinct contribution.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: The operational utility of Rao DP remains unclear. Reviewers questioned what concrete problems Rao DP solves that existing frameworks cannot, and noted the lack of conversion theorems or clear practical applications beyond reparameterizing known mechanisms.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because it does not demonstrate clear operational or practical advantages over existing frameworks like Gaussian DP, not because the information geometry perspective on differential privacy lacks theoretical merit.

paper_title: Distributed PATE and CaPC on a DIET: Private Knowledge Transfer without Public Data or Private Inference

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The paper integrates existing techniques (PATE, programmatic data generation, data-free KD) rather than introducing a new algorithmic mechanism. Reviewers noted limited experimental scope (MNIST, CIFAR-10, TissueMNIST) and unconvincing validation for real-world sensitive domains like healthcare. Despite addressing some concerns during rebuttal, key questions about novelty and scale remained unresolved.
