secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Baseline results are inconsistent with existing literature (e.g., STIDGCN MAE on PEMS08 reported as 19.57 vs 13.45 in original paper). The ablation study is too simple and doesn't demonstrate the contribution of each component.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because it lacks novelty (merely combining existing spatiotemporal models), not because the problem or experimental setup is fundamentally flawed.

paper_title: Identifying Unperturbed Cellular Programs Enables Accurate Single-Cell Perturbation Prediction

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The paper was rejected due to both method concerns (theoretical identifiability guarantees rely on strong assumptions unlikely to hold in real biological systems) and experiment concerns (weak baselines, missing key comparisons, limited datasets)

main_rejection_cause.reason: The identifiability guarantees rely on strong, biologically questionable assumptions: linear SCM with Gaussian noise in latent space (biological networks are non-linear and data is count-based), diffeomorphism decoder (invertible mapping from low to high dimension is implausible), and perturbation richness requiring diverse single-gene perturbations to excite all causal pathways.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Missing comparisons to linear baselines, SAMS-VAE, GPerturb, and transformer/graph-based models. Only Norman2019 dataset used. No quantitative evaluation of inferred causal structure. Metrics (RMSE, R²) noted as problematic for high-dimensional gene expression. No ablation demonstrating CRL/DAG component contributions.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because the theoretical guarantees don't hold under realistic conditions (non-linear, non-Gaussian biological data), not because the core idea of disentangling variant/invariant subspaces lacks merit.

paper_title: CP4D: Compositional physics-aware 4D scene generation

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The paper was rejected due to both method concerns (limited technical novelty combining existing components, complex pipeline with many failure points) and experiment concerns (unconvincing results, weak comparisons)

main_rejection_cause.reason: The proposed framework consists primarily of existing components (VLM, physics simulators, SDS refinement, depth estimation) without sufficient technical novelty. Decoupling static background from dynamic foreground is not novel in 4D generation. The contribution amounts to system integration rather than algorithmic innovation.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Results are unconvincing: only 17 simple prompts, very short video clips, no significant camera motion. Comparisons to Sora/Wan are questionable given their actual capabilities. Vbench/Worldscore results don't match visual quality of demos. No robustness analysis across diverse scenarios.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because it lacks technical novelty (existing components combined without new mechanisms), not because the application domain of physically-grounded 4D scene generation is unimportant.

paper_title: Neural Mutual Information Estimation in Real Time via Pre-trained Hypernetworks

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The paper was rejected primarily due to experiment concerns (limited high-dimensional evaluation despite claiming general applicability) and secondary method concerns (novelty questions about DV-based MI estimation)

main_rejection_cause.reason: Limited high-dimensional evaluation despite the method claiming broad applicability. For high-dimensional data (512-dim), the method relies on slicing which is an approximation, and no empirical analysis of high-dimensional performance trends is provided. The synthetic pretraining data diversity is not quantified.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: DV-based representation learning for MI is not new (Neural Methods for Point-wise Dependency Estimation, NeurIPS 2020). The synthetic data pretraining approach is used in computer vision. The novelty may primarily lie in the model architecture rather than the overall framework.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of limited high-dimensional evaluation (only ~20D tested directly, slicing for higher dimensions), not because the core efficiency breakthrough (100x speedup via hypernetwork) is unimpressive.

paper_title: EDIF: Editing via Dynamic Interactive Tuning with Feedback

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Method has empirical rather than theoretical support for DiT block selection, and experiments show limited improvement with additional computational cost

main_rejection_cause.reason: The method relies on empirical observations for block-wise influence adjustment without sufficient theoretical support. The choice of which blocks to adjust is heuristic, and the additional computational overhead was not adequately justified. Even the single follow-up experiment using Qwen-Image Editing showed the method is not directly applicable to improve performance.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: No clear secondary rejection cause is supported by the reviews.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of method soundness concerns (empirical block choices without theoretical backing and limited performance gains), not because of experiment design.

paper_title: CLIP-TTA: Robust Test-Time Adaptation via Dual Regularization Beyond Optimal Transport

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Limited novelty as incremental addition to CLIP-OT without theoretical justification for how proposed losses address overconfidence/ECE reduction

main_rejection_cause.reason: The paper builds directly on CLIP-OT with only two additional loss functions (cosine similarity and information maximization), constituting a limited conceptual advance for ICLR. More critically, the paper lacks a theoretical explanation linking these losses to ECE reduction or overconfidence prevention.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Hyperparameter sensitivity analysis shows extreme variation across tasks, undermining the method's robustness claims. The optimal hyperparameters differ substantially between datasets, making the approach impractical for deployment.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of limited novelty and lack of theoretical justification for the proposed losses, not because of experimental completeness.

paper_title: Route Experts by Sequence, Not by Token

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Critical flaw in online inference mechanism causes the method to degenerate to standard token-level TopK during autoregressive generation, undermining the core contribution

main_rejection_cause.reason: The online SeqTopK mechanism for autoregressive inference is fundamentally flawed: lacking access to future tokens, it cannot perform true sequence-level optimization and effectively collapses to standard per-token TopK, as acknowledged by the appendix results showing similar performance to baseline TopK.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: The lack of full pre-training experiments (only fine-tuning validation) leaves the long-term stability of SeqTopK unproven, and the heuristic bounds to prevent degenerate allocations add complexity without theoretical grounding.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of a critical flaw in the online inference mechanism that causes it to degenerate to standard TopK, not because of lack of experimental coverage.

paper_title: ReportBench: Evaluating Deep Research Agents via Academic Survey Tasks

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Narrow quality definition and inability to evaluate higher-order scientific reasoning (insight, synthesis, critical analysis), making the benchmark vulnerable to gaming with superficial reports

main_rejection_cause.reason: The benchmark only evaluates factuality and citation correctness, not higher-order scientific reasoning (insight, synthesis, critical analysis, logical coherence). An agent could produce a report that scores highly on all metrics by simply restating obvious facts from retrieved papers, without qualifying as a survey paper.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Very low citation recall (3-4%) even for the strongest agents suggests the task may be miscalibrated or the metric does not align with how human researchers judge adequacy. The heavy reliance on automated LLM-based evaluation without sufficient human validation creates potential bias.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of incomplete evaluation that doesn't assess scientific insight and synthesis quality, not because of lack of methodological novelty.

paper_title: SinoMultiAffect: A Chinese Multi-Label and Fine-Grained Emotional Text Dataset with fMRI Data

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Dataset quality is compromised by low inter-annotator agreement (0.346 Jaccard index) and an ambiguous 35-label taxonomy, while the fMRI alignment work is fundamentally underpowered with only 3 participants

main_rejection_cause.reason: The fMRI component includes only 3 participants and 120 stimuli, which is statistically underpowered. The reported alignment metrics (Hit@1=0.17) are at or slightly above random, and the paper does not provide statistical tests or within/cross-subject validation, making the VAD-guided alignment findings exploratory at best.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: The low inter-annotator agreement (Jaccard index of 0.346) for the 35-label taxonomy indicates the categories are too ambiguous or subjective, calling into question the validity of the ground-truth labels and making it difficult to determine whether LLM errors reflect actual failures or correctly identified label ambiguity.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of experiment soundness issues (underpowered fMRI study and low annotation quality), not because of lack of dataset novelty.

paper_title: Posterior Restoration for Enhanced LLM Pruning

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The paper has weak novelty (two-stage pruning and posterior criteria follow prior work) and insufficient experiments (only 7B models, weak baselines, missing comparisons).

main_rejection_cause.reason: The two-stage pruning approach (prune mask then update mask) is common in pruning literature, and the three posterior criteria are simple extensions of prior work such as magnitude and Wanda. Reviewer JhPA notes the method mainly follows existing approaches with limited technical contribution.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Experiments are limited to 7B-parameter models only, lack comparison with methods like Wanda and SparseGPT, missing ablation on sensitivity to Delta-p, and baseline comparisons are weak. The PPL degradation under 50% sparsity is significantly worse than SparseGPT, suggesting non-competitive performance.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because the method's novelty is weak (common two-stage approach with simple criteria extensions), not because the problem addressed is unimportant or the writing unclear.

paper_title: MemoryBench: A Benchmark for Memory and Continual Learning in LLM Systems

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The paper's LLM-as-user simulator lacks sufficient validation to ensure results reflect realistic human-system interactions, and the approach does not sufficiently differentiate from existing frameworks.

main_rejection_cause.reason: Despite rebuttal claiming human validation showed indistinguishable simulated feedback from human feedback, the low inter-annotator agreement (Kappa) and limited scope of the human study failed to convincingly prove the simulator is a valid proxy for realistic human learning trajectories. Reviewer 6W2s notes no human study to calibrate fidelity of simulated user behavior.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: The area chair notes the approach does not sufficiently differentiate itself from existing LLM memory evolution frameworks to constitute a significant methodological advance. Reviewer dhtk mentions missing discussion of recent related benchmarks.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because the simulated user feedback lacks sufficient validation (low Kappa scores), not because the problem formulation or benchmark scope is inadequate.

paper_title: Crossing the Separation Point: Stabilizing Decision-Focused Learning with Variational Free-Energy

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The paper has theoretical clarity issues (unclear notation, missing assumptions in proofs), mixed empirical performance, and missing ablations. The method combines weighted loss and perturbation techniques that already exist with only dynamic weighting as novel contribution.

main_rejection_cause.reason: Multiple reviewers flagged unclear notation, missing assumptions and lemmas in proofs, confusion between true cost and predicted cost in driving instability, and an informal analysis. Reviewer 6Qez raised multiple technical questions about definitions and assumptions. Reviewer kQuS noted theoretical convergence analysis leveraging LP properties is lacking.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Missing ablations for the repulsive term (request from Reviewer n7Ry), single-seed evaluations without error bars, mixed performance across benchmarks with the method performing much worse than baselines on some tasks. Reviewer GBSN noted missing hyperparameter comparisons and convergence analysis.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of theoretical soundness issues (unclear definitions, missing assumptions) and incomplete experiments (missing ablations, single seed), not because the core problem of non-smoothness in DFL is unimportant.

paper_title: Continuous Autoregressive Language Models

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The paper lacks standard language modeling evaluations (QA, reasoning, long-context recall) and relies too heavily on Brier score correlations. Comparisons to existing multi-token and hierarchical methods are missing or underdeveloped. No rebuttal was provided.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The paper shows no actual language modeling performance (exact-match decoding), relies primarily on Brier score correlations which reviewers found insufficient. Missing comparisons to multi-token methods like Medusa, block transformers, MegaByte, and Large Concept Models. No in-context recall evaluations, no QA or reasoning benchmarks.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: The Brier score correlation to cross-entropy is not sufficient to justify good language modeling capability, especially on WikiText-103 alone. Reviewer FBcT notes the experiment section is 'delusive/insufficient'. Multiple ablations missing including on number of stochastic MLPs and compressor determinism.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because the experiments lack standard LM benchmarks and rely on Brier score correlations alone, not because the hierarchical modeling paradigm is conceptually flawed.

paper_title: AsyncTool: Evaluating the Asynchronous Function Calling Capability under Multi-Task Scenarios

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The benchmark's core design involves significant simplifications (fixed latency, deterministic trajectories, correctness-only metrics) that limit realism and generalizability. Despite addressing some concerns via rebuttal, key issues remain around simplified latency modeling and lack of efficiency metrics.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The benchmark relies on fixed one-round tool delay which does not reflect the stochastic and heterogeneous nature of real-world tool latencies. The simplified latency model limits realism and may only test context-switching rather than genuine temporal reasoning. Reviewers consistently flagged this as the most significant concern.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: The evaluation focuses largely on correctness without directly measuring idle-time utilization, scheduling optimality, or tool-call efficiency. Reviewer fuiW notes no penalty for excessive or unnecessary tool calls. Also missing explicit scheduling or efficiency metrics. Deterministic trajectories may turn evaluation into plan following rather than plan generation.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of the simplified experimental design (fixed latency, no efficiency metrics, deterministic trajectories), not because the underlying problem of evaluating asynchronous tool use is poorly motivated.

paper_title: R²AG: Learning to Reason, Retrieve, and Self-Evolve through a Multi-Branch Retrieval Tree

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Severe clarity issues regarding model definition, assumptions, and mathematical formulations; unfair baseline comparisons mixing different retrievers/generators

main_rejection_cause.reason: Multiple reviewers identify severe clarity issues including unclear model definition (retrieval steering model identity and training target), confusing assumptions (Assumption 2.2 is described as potentially self-contradictory), ambiguous mathematical formulations (Equations 2-4 lack explanation of how probabilities are computed), and vague self-evolution mechanism. These fundamental clarity problems prevent understanding of what the paper actually proposes.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Reviewer UiW2 points out that experiments mix different retrievers (BM25, NV-Embed, multilingual-E5) and generators, making it impossible to isolate whether improvements come from the proposed algorithm or stronger backbone models. Many baselines lack results or were cited from prior papers rather than re-evaluated in a consistent setup.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of severe clarity issues (unclear model definition, confusing assumptions, ambiguous math formulations) that prevent understanding of the proposed method, not because the underlying idea of reasoning-augmented retrieval trees lacks merit.

paper_title: Parallelizing Tree Search With Twice Sequential Monte Carlo

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Missing critical baselines (SPO, TRT-SMC) essential for evaluating whether TSMCTS advances the state of art; persistent presentation issues with notation inconsistencies

main_rejection_cause.reason: Reviewer oJ94 repeatedly emphasizes that the paper compares against an unnamed 'SMC baseline' rather than established prior SMC-based planners (SPO, TRT-SMC). Without these critical baselines, there is no evidence that TSMCTS advances the state of the art. Reviewer WwXY also notes lack of comparison with robust PUCT variants and MuZero-style planners. The absence of SPO comparison is described as a strict requirement for acceptance.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: No clear secondary rejection cause is supported by the reviews.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of missing essential baselines (SPO, TRT-SMC) needed to demonstrate state-of-the-art advancement, not because the idea of integrating MCTS backpropagation with SMC is uninteresting.

paper_title: SmartDS-Solver: Agentic AI for Vertical Domain Problem Solving in Data Science

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Novelty concerns - overall architecture combines known techniques (SFT, GRPO, data augmentation, hierarchical agents) with only SARTE as novel component; persistent presentation quality issues

main_rejection_cause.reason: Multiple reviewers (J3ei, 2DKn, area chair) conclude that the overall architecture combines known existing techniques (SFT, GRPO, data augmentation, hierarchical agents) with only the SARTE mechanism as a meaningful novel contribution. Reviewer 2DKn explicitly states the method is 'incremental.' The area chair summarizes that reviewers are unconvinced the full system represents a fundamentally new methodological advance rather than a well-engineered integration.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: No clear secondary rejection cause is supported by the reviews.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because the contribution is viewed as an incremental combination of existing techniques (SFT, GRPO, hierarchical agents) rather than a fundamentally new methodological advance, not because the empirical results (81.8% win rate) are weak.

paper_title: Query-Kontext: An Unified Multimodal Model for Image Generation and Editing

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Data fairness concerns due to heavy reliance on in-house Chinese dataset (170M+) versus only 30M English open-source; limited novelty beyond sRoPE design; insufficient ablation of key components

main_rejection_cause.reason: Reviewers Uvkf and Asae raise concerns that the large proportion of in-house Chinese image-text pairs (170M+) compared to only 30M English open-source data raises serious fairness issues in comparative evaluation. Reviewer Asae states this 'increases concern about the fairness in comparative evaluation and the soundness of empirical validity.' The in-house dataset is not public, limiting reproducibility.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: The definition of 'kontext' tokens is described as vague and hard to follow by reviewer Asae. Reviewer Nkxi remains confused about why text embedding is concatenated before feeding into the connector after rebuttal. Reviewer Uvkf notes the paper does not fully explain why the decoupling of reasoning and synthesis works.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of data fairness concerns (heavy reliance on in-house Chinese dataset) and reproducibility limitations, not because the decoupling of reasoning and rendering is inherently uninteresting.

paper_title: IL3D: A Large-Scale Indoor Layout Dataset for LLM-Driven 3D Scene Generation

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Fundamental lack of novelty - dataset construction follows exactly the same pipeline as OptiScene, merely scaled up; work only releases a dataset with minimal methodological contribution

main_rejection_cause.reason: Reviewer EDZ2 explicitly states 'The dataset construction follows exactly the same fundamental pipeline as OptiScene, which is based on the Holodeck and merely scales it up. There is no substantive difference.' Reviewer N3X notes the contribution 'beyond data aggregation and automatic labeling is limited.' Reviewer EDZ2 summarizes 'The work only releases a dataset; the downstream methods and prompts are almost identical to prior art, with no innovation.'

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: No clear secondary rejection cause is supported by the reviews.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because it lacks novelty (dataset construction follows prior work exactly, merely scaled up) and provides no downstream innovation, not because the need for a large-scale 3D indoor scene dataset is unimportant.

paper_title: 3D-ATRES: Ambiguity-Tolerant Learning for 3D Referring Expression Segmentation

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The paper was rejected primarily due to limited novelty (incremental over 3D-LLaVA using known techniques) and insufficient statistical evidence for claimed improvements, with reviewers noting the method is a complex multi-stage pipeline without clear statistical significance.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The paper's technical novelty is incremental. TR2SS resembles prior scene-graph parsing work (ViL3DRel, X-RefSeg3D), NASA extends standard geometry-aware contrastive alignment, and AAP parallels prior GMM-based noise-robust segmentation. No rebuttal was provided to address these concerns.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Performance gains are within 1-3 percentage points without standard deviations or multi-run averages, making statistical significance uncertain. Table 1 mixes numbers from prior papers and local re-runs without clarifying input resolution, instance proposals, and instruction budget consistency.

paper_title: Linearly Independent Feature Extraction

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The paper was rejected due to limited empirical validation with very few experiments, missing comprehensive baselines (including recent deep invariant/causal OOD frameworks and two-stage methods like DFR), and concerns about the relevance of theory to deep networks.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The evaluation is limited to linear models with very few experiments. Missing comparisons with recent deep OOD frameworks (LFF, JTT, Logit Correction, DeNetDM), and two-stage baselines (DFR, Domain-Adjusted ERM). No ablation studies or sensitivity analyses provided.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: The identifiability assumption (state of environment is recoverable) may not hold under fundamental limitations. Theory doesn't clearly support claims for deep networks; evaluation limited to linear settings makes relevance to practical deep learning unclear.

paper_title: Scale-aware Message Passing for Graph Node Classification

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The paper was rejected primarily due to concerns about novelty and conceptual framing, with substantial overlap with prior multi-hop/multi-scale GNN literature not adequately acknowledged, and concerns about the theoretical justification.

main_rejection_cause.reason: Multi-hop aggregation has been around for years (MixHop 2019, k-hop GNN 2020, LanczosNet, etc.). The paper doesn't properly contextualize with prior work on undirected multi-hop GNNs, directed GNNs, graph transformers, or graph coarsening methods.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: No clear secondary rejection cause is supported by the reviews.

paper_title: UPrompt: Bidirectional Multi-granularity Learning for Vision-Language Models

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The paper was rejected due to limited novelty compared to recent multi-level hierarchical prompt works (TAP, HiCroPL), limited backbone comparisons (only CLIP ViT-B/16), and concerns about writing clarity and reproducibility.

main_rejection_cause.reason: Limited novelty - TAP and HiCroPL already explore multi-level or hierarchical prompts. UPrompt mainly formalizes existing ideas within a U-shaped structure rather than introducing fundamentally new mechanisms.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: No comparisons with stronger or newer VLM backbones such as SigLIP/SigLIP-2, EVA-CLIP, or E5-V. Results only on CLIP ViT-B/16, limiting the claim of generality.

paper_title: Multi‑view Adaptive Partitioning with Global Association for Graph Anomaly Detection

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The paper was rejected due to limited novelty (similar to GAAP, GADAM, UniGAD) and concerns about problem positioning - the challenges addressed exist in all supervised GNNs, not specific to graph anomaly detection.

main_rejection_cause.reason: Limited novelty - Multi-Pattern Global Association is a simple combination of local and global node similarity, similar to GAAP, GADAM, and UniGAD. The motivation (tabular attributes, long-range dependencies) and approach are not sufficiently differentiated from prior work.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: The work is not properly positioned - the challenges discussed (tabular attributes, long-range dependencies) exist in almost all supervised GNNs, raising questions about what unique challenges in graph anomaly detection are being targeted.

paper_title: Graph Unlearning via Reconstruction --- A Range-Null Space Decomposition Approach

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The justification for key design choices remains informal, and case-specific formulations undermine the generality of the framework.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The justification for key design choices (e.g., why (k-1)-th layer reconstruction is optimal) remains informal. Additionally, the method requires case-specific formulations for different scenarios (low ratios, high ratios, edge unlearning), which weakens the perceived generality of the framework.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: No clear secondary rejection cause is supported by the reviews.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of informal justification of key design choices and lack of generality due to case-specific formulations, not because of insufficient experiments.

paper_title: CASPO: Confidence-aware Step-wise Preference Optimization for Reliable Reasoning in Large Language Models

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The approach derives much of its success from the strength of the teacher/evaluator model rather than a systematic methodological contribution.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The method relies heavily on a strong teacher/evaluator model (Qwen-Math) for step correctness, and appears engineering-driven with limited methodological novelty. The approach does not sufficiently articulate a systematic algorithmic contribution beyond leveraging the teacher model's strength.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: The effectiveness of the method is questionable given that the trained model fails to surpass the teacher/evaluator model used for annotation, raising concerns about scalability and practical utility.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of limited methodological novelty and heavy reliance on a strong teacher model, not because of poor experimental design.

paper_title: RAAG: RATIO AWARE ADAPTIVE GUIDANCE

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The theoretical analysis is fundamentally flawed and not convincing, with inconsistencies in core definitions and imprecise notation.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The theoretical analysis is fundamentally flawed. The quantity analyzed (difference between trajectories) is not well-motivated, Proposition 3.1 is unclear in relevance, and the theory does not lead to useful algorithms—the practical approach requires heuristics that work for some models but degrade quality for others.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: The method does not work for diffusion models (e.g., SD-v2) without explanation, and widely used metrics like FID are not reported, making objective performance assessment difficult.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of fundamentally flawed theoretical analysis and poor alignment between theory and practice, not because the problem identification was incorrect.

paper_title: Constrained Stochastic Multi-Objective Optimization

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Limited technical novelty; the core contributions represent incremental extensions of existing stochastic constrained optimization techniques to the multi-objective setting.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The methods largely extend existing stochastic constrained optimization techniques to the multi-objective setting using standard tools like scalarization, moving average estimators, and quadratic surrogate functions. The technical core remains incremental relative to prior work.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Evaluation is restricted to low-dimensional synthetic problems with only two objectives and lacks comparisons to modern stochastic multi-objective optimization baselines, limiting claims of generality and practical impact.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of limited technical novelty and incremental contribution, not because of theoretical flaws or poor presentation.

paper_title: QuadSentinel: Sequent Safety for Machine-Checkable Control in Multi-agent Systems

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Presentation and clarity issues, reliability/robustness concerns, and missing overhead/latency analysis for real deployments.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The presentation is complex with frequent mixing of language descriptions and mathematical notation, making the core methodology difficult to follow. Key design details are insufficiently explained, and the pipeline is described as overly formal given the conceptual simplicity of the approach.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: The framework relies heavily on correctness of offline policy-to-rule translation but provides limited quantitative evaluation of translation fidelity. Additionally, the claim of low-overhead is not validated empirically with actual latency, throughput, or cost measurements for real deployments.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of poor presentation and clarity issues, not because the underlying problem or approach lacks significance.

paper_title: Inference-Time Diffusion Model Alignment via Random Ordinary Equations

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The main claim about parameter efficiency being important is not supported by evidence, as eps-action methods often achieve comparable or better performance with similar computational cost

main_rejection_cause.reason: The central claim about parameter efficiency being critical is not supported by evidence. Table 5 shows eps-action methods achieve comparable or better reward with comparable or lower time cost. Authors promised additional scaling experiments on PixArt-Alpha-XL 512/1024 but did not provide them.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Missing critical comparisons including: ODE-based value estimation baselines (Demons, DNO), best-of-n sampling under pure ODE or SDE trajectories, and quantified computational cost analysis across resolutions and model sizes.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because the central parameter efficiency claim is not supported by empirical evidence (eps-action methods perform equally or better), not because the RODE formulation itself is flawed.

paper_title: GeoSplat: A Deep Dive into Geometry-Constrained Gaussian Splatting

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Severely limited experimental validation confined to only two indoor datasets, missing critical benchmarks like NeRF Blender and Mip-NeRF 360 outdoor scenes

main_rejection_cause.reason: All experiments limited to Replica and ICL indoor datasets. Critical omissions include: object-level NeRF Blender datasets (lego, mic), unbounded outdoor 360 scenes (Mip-NeRF 360, Tanks & Temples), and discussion of how the surface manifold assumption handles non-surface elements like sky or distant backgrounds.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Section 3.2 on geometric estimation presents theorems and complex equations (Eq. 12, Thm 3.2) without intuitive explanation or high-level overview, making it impossible to assess technical contribution from the main paper.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because the experimental validation is severely limited to only two indoor datasets, not because the curvature-guided geometric prior idea itself lacks merit.

paper_title: Purifying Task Vectors in Knowledge-Aware Subspace for Model Merging

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Reliance on task-domain data limits applicability in data-free merging scenarios, and incompatibility with several recent SVD-based static merging methods undermines the plug-and-play claim

main_rejection_cause.reason: The method requires accessing task-domain data to construct covariance matrices, limiting appeal in data-free merging scenarios. This requirement is not justified by the modest performance gains observed, particularly for large-scale generative models. Additionally, PAVE is incompatible with several recent SVD-based static merging methods, significantly limiting applicability.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: No clear secondary rejection cause is supported by the reviews. While limited theoretical grounding and performance variability across methods were noted, they are secondary to the core applicability limitations.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because its data dependency limits practical use in data-free scenarios and compatibility issues narrow its applicability, not because the purification approach lacks technical merit.

paper_title: Fire on Motion: Optimizing Video Pass-bands for Efficient Spiking Action Recognition

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Serious theoretical concerns about the frequency-domain derivation correctness, including flawed band-pass property claims and mischaracterized LIF neuron response

main_rejection_cause.reason: Reviewer 6T5D identified multiple theoretical flaws: (1) omega1 < omega2 not ensured and Eqs 3-5 disconnected from Eq 2, making band-pass property ungrounded; (2) Eq 9 claims |HLIF(e^j0)|^2 = 1 but actual LIF response is 1/sqrt(1+(omega*tau)^2); (3) nonlinear LIF processes not discussed; (4) 'uncorrelated frequency bins' assumption in Eq 24 is statistically unfounded.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Limited ablation studies - missing ablation on loss components (L_int or L_grad alone), and hyperparameter settings (A=0.1, alpha=1e-2) not validated across datasets.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of serious theoretical flaws in the frequency-domain derivation that undermine the core band-pass justification, not because the empirical performance gains are insufficient.

paper_title: Mind the gap: A method for evaluating and comparing regional knowledge in LLMs

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Lack of technical novelty combining existing evaluation techniques, and Wikidata coverage bias for underrepresented regions not empirically addressed

main_rejection_cause.reason: The paper combines existing evaluation techniques (token overlap, embedding similarity, LLM-as-judge, multiple-choice accuracy) without significant methodological innovation. Multiple reviewers (1sck, PyBt) note this lack of technical novelty as a major limitation.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Wikidata coverage bias for underrepresented regions like Latin America not empirically analyzed or mitigated. Selected Wikidata properties (P19, P625) limit answer diversity mostly to locations. Evaluation reliability not validated against human judgments.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because it lacks technical novelty (combining existing methods without algorithmic contribution), not because the cultural knowledge evaluation problem is unimportant.

paper_title: CoT-MT$^3$ : CoT-Guided Meta Test-Time Training for Multimodal Reasoning

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Limited novelty in the core approach (retrieval-specific CoT has been explored in existing ICL literature) and concerns about whether MT3 is truly a meta-learning approach vs. a prompt diversification strategy.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The retrieval-specific Chain-of-Thought idea for improving retrieval quality has been explored in existing ICL literature (e.g., iterative demonstration selection). Additionally, MT3 is described as a 'meta-learning paradigm' but reviewers found it lacks the standard definition of meta-learning (no inner/outer loop, no bi-level optimization), making it more of a prompt diversification strategy.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: The paper only validates on mathematical multimodal reasoning datasets, yet claims to be a unified multimodal approach. The retrieval-specific CoT prompt is explicitly math-oriented, raising concerns about generalization to other domains like VQA or general multimodal reasoning.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of limited novelty in the core retrieval-specific CoT approach and concerns about the meta-learning claims, not because the experimental setup was fundamentally flawed.

paper_title: Improving Few-Shot Design Optimization By Exploiting Auxiliary Information

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Insufficient evaluation scope (only one custom benchmark) and lack of comparisons to state-of-the-art black-box optimization methods, particularly methods that could be adapted to leverage the auxiliary information.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The method is evaluated only on a single custom gripper benchmark, making it difficult to assess general applicability across domains like molecular design or materials design. Additionally, the paper lacks direct comparisons to state-of-the-art black-box optimization methods from literature.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: The core idea of leveraging context information is not sufficiently novel as multi-modal foundation models have already proven that integrating multi-modal information is beneficial. The approach treats auxiliary information h(x) as an 'extra modality', which has been explored in prior work.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of insufficient evaluation scope (single benchmark, lacking SOTA BO baselines), not because the underlying method concept was fundamentally flawed.

paper_title: S$^2$-ETC: Semantic-Structure Aware Encrypted Traffic Classification via Hyper-Bipartite Graph

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Experimental concerns including problematic ablation results (semantic branch removal yields better performance on USTC-TFC2016), inconsistent implementation details, and outdated datasets limiting real-world applicability.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The ablation study raises doubts about the semantic branch's effectiveness: removing it yields better performance on USTC-TFC2016 than the full model. Additionally, implementation details are inconsistent with settings disclosed in the code, and the static alpha value contradicts the claimed 'adaptive learning' capability.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: The datasets used are outdated (2016/2017) and do not represent realistic characteristics of modern encrypted traffic. Strong pre-training baselines like YaTC are missing from comparisons, and the paper lacks discussion of common over-squashing solutions.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of experimental weaknesses (problematic ablation results and outdated datasets), not because of fundamental flaws in the HBG architecture design.

paper_title: MegaScience: Pushing the Frontiers of Open Post-Training Datasets for Science Reasoning

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Unresolved ethical/legal flaw regarding data sourcing - mass scraping of 12,000+ copyrighted textbooks without clear permission presents fundamental legal and ethical violation that cannot be fixed by after-the-fact filtering.

main_rejection_cause.reason: Copyright and data sourcing issues with mass scraping of 12,000+ university-level textbooks without clear permission presents a fundamental ethical and legal violation. LLM-based filtering is legally insufficient and technically unreliable for determining copyright status. Accepting such work would set a problematic precedent regarding data sourcing standards.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: No clear secondary rejection cause is supported by the reviews.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of unresolved copyright and data sourcing issues (mass scraping of copyrighted textbooks), not because of methodological or experimental weaknesses.

paper_title: Benchmarking World-Model Learning

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Limited generalizability beyond 2D grid-world settings and concerns about benchmark reliability due to sensitivity to prompt design affecting relative model rankings.

main_rejection_cause.reason: While 2D grid worlds enable controlled experimentation and affordable human evaluation, the benchmark remains largely limited to LLMs operating in simple environments. Framing the contribution as a general 'world model' benchmark appears somewhat overstated given the limited scope.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Sensitivity to prompt design is concerning: while alternative prompts preserve the overall gap between LLM and human performance, they affect relative rankings among LLMs, raising concerns about the benchmark's reliability for measuring improvements or fine-grained model differences.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of limited generalizability (2D grid-worlds only) and prompt sensitivity concerns, not because the WorldTest evaluation protocol concept was fundamentally flawed.

paper_title: HyperHELM: Hyperbolic Hierarchy Encoding for mRNA Language Modeling

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Experiment issues dominated the rejection: incomplete baselines, missing variance estimates, limited reproducibility, and the method primarily extends existing hyperbolic methods without sufficient methodological novelty.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The evaluation lacked critical mRNA-specific baselines (mRNA-FM, AIDO.RNA-CDS, Orthrus, Evo2) and failed to report variance estimates or confidence intervals for small downstream datasets, undermining the reliability of performance claims.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: While applying hyperbolic geometry to mRNA modeling is novel as an application, the paper primarily extends the HELM framework with limited methodological innovation beyond adapting existing hyperbolic learning techniques.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of experiment incompleteness (missing baselines, no variance reporting, reproducibility issues), not because the core idea of hyperbolic mRNA modeling lacks significance.

paper_title: Automated Algorithm Design with LLMs: A Benchmark-Assisted Approach to Black-Box Optimization

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Method novelty issues: significant overlap with prior LLM-driven evolutionary methods (EoH, ReEvo), and the approach is primarily a rebranding of in-context learning with benchmark-guided prompts rather than genuine algorithmic innovation.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The BAG framework is essentially a minor adjustment to existing evolutionary paradigms, replacing internal guidance sources with external benchmark algorithms, which represents incremental rather than fundamental innovation.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Evaluation is confined to PBO/BBOB benchmark suites covering only unconstrained numerical optimization, with no evidence of generalization to combinatorial or constrained optimization domains.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because its novelty is limited (BAG primarily reuses benchmark algorithms as prompts, similar to EoH/ReEvo), not because the AttnLRP analysis of prompt components lacks value.

paper_title: MIDAS: Mosaic Input-Specific Differentiable Architecture Search

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Method soundness issues: the semantic meaning of using inner products between queries and keys as architecture weights is unclear and lacks principled justification, combined with marginal empirical improvements.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The defined queries (from raw features) and keys (from operated features) do not constitute true self-attention, and the semantic meaning of their inner product as an architecture weight is unclear and lacks principled justification.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: No clear secondary rejection cause is supported by the reviews.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of method soundness concerns (unclear justification for inner product as architecture weight), not because the experimental evaluation was insufficient.

paper_title: Towards High-Order Mean Flow Generative Models: Feasibility, Expressivity, and Provably Efficient Criteria

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Experiment absence: the paper contains no empirical validation whatsoever, which is critical for an applied ML venue, despite solid theoretical contributions.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The paper provides no empirical validation whatsoever—no toy experiments, simulations, or demonstrations of practical behavior—which leaves the theoretical Second-Order MeanFlow as an unvalidated construction with unknown real-world applicability.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: The technical contribution builds substantially on prior circuit complexity work for Transformers, with the MeanFlow extension being relatively straightforward.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of the complete absence of experiments (no empirical validation), not because the theoretical results on circuit complexity and Second-Order MeanFlow lack rigor.

paper_title: From Evidence to Trajectory: Abductive Reasoning Path Synthesis for Training Retrieval-Augmented Generation Agents

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Mixed concerns: conceptual rigor of 'abductive reasoning' framing remains insufficient despite empirical effectiveness, and fairness issues with baseline comparisons (different backbones) persist after rebuttal.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The 'abductive reasoning' framing is overstated; the implementation is essentially an LLM-driven trajectory reconstruction without formal optimality guarantees or principled justification for the 0.9 cosine similarity threshold.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Baseline comparisons involve different LLM backbones (weaker models for some baselines, stronger for others), raising fairness concerns despite the rebuttal's clarifications.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of conceptual soundness concerns (overstated abductive reasoning framing), not because the empirical results on multi-hop QA were insufficient.

paper_title: Motion-Aware Surface Smoothing for Monocular Avatar Representations

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Limited novelty with only L_smooth as a solid contribution while other gains come from Sapiens baseline; performance drop in ActorHQ novel pose highlights limitations

main_rejection_cause.reason: Only the L_smooth term represents a solid novel contribution; other claimed improvements primarily come from Sapiens-based normal priors, making the incremental novelty insufficient for ICLR standards

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Missing mesh-level evaluation metrics (Chamfer Distance, P2S), missing important baselines (iHuman, HUGS, ExGA), and performance drop on ActorHQ novel pose not adequately explained

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of limited novelty with only incremental contributions beyond existing techniques, not because the method is poorly executed or the problem is unimportant.

paper_title: Meaningless Tokens, Meaningful Gains: How Activation Shifts Enhance LLM Reasoning

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Insufficient experimental validity with unreliable baseline comparisons and marginal gains; method novelty limited by prior work on similar effects

main_rejection_cause.reason: Baseline results are notably lower than original paper reports, making reported gains unreliable; temperature and pass@K not properly controlled; sensitivity analysis reveals gains are fragile and highly sensitive to hyperparameter choices

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: The 'meaningless-token effect' has been explored by prior work (Pause Tokens and related methods), limiting novelty; layer-1 only analysis is incomplete for explaining effects in deep networks

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of unreliable experimental results and insufficient baseline comparisons, not because the underlying observation is uninteresting.

paper_title: HNDiff: Haze-Noise Diffusion for Image Dehazing

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Lack of clarity with unclear hierarchical structure between components; physical model consistency in latent space questionable; marginal gains

main_rejection_cause.reason: Figure 2 is difficult to understand and does not clearly illustrate the two-stage training process; 'ground truth prior' meaning is unclear; no clear hierarchical structure between HNDiff, HANS, and Latent HNDiff components

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Missing real-world scenario experiments on RTTS dataset initially; insufficient comparison with ASM-based methods; haze estimator architecture and loss function not specified

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of unclear presentation and lack of clear motivation between components, not because the physical integration approach is fundamentally unsound.

paper_title: Provably Learning Task-Relevant World Representation

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Paper is confusing with 'identifiability' used in different senses; Section 4 novelty questionable; downstream utility unconvincing

main_rejection_cause.reason: The term 'identifiability' is used with different meanings in Section 3 (temporal task structure) and Section 4 (latent variables), making the paper confusing and difficult to follow; reviewers explicitly maintained confusion after rebuttal

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Gap between theory (CI oracle) and practice (approximations using InfoNCE variational bounds) is not adequately bridged; downstream utility is unconvincing with modest improvements and missing confidence intervals

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of unclear writing and conceptual confusion about what 'identifiability' means in different sections, not because the theoretical results are technically incorrect.

paper_title: Cross-View Open-Vocabulary Object Detection in Aerial Imagery

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Limited methodological novelty as straightforward combination of existing contrastive learning techniques; significant reproducibility concerns and presentation issues

main_rejection_cause.reason: The proposed approach combines established contrastive learning techniques (InfoNCE, CLIP-style objectives) without introducing fundamentally new insights; lacks theoretical analysis or principled explanation of how the losses fundamentally differ from existing multi-view or domain adaptation approaches

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Important details underspecified (temperatures, thresholds, handling of VisDrone videos); inconsistent experimental settings across tables (Tables 1, 4, 5, 6); formatting issues including citation errors and missing evaluation units; quality control for ChatGPT-generated vocabulary expansion superficial

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of limited methodological novelty and presentation issues, not because the problem formulation is unimportant or the experiments are completely inadequate.

paper_title: FaceMoE: Mixture of Experts for Low-Resolution Face Recognition

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The MoE architecture's effectiveness is questionable as removing individual experts only leads to marginal performance drops, and there is a fundamental tension between load balancing and semantic specialization that the authors haven't resolved. Additionally, computational overhead limits practical applicability in real-time surveillance settings.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The MoE effectiveness is questionable - removing individual experts only leads to marginal performance drops (0.11% on BRIAR). There is a fundamental tension between load balancing (forcing equal expert usage) and semantic specialization (experts focusing on rare features like specific landmarks) that the authors haven't resolved.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Memory and computational overhead for LR-FR deployed in real-time surveillance settings significantly limits practical applicability. The efficiency claims were oversold.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of fundamental issues with MoE effectiveness and the tension between load balancing and specialization, not because the experimental benchmarks or evaluation protocols were inadequate.

paper_title: Optimal Stopping for Sequential Bayesian Experimental Design

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The empirical evaluation is weak with experiments that are too simple and too few, lacking comparisons with highly relevant methods like Knowledge Gradient policies and Bayesian optimization literature. Additionally, the hand-designed stopping schedule and hyperparameters require more ablation studies.

main_rejection_cause.reason: Limited evaluation - only simpler posterior design and constant cost cases shown. The paper neglects highly relevant related work (Knowledge Gradient policies, BO literature, stochastic processes) and lacks comparative baselines. Only one run sample with no confidence intervals provided.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Hand-designed stopping schedule and hyperparameters lack sufficient ablation studies. Computational complexity and wall-clock efficiency not adequately discussed. The paper presents training results rather than test results.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of weak empirical evaluation with few experiments and insufficient comparisons, not because the theoretical formulation or algorithm design was fundamentally flawed.

paper_title: MoReFlow: Motion Retargeting Learning through Unsupervised Flow Matching

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Limited experimental evaluation with only two baseline methods compared, insufficient qualitative evidence, and concerns about scalability and generalization to unseen characters. The paper also lacks clarity on the conditioning mechanism and separate tokenizers design.

main_rejection_cause.reason: Only two baseline methods compared despite many relevant cross-embodiment retargeting approaches in related work. Results aggregated across embodiments preventing detailed analysis (humanoid vs. non-humanoid). Insufficient qualitative evidence for key claims.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: The conditioning feature vector is insufficiently described and the rationale behind separate tokenizers vs. shared tokenizers is unclear. The multi-sample coupling strategy for unpaired learning lacks clear explanation of how it facilitates generalization.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of limited experimental evaluation with few baselines and insufficient evidence, not because the core idea of using flow matching in tokenized motion space was fundamentally unsound.

paper_title: Multimodal Generative Composition Recommendation

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The architectural novelty is modest with most technical contribution coming from data curation and existing model integration. Baseline comparisons are outdated, and the core challenge of scene harmony (shadow consistency, reflection rendering, perspective alignment) relies entirely on an off-the-shelf tool with no additional innovations.

main_rejection_cause.reason: Architectural novelty is modest - separate projectors, depth tokenization, and instruction format are incremental contributions. Most technical lift comes from data curation and existing model integration. The core scene harmony challenge relies entirely on ObjectStitch with no additional innovations.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Baseline comparisons are outdated (only 2023 or earlier methods). Missing comparisons with recent SOTA like Qwen2.5-VL, InternVL3.0, and Gemini 2.5 Pro. No ablation on depth input contribution.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of limited architectural novelty and outdated baseline comparisons, not because the problem decomposition or data pipeline design was inadequate.

paper_title: Cocktail-Party at the MUSEUM: Referring Audio-Visual Segmentation requires Augmentation

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Technical novelty is not strong - the augmentation approach does not clearly distinguish from prior audio-visual synthesis methods or traditional audio augmentation techniques. The method is highly specialized for musical audio with limited demonstrated applicability to the broader Ref-AVS scope including non-musical cocktail-party scenarios.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The augmentation approach does not clearly distinguish from prior audio-visual synthesis methods or traditional audio augmentation techniques (RIR, SNR noise, codecs, filtering). The MISA framework largely builds upon existing training strategies without introducing substantial new insights.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: The method is highly specialized for musical audio with limited demonstrated applicability to non-musical, sparse, or speech-dominated cocktail-party scenarios. The pipeline's design and controllability are optimized for music without strong evidence of generalization.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of limited technical novelty and narrow specialization to musical audio, not because the problem motivation or benchmark design was flawed.

paper_title: Transfer between Modalities with MetaQueries

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Limited novelty and missing experiments to justify the approach

main_rejection_cause.reason: The method's core component MetaQueries is essentially similar to learnable prompts/queries in prior adapters such as Q-Former, and the overall approach overlaps with DreamLLM and SEED-X. The key question of whether replacing a learnable MLLM with a frozen MLLM constitutes sufficient novelty remains unresolved.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Missing key ablation experiments, particularly using MLLM output tokens as direct input for the connector, and missing interleaved image-text generation tasks that would more clearly demonstrate the advantages of MetaQueries.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of limited novelty compared to prior works like DreamLLM and SEED-X, not because the experiments were unsound.

paper_title: SPECS: Faster Test-Time Scaling through Speculative Drafts and Dynamic Switching

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Limited novelty relative to RSD/GSI and theory-practice gap with idealized assumptions

main_rejection_cause.reason: The main novelty (starting with target model and dynamic switching) overlaps significantly with RSD (draft+reward speculative decoding) and GSI (tilted rewards/scoring). The contribution is relatively limited compared to existing works.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: No clear secondary rejection cause is supported by the reviews.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of limited novelty relative to closely related methods like RSD and GSI, not because of experiment issues.

paper_title: Towards Scalable Web Browsing via Tool-Augmented Programmatic Agent Pair

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Limited novelty as planner-executor and code primitives have been extensively explored, and weak experimental comparisons

main_rejection_cause.reason: The planner-executor architecture has been extensively explored in multi-agent systems literature, and code-based primitives have been previously explored. The contribution is mainly putting existing ideas together rather than novel algorithmic design.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Missing comparison to classical multi-agent systems, ablation showing primitives alone yield similar performance to baseline (11.0% vs 8.9%), and limited generalization evidence beyond search tasks.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of limited novelty (planner-executor is standard multi-agent design), not because the significance of the problem was questioned.

paper_title: Abductive Reasoning over Temporal Knowledge Graphs via Logical Hypothesis Generation

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Substantial similarity to existing work and weak baselines

main_rejection_cause.reason: The core framework is nearly identical to existing work (Reference [1] on static KG abductive reasoning), with only minor modifications: temporal hypothesis generator and PPO replacing GRPO. The method lacks sufficient originality.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Only using outdated GPT-2 as baseline, missing important temporal reasoning baselines (TeMP, xERTE, TiRGN), and missing static KG methods for comparison.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of significant similarity to existing work and lack of originality in the method, not because the problem significance was questioned.

paper_title: All-Task Convergence and Backward Transfer in Federated Domain-Incremental Learning with Partial Participation

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Experimental scope too narrow relative to theoretical claims about all-task convergence

main_rejection_cause.reason: All experiments are restricted to small-scale vision datasets with ResNet-18, with no multimodal, NLP, or large-scale federated settings tested. The 'all-task convergence' claim is exaggerated relative to the empirical evidence.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: The server-side proximal term is essentially a FedProx/EWC variant with new theoretical framing, making the algorithmic contribution modest.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of narrow experimental scope (only ResNet-18 on vision) that doesn't support the broad theoretical claims, not because the theoretical contribution itself was questioned.

paper_title: Training Dynamics Explain Safe Early Exits in Diffusion Language Models

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The paper has severe clarity and soundness issues: reviewers found it largely illegible, with undefined notation, unexplained definitions, and theoretical assumptions that don't match empirical observations.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The theoretical results require a contraction assumption (α < 1) for global stability, but empirical estimates show α̂ > 1 (amplifying), fundamentally undermining the theoretical guarantee. Reviewers could not understand or verify Lemma 3.1, Theorem 3.2, Theorem 3.3.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: The paper is described as largely illegible by multiple reviewers - undefined notation, unexplained definitions (like f_s^{(t)}, m_t, I_t), and algorithm relegated to appendix. Core quantity P in equation 6 was not explained.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because the theoretical framework is unsound and incomprehensible, not because the core idea of using training dynamics for early-exit guarantees lacks merit.

paper_title: Robust Learning of Diffusion Models with Extremely Noisy Conditions

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The paper's RDC mechanism lacks proper mathematical grounding - the SDE derivation is unconvincing and the gap between theoretical formulation and actual implementation is too large.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The RDC SDE lacks proper derivation - no demonstration that dynamics produce tractable marginal p_t(ŷ), no training algorithm simulating SDEs in a numerically well-defined way. The paper sells RDC as principled diffusion but it's informal noise augmentation.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Critical training details are missing or contradictory: λ in Algorithm 1 undefined, no precise schedule for encoder training/fine-tuning, insufficient ablations on RDC's actual contribution, and baseline coverage is limited.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because the RDC mechanism lacks mathematical rigor and reproducibility, not because the problem of training with noisy conditions is unimportant.

paper_title: ACTIVE-o3 : Empowering MLLMs with Active Perception via Pure Reinforcement Learning

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The paper's contribution is perceived as incremental - primarily GRPO with reward shaping applied to active perception, with scope-to-generality alignment concerns remaining unresolved.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The method is essentially GRPO with reward shaping for the zoom-in/region-selection task, described as too tailored and incremental by reviewers. The general active perception framework shrinks to a specific 2D zooming problem.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: No clear secondary rejection cause is supported by the reviews.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of perceived incremental novelty, not because the experiments or clarity of presentation were insufficient.

paper_title: GUI-Shepherd: Reliable Process Reward and Verification for Long-Sequence GUI Tasks

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The method is closely related to standard value-function approaches in RL with limited conceptual novelty, and reviewers remained unconvinced about whether PRM is fundamentally necessary over simpler alternatives.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The contribution is close to standard value-function/Q-function approaches in RL, with reviewers questioning whether the reasoning-based PRM is necessary over simpler value heads. The method does not extend beyond standard RL objective adaptations.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Only one model and one benchmark were initially evaluated, with concerns about missing baselines (naive GRPO, PPO with value function) and limited scope of evaluation despite added experiments during rebuttal.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of limited methodological novelty, not because the experiments failed to demonstrate empirical value.

paper_title: UniARM: Towards a Unified Autoregressive Reward Model for Multi-Objective Test-Time Alignment

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The paper over-claims 'Pareto-optimal' or 'strictly more Pareto-efficient' preference modeling without communicating coverage/optimality conditions, and lacks sufficient theoretical explanation for why the parameterization yields better Pareto fronts.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The paper makes strong claims about 'Pareto-optimality' without stating or defending what 'optimal' representation means at the single input-response pair level, or how one would certify coverage against a true oracle frontier. The mechanism explanation is post-hoc.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: The method is an incremental extension of PARM with MoSLoRA being an improved version of PBLoRA. Reviewers noted the contribution is minor changes to prior work plus a regularizer.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of over-claiming and weak theoretical explanation for optimality, not because the empirical results or experimental design were insufficient.

paper_title: Counting Hallucinations in Diffusion Models

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The JDM method is under-developed and lacks sufficient detail about architecture, implementation, and computational overhead. Additionally, the evaluation is limited to small-scale models without validation on large-scale diffusion models like Stable Diffusion or FLUX.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The proposed Joint Diffusion Model (JDM) lacks critical architectural details, implementation specifics, and discussion of computational overhead. The method description in Section 5.5 is under-developed and not conference-ready according to multiple reviewers.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: The evaluation is limited to synthetic datasets and small-scale models. Reviewers consistently request evaluation on large-scale text-to-image diffusion models like Stable Diffusion or FLUX, which is the community's main concern.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of the under-developed JDM method lacking architectural details and implementation clarity, not because the problem of counting hallucinations is unimportant.

paper_title: Fine-tuning VLMs Without Forgetting Is Easier Than You Think

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The paper's core findings are primarily validated on a single classification-style VQA task, and prior work (IIMM, ICCV 2025) shows contradictory results that the paper does not adequately address. The approach is also incremental, using well-known fine-tuning strategies.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The paper's conclusions are primarily validated on a single classification-style VQA task (ImageNet-VQA). The rebuttal did not adequately address concerns about generalization to non-classification tasks like captioning or reasoning.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: The core finding (small learning rates or LoRA prevent forgetting) is not conceptually novel - it aligns with prior work on scaling laws for forgetting and LoRA's regularization effects. The paper does not sufficiently engage with contradictory recent work (IIMM).

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of insufficient task diversity in experiments and failure to address contradictory prior work, not because the 2x2 evaluation framework is not useful.

paper_title: SyncLipMAE: Contrastive Masked Pretraining for Audio–Visual Talking-Face Representations

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The paper uses the same datasets for pre-training and downstream evaluation, limiting evidence for transferability and giving unfair advantage over baselines. Non-standard benchmarks for VSR miss standard LRS2/LRS3 results, and visual dubbing results in supplementary are not SOTA.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The same datasets are used for pre-training and downstream evaluation, limiting evidence for transferability and potentially giving an unfair advantage over baselines that may not have been retrained on these datasets. This is a serious issue especially for synchronization evaluation which is commonly evaluated zero-shot.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Non-standard benchmarks for VSR (missing LRS2/LRS3), and the rebuttal did not fully address the need for standard evaluations to enable fair comparison with existing methods.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of the train/test dataset overlap that undermines fair comparison and transferability evidence, not because the two-bypass masking approach lacks novelty.

paper_title: BERNOULLI FLOW MODELS

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The innovation over existing discrete diffusion models and discrete flow matching is unclear. Performance does not show significant improvement over baselines (BLD achieves better FID on FFHQ), and ablation studies are incomplete.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The innovation of BFM over existing work on discrete diffusion models and discrete flow matching is not clearly articulated. The paper does not adequately address why replacing BLM noise scheduling with a flow-matching-inspired one should improve over established formulations.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: On high-resolution image synthesis (LSUN/FFHQ), BFM underperforms BLD significantly (e.g., FID 10.87 vs 5.85 on FFHQ). The ablation study is not comprehensive, lacking systematic analysis of probability-path design, temperature, and step count.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of unclear innovation over existing discrete diffusion models and weak performance on high-resolution benchmarks, not because the theoretical derivation is unsound.

paper_title: SVRG and Beyond via Posterior Correction

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The paper's proposed method (IVON-PC) shows only minor empirical improvements over baselines, and the evaluation is based on single runs without variance analysis. The connection between SVRG and posterior correction does not yield clear practical benefits.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The empirical improvements are minor and often within error bars. Figure 3 and 5 show that IVON-PC ultimately requires similar gradient computations as SVRG to reach comparable final performance. All runs appear to be single runs without variance analysis, making it difficult to judge actual improvement.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: The paper lacks analysis of added computational cost from Hessian approximations. The rebuttal added Figure 1 but it shows the same pattern - initial improvement but similar final performance to other methods.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of weak empirical improvements (only minor gains within error bars) and single-run evaluation without variance analysis, not because the theoretical connection between SVRG and posterior correction is unsound.

paper_title: Computability of Agentic Systems

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The paper lacks empirical validation of its theoretical framework; despite solid proofs and clear hierarchy, reviewers consistently noted the absence of experiments demonstrating that complexity separations manifest in realistic agent stacks.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The paper provides no empirical evidence that the proposed complexity separations are observable in real agent pipelines. Multiple reviewers requested even small controlled experiments or case studies to validate the theoretical claims, but no experiments were added during rebuttal.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: While the theoretical framework is clear, the practical relevance argument remains narrative and proxy-based. The abstract's claim about 'practical efficiency' was misleading since computation graphs are theoretical constructs, not real agent benchmarks.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because it lacks empirical validation of its theoretical complexity hierarchy, not because its method is theoretically unsound.

paper_title: LLM-based Automated Theorem Proving Hinges on Scalable Synthetic Data Generation

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Critical experimental comparisons and ablation studies were missing from the original submission and only added during rebuttal, raising concerns about thoroughness.

main_rejection_cause.reason: Missing critical experiments including ablation studies isolating contribution of data synthesis vs adaptive beam size, comparisons with whole-proof generation methods, zero-shot performance of base model, and sensitivity analysis on hyperparameters. These should have been included in the original submission.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: The methodology lacks sufficient intuition for key ideas like why constrained decoding enhances tactic diversity or how pruning parameters are chosen. Critical explanations were only added to appendix rather than main body.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because critical experiments were missing from the original submission and placed in appendix, not because the method is fundamentally unsound.

paper_title: BiNoMaP: Learning Category-Level Bimanual Non-Prehensile Manipulation Primitives

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The contribution is perceived as procedural integration rather than methodological advance, with limited novelty for the ML audience and unresolved concerns about generalization.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The paper's technical core is largely procedural, combining existing components without proposing new representations, objectives, or architectures. Reviewers perceive it more as an application note or system integration paper rather than a conceptual advance suitable for ML venue.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Category-level generalization is limited to size variations, and the geometry-aware optimization contains heuristic hand-tuned parameters with arbitrary hyperparameters. The method cannot generalize beyond objects with similar geometry and contact conditions.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because it lacks sufficient novelty for the ML community, being perceived as a system integration paper, not because the experiments are fundamentally flawed.

paper_title: SupGRPO: Enhancing GRPO with Matching-based Online SFT for Text Spotting
