main_rejection_cause.reason: The evaluation is limited to FaceApp-generated deepfakes only, missing identity/expression swaps and cross-dataset evaluations on standard benchmarks like FF++ and Celeb-DF. No user study to assess interpretability at human perception level.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Annotations rely on proprietary MLLMs (GPT-4o) which may introduce bias; FiFa-MLLM is trained and evaluated on the same source data, risking shortcut learning rather than generalizable features.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of incomplete evaluation scope and reliability concerns with synthetic annotations, not because of fundamental method flaws.

paper_title: CTA-Flux: Integrating Chinese Cultural Semantics into High-Quality English Text-to-Image Communities

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The paper's contribution is primarily an engineering adaptation of existing T2I models with limited novelty in algorithmic design, despite addressing a practical cross-lingual application.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The method represents a bilingual extension through an auxiliary language branch and feature alignment, which resembles existing multimodal adaptation techniques; the contribution lies more in application and engineering than theoretical innovation.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Experiments focus exclusively on Chinese prompts with a hand-crafted cultural benchmark. No evaluation of how well the approach generalizes to other languages with different morphology or script systems.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of limited novelty in the architectural approach, not because of weak experimental validation.

paper_title: Segmented Operations using Matrix Multiplications

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The paper demonstrates theoretical novelty with the MMV-RAM model but lacks sufficient experimental validation on general chip designs or prevalent architectures beyond the Huawei Ascend 910B.

main_rejection_cause.reason: Experimental validation is limited to only the Huawei Ascend 910B accelerator. The paper does not demonstrate whether the contributions generalize to other architectures like NVIDIA GPUs or TPUs.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: SpMV experiments compare the NPU implementation against CPU baselines (MKL, Eigen) rather than optimized implementations on the same hardware, making the comparison unfair and limiting the validity of performance claims.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of incomplete experimental validation across different hardware platforms, not because of theoretical weaknesses.

paper_title: Iter-AHMCL: Alleviate Hallucination for Large Language Model via Iterative Model-level Contrastive Learning

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The evaluation relies on older/weaker open models (7B/8B-era variants) with capability preservation benchmarks near chance-level regime (C-Eval around ~25%), making results noisy and conclusions unreliable. The method's mapping from safety labels to truthfulness is questioned, and test set inflation risk exists due to iterative selection on evaluation data.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The evaluation relies on older/weaker open models (LLaMA2, Alpaca, LLaMA3-8B-Instruct) and key capability preservation benchmarks are near chance-level (C-Eval around ~25%), making small deltas difficult to interpret and conclusions unreliable.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: The data/label mapping from safety to truthfulness using PKU-SafeRLHF (safe=true/false) for truthfulness training is questioned, as safety and factual truth are related but not equivalent.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because its experimental evaluation is not compelling enough (weak baselines, near-chance benchmarks), not because the core iterative contrastive method lacks novelty or theoretical grounding.

paper_title: InstructX: Towards Unified Visual Editing with MLLM Guidance

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Limited novelty - the approach mainly extends the MetaQuery 'query + connector' paradigm with only incremental modifications (LoRA fine-tuning instead of freezing MLLM, small MLP instead of large Transformer). The paper reads more like a technical report than a research contribution.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The approach mainly extends the MetaQuery 'query + connector' paradigm by replacing the large Transformer connector with a small MLP and adding LoRA fine-tuning. The claimed unified image/video capability mainly relies on the pre-trained Wan 2.1 backbone rather than a new algorithmic contribution.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Authors only provided qualitative results when image data is completely excluded, leaving the request for quantitative ablation unresolved.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because its novelty is limited (incremental extension of MetaQuery), not because the experimental evaluation or practical feasibility is weak.

paper_title: Flash Multi-Head Feed-Forward Network

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Limited novelty in core methodology - both core ideas (mirroring MH Attention in FFNs and improving kernel via tiling) have been proposed before. The most relevant novelty is the re-scaling of internal component sizes in multi-head FFN. Additionally, experiments only go up to 1.3B parameters.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The core methodologies (mirroring MH Attention in FFNs, tile-wise kernel implementation inspired by FlashAttention) have already been proposed in prior work like MH-MoE. The main novelty is the re-scaling of internal component sizes.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Experiments only test up to 1.3B parameters, lacking large-scale experiments to verify the scaling effect. The paper claims broad applicability but lacks evidence beyond small models.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because novelty is limited (building on existing MH-MoE and FlashAttention ideas), not because the empirical validation or theoretical foundation is fundamentally flawed.

paper_title: Multi-path reasoning on a budget: towards theoretically optimal hyperparameter-free adaptive self-consistency

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Novelty concerns remain after rebuttal - the approach refines similar margin-based heuristics and inherits limitations from ASC/ESC without substantially new conceptual perspective. Practical utility of theory and runtime analysis not sufficiently addressed.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The proposed Blend-ASC approach refines similar margin-based heuristics inherited from ASC/ESC without introducing substantially new conceptual perspective on the core allocation problem.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Practical utility concerns not sufficiently addressed - real-world runtime, wall-clock costs, and latency/cost trade-offs are unclear. Batch inference assumption limits applicability to online or per-query latency constrained scenarios.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because the novelty is incremental (blending existing methods) and practical feasibility not demonstrated, not because the theoretical analysis is weak.

paper_title: Parallel Test-Time Scaling with Multi-Sequence Verifiers

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Incremental novelty - the method is effectively an over-engineered Self-Consistency using consensus signals. Reliance on ad-hoc 'Wait' delimiter constitutes fragile prompt engineering. Training on only 224 problems raises overfitting concerns, and dependence on symbolic equivalence limits applicability.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The method is effectively an over-engineered Self-Consistency utilizing consensus signals. The core innovation (incorporating symbolic equivalence consensus frequency) builds incrementally on existing ideas rather than introducing a fundamentally new paradigm.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: The strict dependence on symbolic equivalence (SymPy) for determining answer equivalence renders the method inapplicable to general-purpose reasoning or fuzzy domains where equivalence checking is unreliable.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because novelty is incremental (over-engineered Self-Consistency) and feasibility is limited (symbolic equivalence dependency, scalability issues), not because the experimental validation is fundamentally flawed.

paper_title: DRGSplat: Depth-Regularized 3D Gaussian Splatting

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The method is perceived as incremental, driven primarily by strong off-the-shelf depth models rather than novel technical contributions. The normal and curvature regularization approach is viewed as a minor modification of existing depth regularization methods.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The core contribution of depth regularization via rendered depth, normal, and curvature losses is viewed as an incremental improvement over prior works (DN-Splatter, etc.) rather than a fundamentally new idea. Reviewers noted the performance improvement mainly comes from the strong off-the-shelf geometry estimator (Metric3Dv2) rather than technical innovation.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Missing key baselines (DN-Splatter, PGSR, VCR-Gaussian) and TNT benchmark evaluation as noted by reviewers. The ablation on depth model variations was considered incomplete for ruling out that the method simply benefits from a stronger depth backbone.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because the method lacks sufficient novelty (incremental over prior depth regularization works), not because the experiments are fundamentally flawed.

paper_title: BioRNN: Bio-Inspired Synergistic Integration of Neuromodulation and Wave Propagation in Recurrent Networks

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The biological motivation for the wave equation-based RNN is unconvincing, and empirical performance is poor—worse than plain vanilla GRU on every experiment.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The model does not convincingly demonstrate competitiveness. On ESC-50, BioRNN is noticeably below a simple GRU. On nsCIFAR-10, BioRNN (54.2%) is far below coRNN. On sMNIST, 98.1% cannot be seen as competitive since this accuracy can be achieved with much simpler methods. Comparisons with state-of-the-art sequence learning models (SSM-like networks) are entirely missing.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: The biological motivation is weak—the link between physical wave equations and biologically inspired recurrent dynamics is unconvincing. The discretization scheme is standard numerical analysis claimed as a major contribution. The modulator (key innovation) has only minor impact on performance in most tasks.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of poor empirical performance (not competitive even with vanilla GRU), not because the theoretical analysis is fundamentally flawed.

paper_title: CGTFra: General Graph Transformer Framework for Consistent Inter-series Dependency Modeling in Multivariate Time Series

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The framework largely re-combines existing graph Transformer components with incremental design choices. The theoretical justification for consistency alignment is weak, and the motivation for dependency consistency is underspecified.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The dynamic graph learning lacks innovation and appears to be a standard adaptive graph construction method widely explored in prior works. The claim that inter-variate dependencies (IVD) are modeled exclusively in shallow layers is unconvincing, weakening the motivation for promoting consistent IVD modeling.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Some claims are overstated and contain factual errors (e.g., claiming consistent enhanced performance on ETT datasets when FilterNet outperforms on ETTm1 and ETTm2 in MSE). Inconsistent bolding in tables. Claims about DGL effects on ECL conflict with table results.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of limited novelty (incremental recombination of existing graph Transformer components), not because the experimental results are completely negative.

paper_title: Regressor-free Intermediate Layer Distillation via Teacher Pruning

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The core idea overlaps significantly with prior work (prune-then-distill and InDistill), and the theoretical justification is weak. Experiments are limited to small datasets without ImageNet validation.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The core idea of pruning the teacher for distillation has been explored in Park & No (ECCV 2022) and InDistill. The authors do not clearly distinguish their method beyond using intermediate (rather than logit) distillation. The mutual information argument is superficial and does not convincingly explain why pruning helps.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Experiments are limited to small toy datasets (CIFAR-100 and TinyImageNet) without ImageNet validation. Key phenomena are unexplained (VGG on TinyImageNet performance drop, ShuffleNetV2 difficulty). Missing comparisons with numerous existing SOTA methods in knowledge distillation.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of limited novelty (overlaps with prune-then-distill and InDistill), not because the experimental setup is poorly designed.

paper_title: Inductive Representation Learning of Temporal Pattern Subgraphs in Temporal Networks

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Marginal innovation with components borrowed from prior work (attention-based aggregation from TGAT, triplet loss from DynamicTriad). Outdated baselines and limited datasets reduce experimental credibility.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The claimed methodological innovation is marginal—many components (attention-based aggregation, triplet loss) are borrowed from prior work such as TGAT and DynamicTriad without substantial conceptual advancement. The paper lacks theoretical analysis of why the combination of TFS and FFS patterns is optimal.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Evaluation is restricted to only two small datasets (Reddit and Wikipedia, 9-10k nodes), leaving scalability and generalizability untested. Baselines are outdated (most from 2018-2020) and missing comparisons with recent methods like DyGFormer and GraphMixer. Neither source code nor hyperparameters provided.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of marginal innovation and outdated experimental baselines, not because the core idea of modeling temporal subgraph patterns is fundamentally unsound.

paper_title: Plug-and-Play Label Map Diffusion for Universal Goal-Oriented Navigation

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Marginal SPL improvement suggests SR gains come from increased exploration rather than quality navigation decisions; method novelty is considered incremental; key baselines missing

main_rejection_cause.reason: Missing results for key baselines (FBE, OpenFMNav) and the marginal SPL improvement on ObjectNav (main metric) suggests the method increases exploration steps rather than improving navigation decision quality, undermining the core claim of effectiveness.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Obstacle-guided diffusion is viewed by reviewers as a minor modification of existing diffusion-based map completion methods (Ji et al., 2024), adding only a heuristic prior rather than addressing fundamental limitations of diffusion models in navigation.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because its main metric SPL improvement is marginal and stems from increased exploration rather than improved navigation quality, not because the plug-and-play diffusion framework lacks practical utility.

paper_title: MCPVerse: An Expansive, Real-World Benchmark for Agentic Tool Use

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Benchmark tasks not shareable or inspectable, critical methodology gaps (key-policy conflict, drift risk), ambiguous statements and unsupported claims

main_rejection_cause.reason: The benchmark tasks are not shareable or inspectable, preventing verification of task quality and making reproducibility impossible; reviewers cannot vet whether tasks are actually high-quality or size the magnitude of the contribution.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Critical methodology gaps including key-policy conflict (reproducibility claim vs. API key requirements), drift risk (unversioned MCP specs), and time-sensitive ground truth that undermines long-term comparability.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because the benchmark is not reproducible (tasks not shareable, time-sensitive validation, key-policy conflicts), not because the benchmark design or tool integration approach lacks merit.

paper_title: Single-Step Bidirectional Unpaired Image Translation Using Implicit Bridge Consistency Distillation

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Missing comparison with optimal transport methods (NOT, DIOTM), unfair diffusion baselines, modest novelty as combination of existing methods

main_rejection_cause.reason: Missing critical optimal transport baselines (NOT, DIOTM) that are essential for fair comparison with state-of-the-art one-step methods; diffusion baselines use different backbones making comparison unfair; diversity evaluation absent.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: The proposed approach is primarily an engineering combination of consistency distillation, DMD, and cycle-consistency loss for DDIB, with adaptive DMCD weighting as the main novelty; not a fundamentally new algorithmic contribution.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because it lacks comparison with optimal transport methods (NOT, DIOTM) and uses unfair diffusion baselines, not because the one-step inference efficiency or bidirectional training design is uninteresting.

paper_title: CellPainTR: Generalizable Representation Learning for Cross-Dataset Cell Painting Analysis

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: CellProfiler features inappropriate for cutting-edge ML research, no comparison to deep learning methods, unclear methodology with missing ablations, grandiose claims

main_rejection_cause.reason: The entire approach presumes CellProfiler features are appropriate for cutting-edge ML research despite strong evidence that self-supervised deep image models (MAEs, ViTs) significantly outperform hand-crafted features in extracting biological signal and enabling robust batch correction.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: No comparison to deep learning-based representation methods, no analysis of learned internal representations, no diversity evaluation, and unclear baseline definitions (Baseline, Sphering) make evaluation incomplete.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because it uses CellProfiler features for cutting-edge ML research without comparing to self-supervised deep learning methods that extract richer biological signal, not because addressing batch effects in cell painting is unimportant.

paper_title: BoMM: Multi-Modality Large-Small Model Bidirectional Collaboration

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Limited algorithmic novelty (GPGA and PDMAC are adaptations), incomplete baselines (missing federated multimodal methods), synthetic evaluation only, generic convergence analysis

main_rejection_cause.reason: GPGA and PDMAC are merely adaptations of existing methods (optimal transport-based alignment, DPO) rather than fundamentally new algorithms; the primary novelty lies in problem formulation rather than algorithmic contribution.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Evaluation is limited to two datasets with synthetic missing-modality settings; missing comparison to existing multimodal federated learning methods (FedMBridge, FedMKT, FedMVP) that directly address the same problem setting.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because its algorithmic novelty is limited (adapting OT and DPO) and baselines are incomplete (missing federated multimodal methods), not because the bidirectional large-small model collaboration paradigm is uninteresting.

paper_title: Enhancing Social Intelligence in LLMs with Hierarchical Reasoning and Utterance-Level Goal Rewarding

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The method's reward design was judged as arbitrary and lacking theoretical justification, with Reviewer V13c unconvinced by the rebuttal that failed to provide principled grounding for variance-gating

main_rejection_cause.reason: The variance-gated reward mechanism and overall reward design were viewed as arbitrary heuristics without sufficient theoretical grounding, with the rebuttal failing to convince reviewers that these choices are principled rather than ad-hoc

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: The technical contribution was considered incremental, combining existing rewards with standard HRL principles and treating the social intelligence aspect as largely handled by the pre-trained LLM rather than the proposed RL algorithm

paper_title: GeoSDF: Plane Geometry Diagram Synthesis via Signed Distance Field

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The method's core approach was perceived as a straightforward application of existing geometric constraint solving principles rather than a paradigm shift

main_rejection_cause.reason: The core idea of formulating geometric constraints as an optimization problem with gradient descent was viewed as a natural application of established techniques in Geometric Constraint Solving rather than a significant advance

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: No clear secondary rejection cause is supported by the reviews.

paper_title: ReSplat: Learning Recurrent Gaussian Splats

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The method was viewed primarily as an initialization strategy for subsequent optimization rather than a standalone feed-forward reconstruction pipeline

main_rejection_cause.reason: The recurrent refinement approach was considered similar to existing feed-forward initialization methods combined with 3DGS optimization, raising questions about whether the recurrent design is truly novel or essential

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Comparisons were limited to certain optimization-based methods in sparse-view settings without fair comparisons to concurrent initialization-plus-optimization approaches

paper_title: MoVE: Synergistic Integration of Temporal and Cross-Variable Experts for Efficient Multivariate Time Series Forecasting

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The method was criticized as an engineering assembly of existing components without compelling new modeling principles

main_rejection_cause.reason: The framework was viewed as an aggregation of existing methods (CycleNet, transformer-based cross-variable attention, MoE gating) without a compelling new modeling principle, similar to existing works like SST, TimeXer, and TimePro

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: The ablation study was incomplete (missing PALCL toggle), the model achieved best results in only a limited number of cases out of 16, and visualization was found unappealing and insufficient

paper_title: Can Large Language Models Develop Gambling Addiction?

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The definition of irrationality was fundamentally flawed, conflating risk-seeking behavior with irrationality, and the limited experimental scope prevented drawing broader conclusions

main_rejection_cause.reason: The conceptualization of irrationality was fundamentally flawed, conflating gambling behavior with irrationality when prompts explicitly instructed goal achievement that required gambling, and the experimental design did not properly establish violations of stated goals

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: The experimental scope was limited to a single gambling task configuration, insufficient to support the broad conclusions about pathological gambling behaviors in LLMs, with additional confounds in prompt complexity analysis

paper_title: Rewiring Experts on the Fly: Continuous Rerouting for Better Online Adaptation in Mixture-of-Expert models

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The method has fundamental theoretical and correctness issues with the confidence-based layer selection strategy, where the paper incorrectly defines high-confidence layers and uses a confidence metric that contradicts stated claims.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The paper contains correctness issues in its optimization strategy: it claims to update 'high-confidence' layers but this should be 'low-confidence' layers, and the confidence formula C_i = -(1/k) sum log(p_{i,j}) is equivalent to entropy where higher values indicate greater uncertainty, contradicting the paper's claim. The area chair identified a counter-example demonstrating that Burg entropy and Shannon entropy claims in rebuttal are mathematically incorrect.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: The optimization objective minimizes cross-entropy loss on already-generated tokens but the goal is to improve routing for future generation steps. Reviewers and area chair note this objective mismatch was not resolved in rebuttal, and there is no theoretical justification for why optimizing on past context guarantees better future performance.

paper_title: PatchMoE: A Time Series Foundation Model with Hierarchical Patch-wise Mixture-of-Experts

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Limited novelty - key architectural components (multi-scale patching, doubly residual stacking, load-balance auxiliary loss) appear in prior works like Pathformer, N-BEATS, and standard MoE training.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The paper's key contributions are incremental: patch-wise experts with different patch sizes are similar to Pathformer's multi-scale block, doubly residual stacking comes from N-BEATS, and load-balance auxiliary loss is standard MoE technique. The area chair concluded the paper does not clearly articulate unique contributions.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Limited benchmark diversity with only 9 datasets and missing ablation on pre-training data scaling. The full-shot comparison uses extended context window (2880) while baselines use shorter windows (512 or less), creating unfair comparison.

paper_title: Representative Action Selection for Large Action Space Meta-Bandits

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Lack of clarity in theoretical contributions and disconnect between theoretical framework and practical applicability to large action spaces.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The paper's theoretical analysis is difficult to follow. Algorithm 1 appears trivial and overly general without clear connection to claimed importance sampling. Theorem interpretations are unclear, particularly why max_{r in R} E_theta[max_{a in r} mu_a] doesn't vanish as epsilon approaches zero. The paper does not clearly explain its connection to existing approaches like X-armed bandits or Zooming algorithm.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Experiments use small toy action spaces that don't demonstrate practical value for large action space applications. The paper is motivated by large action spaces but experiments are disconnected from this motivation.

paper_title: Bayesian Primitive Distributing for Compositional Zero-shot Learning

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Methodological novelty is limited - the core workflow of Bayesian modeling + Monte Carlo sampling is similar to prior work (Prompt Distribution Learning, CVPR 2022), and experimental comparisons use outdated baselines.

main_rejection_cause.reason: Multiple reviewers identified that core components (variational posteriors, Gaussian fusion, normalizing-flow enhancement, Monte Carlo sampling) are established Bayesian/VI tools adapted to CZSL. The workflow of learning probability distributions over prompts and sampling from them is similar to Prompt Distribution Learning (CVPR 2022). Authors emphasized differences in motivation but did not clearly demonstrate major innovations.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Experimental baselines are outdated (from 2022-2023) and fail to incorporate recent methods from CVPR 2024. The paper claims SOTA but lacks comparison with latest published work, raising questions about timeliness and whether improvements are genuinely state-of-the-art.

paper_title: Q-Mirror: Unlocking the Multi-Modal Potential of Scientific Text-Only QA Pairs

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Unresolved concerns about reliability of generated images and lack of evidence for downstream utility - the paper introduces a new task and rubric but fails to demonstrate that TQA-to-MMQA transformation produces useful data for real applications.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The paper lacks evidence that TQA-to-MMQA transformation yields useful data for downstream applications. Reviewer D1fp noted that the most definitive test would be training a VLM on synthetic MMQAs and evaluating on downstream benchmarks. Additionally, the benchmark contains only 440 QA pairs which is insufficient to justify 'large-scale' claims, and generated images still contain factual errors even in 'successful' examples.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Concerns about validity of LLM-as-judge evaluation persist: 62.8% agreement between LLM judges and human annotations is relatively weak, and using models as both generators and judges creates potential self-confirmation bias despite ensemble mitigation.

paper_title: Cross-Cancer Knowledge Transfer in WSI-based Prognosis Prediction

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Central claims rely heavily on single foundation model (UNI2-h), leaving open whether transferability patterns are model-specific rather than fundamental to histopathology

main_rejection_cause.reason: The study's conclusions are entirely contingent on the feature space of a single foundation model UNI2-h. The observed transferability patterns and derived insights may be model-specific artifacts rather than fundamental to histopathology, severely limiting the generalizability of core findings.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Missing completed experiments validating findings with alternative foundation models (e.g., CTransPath). The added few-shot experiments and baselines after rebuttal did not fully resolve doubts about practical significance and robustness.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because its central transferability findings are tied to a single foundation model without cross-model validation, not because the problem is unimportant or the experiments are poorly conducted.

paper_title: Enhancing Object Discovery for Unsupervised Instance Segmentation and Object Detection

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Novelty and significance insufficient for ICLR; incremental contribution building on CutLER/CuVLER with marginal improvements

main_rejection_cause.reason: The method follows the same pseudo-labeling approach as CutLER/CuVLER. The three proposed modules (adaptive temperature, boundary augmentation, rank filtering) are spectral pre/post-processing heuristics on classical NCut, lacking new learning principles or theory. DiffCut represents a more substantive departure from prior work.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: No clear secondary rejection cause is supported by the reviews.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because it represents an incremental contribution using heuristics layered on existing normalized cut methods rather than a machine learning innovation with sufficient significance for ICLR.

paper_title: PPI Candidate Ranking: Large-Scale Evaluation of a Domain Knowledge–Guided Pipeline

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Limited methodological novelty; core approach is post-hoc integration of existing self-explainable models (D-SCRIPT, Topsy-Turvy) without introducing novel learning paradigms

main_rejection_cause.reason: The framework primarily performs post-hoc integration and refinement of outputs from existing self-explainable models (D-SCRIPT, Topsy-Turvy). While it cleverly repurposes intermediate representations, it does not introduce a novel learning paradigm or architectural advance, positioning the work as incremental rather than foundational.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Key baseline comparisons remain missing, including classical sequence-similarity methods (BLASTp, HMMER). Also absent is quantitative ablation analysis isolating each re-ranking signal's individual contribution, leaving unique advantages incompletely proven.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because it represents an incremental post-processing integration of existing models rather than a novel methodological contribution, not because the problem or experiments are fundamentally flawed.

paper_title: ICE-Coder: Integrating White-box and Black-box Testing in Execution-guided Multi-agent Code Generation

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Unclear novelty; method combines existing techniques (multi-agent coding, coverage-guided testing, code review) without clear conceptual or methodological departure from prior work

main_rejection_cause.reason: The primary contribution is combining existing techniques (multi-agent code generation, coverage-guided testing, LLM-based error diagnosis) into a pipeline. Prior work is cited for each component, and the specific combination feels like an incremental system-building paper rather than a fundamental research advance.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Evaluation relies solely on a single 90-problem dataset (LiveCodeBench-Hard). No results on other code-context benchmarks (HumanEval, MBPP) or easier/different difficulty levels are provided, limiting confidence in generalization.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because the novelty is unclear—the main contribution is combining existing techniques without a clean, identifiable takeaway—rather than because the results are poor.

paper_title: Security Tensors as a Cross-Modal Bridge: Activating Text-Aligned Safety to Vision in LVLMs

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Conceptual framing concerns; method resembles prompt-tuned guard mechanism but is not acknowledged as such, and produces only rejections rather than addressing dual goals of helpfulness and harmlessness

main_rejection_cause.reason: The method is not clearly differentiated from existing techniques such as prompt tuning, test-time prompt tuning, or guard-model-based safety filtering. Conceptually, it behaves like a prompt-tuned guard mechanism that detects and rejects harmful prompts, yet this resemblance is not acknowledged and the approach is framed as a novel cross-modal alignment contribution.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: No commercial models were evaluated, and the three datasets (VLGuard, MM-SafeBench) are relatively small with limited diversity. The paper does not compare against broader guard models or safety defenses standard in this line of work.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of conceptual framing concerns—the method functions as a guard mechanism but is not acknowledged as such—rather than because of weak empirical results or lack of technical merit.

paper_title: ReconstructionNet: A Neural Network Architecture for Uncertainty-Aware Predictions with Explainability

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The paper suffers from limited novelty and unresolved scalability concerns. The core methodology (reconstruction loss as regularizer for classification) has been used in prior work, and the architectural choice of creating one encoder per class makes it impractical for any real-world application with many classes. The authors' claim that the method is "primarily intended for domain-specific applications with a small number of classes" does not convincingly address concerns about scalability.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The method requires constructing a separate autoencoder for each class, making it computationally infeasible as the number of classes grows. This fundamental architectural limitation was not convincingly addressed in the rebuttal. The authors acknowledge this is a limitation but restrict the scope to few-class settings, which does not mitigate the concern.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Reviewers identified that reconstruction loss as a regularizer for image classification is not novel and has been used in prior work including Le et al. (2018) and Ghifary et al. (2016). The rebuttal attempts to distinguish the method but novelty concerns likely remain.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of fundamental scalability and novelty issues in the method, not because of experiment quality.

paper_title: One-Embedding-Fits-All: Efficient Zero-Shot Time Series Forecasting by a Model Zoo

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The paper's core methodology is insufficiently justified and unclear. Key components including the co-embedding extractor, how rankings translate into final predictions, and the advantage subset characterization are not adequately explained, undermining reproducibility and confidence in the key mechanism. The paper cannot be accepted due to unclear description of the core methodology.

main_rejection_cause.reason: Key methodological components are insufficiently justified and unclear. The co-embedding extractor's architecture and objectives, how rankings translate into final predictions, and the rationale for the transfer loss are not adequately explained in the main text.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Important failure modes and robustness questions remain unresolved. Cases where the ensemble underperforms the best single model are not adequately explained, and validation of the multi-channel consensus voting versus simpler alternatives is missing.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of unclear core methodology and insufficient methodological justification, not because it lacks significance or novelty.

paper_title: EventSR-Zero: Training-free Event Video Super-Resolution with Diffusion Priors

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The paper lacks sufficient experimental validation. The evaluation datasets (ECD from 2017 and HQF from 2020) are outdated with low resolutions (240×180), making them unsuitable for validating a super-resolution method that claims to recover high-frequency details. No author rebuttal was submitted, and multiple reviewers independently identified the same dataset limitations and missing comparisons as major concerns.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The evaluation relies on outdated and low-resolution datasets (240×180) that are inappropriate for validating a super-resolution method. Missing comparisons with natural baselines (Event-SR followed by E2V reconstruction) and no evaluation on higher-resolution datasets like EventAid or BS-ERGB.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: The evaluation methodology is questionable since full-reference metrics rely on downsampled comparisons due to lack of real high-resolution ground truth. No-reference metrics such as sim-to-real consistency or high-frame-rate optical flow consistency should be included.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of insufficient and inappropriate experimental evaluation with outdated low-resolution datasets, not because of fundamental methodological flaws.

paper_title: Gestalt Reasoning Machines: Structured Perception for Neuro-Symbolic Inference

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The paper suffers from unfair comparison and restricted scope. The proposed GRM uses a dedicated grouping module trained on a specific synthetic dataset (ELVIS) that provides ground-truth grouping labels, while standard baselines (ViTs, VLMs) are not afforded this task-specific supervision. This makes the comparison fundamentally unfair. Additionally, the work is limited to synthetic data and lacks demonstration of generalization to diverse or real-world scenarios.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The evaluation is limited to a single synthetic dataset (ELVIS) specifically designed around Gestalt grouping principles, creating circular validation. No evaluation on standard visual reasoning benchmarks (CLEVR, RAVEN) or real-world data is provided.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Unfair comparison: GRM uses task-specific supervision (grouping labels from ELVIS) that baselines do not have. This makes the comparison between GRM and standard VLMs fundamentally unfair and does not demonstrate inherent superiority of the neuro-symbolic approach.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of unfair comparison and limited evaluation scope, not because the neuro-symbolic framework design itself is flawed.

paper_title: A Pitfall in Conformal Prediction:  When Shorter Intervals Are Not Better

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The paper's framing substantially overclaims its significance. The title suggests a fundamental 'pitfall in conformal prediction,' but the demonstrated phenomenon arises from an intentionally adversarial, externally randomized post-processing step (the 'Prejudicial Trick') that is not itself a conformal prediction method. The contribution is largely a cautionary example about metric misuse rather than a substantive advance, and the proposed interval stability metric has limited practical value since it is identically zero for all standard deterministic CP methods.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The paper fundamentally misframes its contribution. The 'Prejudicial Trick' is not a conformal prediction method but an externally randomized post-processing step. The paper's title and framing suggest a pitfall in CP itself, but the phenomenon is entirely driven by the contrived randomization introduced by PT. The primary conclusion that 'marginal coverage is insufficient' is not new—the conditional coverage limitation has been extensively studied in existing CP literature.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: The randomization mechanism (returning null set with probability p and enlarged interval otherwise) is a standard probability argument that does not constitute methodological innovation. The proposed interval stability metric is only nontrivial for randomized constructions and identically zero for all standard deterministic CP methods.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of overstated significance and framing that misattributes a contrived example to conformal prediction itself, not because of theoretical flaws in the analysis.

paper_title: SmartSAM: Segment Ambiguous Objects like Smart Annotators

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Limited novelty and incomplete experimental validation

main_rejection_cause.reason: The core idea of generating multiple segmentation hypotheses and selecting the best via similarity-based feature filtering is conceptually simple and largely incremental relative to existing reference-based and personalized segmentation methods (ProSAM, VLP-SAM, VRP-SAM). The method relies on straightforward rule-based mechanisms without introducing fundamentally new algorithmic principles.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Key standard benchmarks (COCO-20i, PASCAL-5i) and stronger state-of-the-art reference-based baselines are missing, making it difficult to assess comparative performance. The comparison with SAM and other methods is unfair since SmartSAM benefits from additional information (reference images, more candidate hypotheses) that baselines do not receive.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of limited novelty and incomplete experimental validation, not because the underlying problem of interactive segmentation ambiguity is uninteresting.

paper_title: MeInTime: Bridging Age Gap in Identity-Preserving Face Restoration

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Visual quality concerns and efficiency issues

main_rejection_cause.reason: The method is approximately 6x slower than other diffusion-based approaches (43.37s per image in cross-age setting), raising serious concerns about practical applicability in real-world scenarios. The efficiency comparison in the rebuttal does not include strong non-diffusion baselines which are likely more efficient.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: The method underperforms strong non-reference-based prior approaches like CodeFormer across multiple metrics (Table 1), and qualitative results show visible artifacts (especially around mouth region in Figs. 6, 10, 12, 16, 18). The user study indicates visual results are not consistently preferred.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of efficiency concerns and visual quality issues, not because the cross-age face restoration problem is unimportant or the decoupled training-inference strategy is conceptually flawed.

paper_title: Learning to Unlearn: Machine Unlearning via Learning the Unlearning Behaviors

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Fundamental logical inconsistency and scalability issues

main_rejection_cause.reason: The method fundamentally relies on retraining to generate m retrained models as supervision for learning the unlearning function U, which directly contradicts the stated motivation of avoiding expensive retraining. If one can efficiently retrain to generate training data, one could simply use retraining for actual unlearning, defeating the entire purpose of the method.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Scalability concerns are unresolved: the largest deletion is 3000 out of 11 million samples (0.03%), which does not meet realistic requirements. Real-world scenarios often need to forget much larger portions (1-10%). The training cost for U is not included in efficiency comparisons despite being substantial (m=1000 retraining operations required).

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of the logical inconsistency that the method requires retraining to avoid retraining, not because machine unlearning is an unimportant research problem.

paper_title: Inference-time Scaling for Time-series Processing

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Moderate improvements with unclear novelty and computational trade-offs

main_rejection_cause.reason: No clear secondary rejection cause is supported by the reviews. The rebuttal effectively addressed most reviewer concerns regarding method distinction from existing techniques, theoretical justification through Bayesian uncertainty, and computational overhead clarification. However, borderline scores and concerns about the degree of novelty persist.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: No clear secondary rejection cause is supported by the reviews.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of unclear distinction from existing self-consistency methods and concerns about the modest 2-12% improvement relative to 1-15x computational overhead, not because the inference-time scaling idea is fundamentally flawed.

paper_title: Latent-Space Reinforcement Learning for Image Segmentation

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Limited novelty and inadequate experimental validation

main_rejection_cause.reason: Performance gains likely stem from the reward engineering (especially IoU metric optimization) rather than the RL framework itself. These rewards could be straightforwardly converted to standard loss functions (e.g., 1-IoU loss, Dice loss) without the complex RL machinery. The paper fails to isolate the contribution of the RL framework versus the reward engineering through ablation studies.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Despite being a computer vision paper, the submission contains no qualitative visualizations whatsoever—no segmentation mask comparisons, no failure cases, no visual analysis. This makes it impossible to assess whether the proposed latent-space modulation leads to meaningful perceptual or structural improvements. The absence of visual results severely undermines the credibility of all numerical claims.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of missing qualitative visualizations and concerns that the RL framework itself contributes minimally beyond what simpler loss functions could achieve, not because reinforcement learning has no place in vision tasks.

paper_title: ReAugment: Learning to Augment Few-Shot Time Series with Model Zoo Guidance

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The paper's contribution is considered incremental. While the idea of using RL for data augmentation in time series forecasting is interesting, reviewers found that the novelty over prior work is not sufficiently justified and the role of reinforcement learning is not fully compelling.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The contribution is incremental and the role of reinforcement learning is not fully compelling. The idea of selecting promising training examples for augmentation has been explored in prior work, and the paper does not sufficiently justify how its approach differs fundamentally from existing methods.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: The improvement of the proposed method is not significant, especially on the Exchange dataset. Statistics from multiple runs should be included for all baselines, not just the presented method, and the gains are marginal.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because its novelty and RL formulation are not sufficiently compelling, not because its problem motivation or writing quality.

paper_title: ELSE: An Extremely Lightweight Adapter of Simple Expression for Vision Transformer Fine Tuning

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The paper has limited novelty as the proposed ELSE method is conceptually close to existing PEFT methods like SSF and BitFit. The theoretical derivation is viewed as an empirical observation rather than a robust new theory.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The concept of adding or tuning a bias/shift vector is conceptually very close to existing methods like BitFit and SSF. The authors' argument that ELSE is fundamentally different because it is an external residual link was not seen as a sufficient leap in architectural innovation.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: The theoretical claim that ELSE is an 'equal form' of a zero-initialized Adapter is somewhat overclaimed. Zero-initialization is already a common 'unwritten rule' in many PEFT implementations, making the paper's focus on this discovery feel less impactful.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of limited novelty relative to existing PEFT methods, not because its experimental results or practical efficiency.

paper_title: The Price of Explainability for Kernel $k$-means

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The paper has serious theoretical issues where the assumption about pre-image existence for cluster means in Gaussian/Laplacian kernels is fundamentally flawed. Experiments are also limited to toy datasets with minimal improvements over KIMM.

main_rejection_cause.reason: For the Gaussian or Laplace kernel, there can never exist a pre-image for cluster means unless all points in a cluster are identical. This makes a relevant part of the theory void, as the norm of the mean is less than 1 while the norm of any mapped point equals 1.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: The experimental section is excessively simplistic with datasets that are almost toy datasets with tiny data scale. The performance improvement over KIMM is minimal and marginal.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of serious theoretical flaws in the kernel clustering analysis, not because its core motivation or problem framing.

paper_title: TEPO: A Transferable EDA Prediction Optimization Method Based on Learngene Characterization

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The paper suffers from limited baselines (only compared with Xavier init), insufficient experimental details, and single dataset concerns with only 120 samples used from a large dataset.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The paper only compares against Xavier for transfer initialization and does not compare to other transfer/flow-tuning/knowledge-transfer frameworks in EDA. All results are single numbers with no standard deviations, significance tests, or repeated trials.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Only 100 designs were used for training and 20 designs for testing from a large-scale CircuitNet-N28 dataset (over 10K samples). This raises significant concerns about effectiveness and scalability, and there is no cross-validation or evaluation on different process nodes.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of weak experiments with limited baselines and insufficient statistical reporting, not because its core SVD-based gene/class knowledge decomposition concept is fundamentally flawed.

paper_title: User-Controllable Dense Video Captioning: A Large-Scale Benchmark and Framework

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The paper's experiments are limited to instructional video datasets with no evidence for generalization to other domains. The practical necessity of user-controllable dense captioning is not convincingly established.

main_rejection_cause.reason: All experiments are restricted to instructional video datasets (YouCook2, ViTT) and the DVC task. There is no empirical evidence that the benchmark or model benefits other video understanding tasks like event detection, VQA, or retrieval.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: The practical necessity and real-world demand for user-controllable dense captioning are not convincingly established. The paper lacks user studies, deployment evidence, or concrete scenarios demonstrating that end-users benefit from or desire explicit control over event density and caption depth.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of limited generalization beyond instructional video datasets, not because its core framework or methodology is fundamentally flawed.

paper_title: NeSyGeo: A Neuro-Symbolic Framework for Multimodal Geometric Reasoning Data Generation

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Limited novelty compared to established neuro-symbolic methods like AlphaGeometry and TrustGeoGen, with heavy reliance on teacher model distillation rather than fundamental methodological breakthroughs

main_rejection_cause.reason: The framework lacks distinct advantages over established methods like AlphaGeometry and TrustGeoGen. Reviewer 4nkp explicitly noted that 'the advantages are not sufficiently distinct' from prior neuro-symbolic approaches, and the reliance on DeepSeek teacher models for reasoning constitutes distillation rather than fundamental generation breakthroughs.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Missing important baseline comparisons (Geometry3K), ablation studies for data scaling experiments, and incomplete coverage of geometric problem types. Reviewer XMfm noted the artificial angle distribution (multiples of 15) may not reflect real-world problem diversity.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of limited methodological novelty compared to AlphaGeometry and TrustGeoGen, not because the experiments were insufficiently reported.

paper_title: CLIP-Map: Structured Matrix Mapping for Parameter-Efficient CLIP Compression

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Fundamental concerns about theoretical soundness of the linear mapping assumption for depth compression and unresolved empirical gaps regarding performance degradation and baseline comparisons

main_rejection_cause.reason: The core assumption that new layers can be expressed as a linear function of old layers remains unvalidated. Reviewer 24zq noted that diagonal initialization 'merely preserves partial weight information, but it does not verify or justify the rationality of the linear mapping hypothesis itself.' This critical theoretical gap undermines the entire mapping-based compression framework.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Dramatic performance drops on specific datasets (Stanford Cars: 88.5 to 50.8; MNIST: 65.8 to 13.0) were attributed to 'dataset sensitivity' without empirical comparison data. Missing comparisons with quantization-based compression methods, which are mainstream compression paradigms.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because the fundamental linear mapping assumption for depth compression lacks theoretical validation, not because the paper was poorly written.

paper_title: Universality and kernel-adaptive training for classically trained, quantum-deployed generative models

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Severely limited empirical evaluation restricted to synthetic parity-check datasets, with no demonstration of practical utility or real-world applicability for quantum generative modeling

main_rejection_cause.reason: The experimental evaluation is restricted to synthetic parity-check datasets without any real-world benchmarks. All four reviewers consistently noted this limitation, with Reviewer 47J7 explicitly stating that experiments on 'real, rather than synthetic, datasets is still necessary to convincingly demonstrate that the IQP-type model is not merely a conceptual toy but a practically relevant approach.'

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: The n+1 hidden qubit universality construction is theoretically sound but impractical for near-term NISQ hardware. No analysis of hardware noise effects or small-scale real quantum hardware testing was provided, and the O(n^2) parameters of the adaptive kernel lack runtime/memory comparisons.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of severely limited empirical evaluation on synthetic data only, not because the theoretical contributions were weak.

paper_title: The Cognitive Bandwidth Bottleneck: Shifting Long-Horizon Agent from Planning with Actions to Planning with Schemas

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: PwS demonstrates suboptimal performance compared to PwA in low-to-medium complexity environments where it should theoretically excel, limiting real-world applicability

main_rejection_cause.reason: PwS demonstrates inferior performance to PwA in low-to-medium complexity settings (ALFWorld: GPT-4.1 achieves only 16%, Gemini-2.0-flash achieves only 1%), despite being designed to scale better. The full ALFWorld benchmark was not used for testing. Reviewer cDAS noted 'PwS does not significantly outperform PwA' in ALFWorld despite it being expected to be more complex.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Missing reproducibility details including prompt templates and implementation details despite the Reproducibility Statement promising them in the appendix. Reviewer J1fi noted that 'key details like prompt format, environment wrappers, model parameters, and handling of invalid actions are missing.'

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because PwS shows suboptimal performance in low-to-medium complexity environments, not because the conceptual framework was poorly motivated.

paper_title: UNAAGI: Atom-Level Diffusion for Generating Non-Canonical Amino Acid Substitutions

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Severely limited experimental scale with only 1000 training structures and 2 NCAA benchmark complexes, fundamental statistical flaws in evaluation protocol, and the core NCAA prediction capability remains undemonstrated

main_rejection_cause.reason: Training on only 1000 PDB structures is orders of magnitude below modern protein models. The NCAA benchmark contains only 2 protein complexes. Evaluation restricted to proteins under 100 residues. The core claim of NCAA prediction capability is fundamentally undermined since the model 'tends to interpolate between canonical-like structures' rather than generating chemically distinct non-canonical amino acids.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Evaluation protocol has fundamental statistical flaws: using sampling frequencies from only 100 iterations as probability estimates is statistically weak; severe selection bias from only evaluating positions where both wild-type and mutant appear in samples; no confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests; missing architecture details, hyperparameters, and training procedures preventing reproduction.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of severely limited experimental scale and fundamental statistical evaluation flaws, not because the conceptual approach was invalid.

paper_title: Fault Tolerant Multi-Agent Learning with Adversarial Budget Constraints

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Limited technical novelty (method is incremental over prior work on fault-tolerant MARL), simple evaluation environments not comparable to standard benchmarks, and scalability claims unvalidated

main_rejection_cause.reason: The Switcher-Adversary formulation is incremental; similar attack vectors and faulty agent scenarios have been addressed in uncited prior work (Li et al. ICLR 2024, Zhou & Liu 2023, Zheng et al. 2023). The theoretical contribution is a straightforward instantiation of zero-sum Markov games.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: The evaluation uses simple environments (Traffic Junction, LBF, MPE) instead of standard benchmarks (SMAC, MAMuJoCo) used in cited works. No comparison to existing robust MARL baselines. Scalability claim (scales better than shielding methods) is unvalidated since experiments only use 6 agents while cited work handles 1024.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because the technical novelty is limited and the method builds on well-established zero-sum Markov game foundations without sufficiently distinguishing from prior work, not because the problem of fault-tolerant MARL is unimportant.

paper_title: STAR: Boosting Time Series Foundation Models for Anomaly Detection  Through State-aware Adapter

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Limited technical novelty (methods inspired by prior work without clear distinctions), unclear mathematical formulations, and borderline acceptance scores even with additional experiments

main_rejection_cause.reason: Several methods are described as being inspired by prior work (e.g., LoRA and Shentu et al., 2024), but precise distinctions are not clearly explained. The technical novelty is limited.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Several variables in equations are undefined, making formulations difficult to follow (e.g., Eq. 1, Eq. 5). The dynamic mask incorporation lacks intuitive explanation.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because the technical novelty is limited with unclear distinctions from prior work, not because the problem of handling state variables in TSFM is unimportant.

paper_title: Privacy Leakage via Output Label Space and Differentially Private Continual Learning

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Limited methodological novelty - the mitigation strategies (DP partition selection, data-independent priors) are well-known and the contribution lies mainly in applying them to continual learning

main_rejection_cause.reason: Both mitigation strategies (DP partition selection from Desfontaines et al. 2022, data-independent priors) come from existing work. The contribution is primarily in applying known approaches to a new problem (CL). The theoretical analysis is sound but not a major breakthrough.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: No direct comparison to existing DP-CL baselines like Desai et al. 2021 or Hassanpour et al. 2022. Limited baseline coverage makes it difficult to contextualize how severe the leakage is in prior methods.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because the methodological novelty is limited (using existing DP techniques), not because the identification of label space as a privacy side-channel lacks significance.

paper_title: The Hidden Link Between RLHF and Contrastive Learning

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Unclear and confusing mathematical derivations, missing key standard benchmarks for evaluation, and no comparisons with other DPO variants or PPO

main_rejection_cause.reason: Evaluation focuses exclusively on mathematical and reasoning benchmarks, missing key general-purpose benchmarks like MMLU, AlpacaEval, MT-Bench, and TruthfulQA. No comparison with PPO (classical RLHF) or DPO variants like IPO and KTO.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Math formulations are extremely unclear with vague notations throughout (e.g., T_phi definition, variable definitions, how equations relate to each other). Key notations like y_l, beta, I_DV, T are not explained when first introduced.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of incomplete experiments (missing key benchmarks and comparisons) and unclear mathematical derivations, not because the mutual information perspective on alignment is inherently flawed.

paper_title: GEDAN: Learning the Edit Costs for Graph Edit Distance

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Critical scalability limitation (128 node hard limit), inference time 10-50x slower than baselines, missing state-of-the-art comparisons, and unclear domain generalizability

main_rejection_cause.reason: The hard limit of 128 nodes due to Gumbel-Sinkhorn complexity is critically restrictive and was not adequately addressed in rebuttal. For real-world applications like program graphs or scene graphs with 300+ nodes, the approach is impractical.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Inference time is 10-50x slower than baselines while only marginally outperforming them. This makes the practical utility marginal at best. Also, domain generalizability not shown beyond molecular graphs.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because the method fails to scale beyond 128 nodes and has dramatically slower inference times, not because learning task-aligned edit costs is an unimportant goal.

paper_title: Nexus-Gen: Unified Image Understanding, Generation, and Editing via Prefilled Autoregression in Shared Embedding Space

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Limited novelty - the prefilled autoregression strategy is viewed as a practical adaptation of teacher forcing rather than a fundamentally new modeling concept, and combining AR and diffusion components within a shared embedding space has been explored in prior work

main_rejection_cause.reason: The prefilled autoregression strategy is viewed as a practical adaptation of teacher forcing or prefix-tuning rather than a fundamentally new modeling concept. Combining autoregressive and diffusion components within a shared embedding space has been explored in multiple prior unified or hybrid generative models. The AC notes that autoregression without prefilling can work in embedding space (e.g., Fluid), contradicting the authors' claim.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Missing comparisons with recent methods (OpenUni, BLIP3-o-8B, Bagel) that achieve higher scores on GenEval. It remains unclear whether generation quality should be attributed to the autoregressive embedding predictor or the diffusion-decoder adaptation.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because the technical novelty is limited (prefilled autoregression is a practical adaptation rather than fundamental breakthrough), not because the experiments are poorly executed or the problem is unimportant.

paper_title: Discerning Minds or Generic Tutors? Evaluating Instructional Guidance Capabilities in Socratic LLMs

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Issues with evaluation rigor including inconsistencies between human and LLM evaluators, contradictions in prompts and scoring criteria, and insufficient details regarding data and methodology

main_rejection_cause.reason: Human-LLM agreement reported without sample size, reliability statistics, or inter-rater reliability. The evaluation protocol has contradictions: generation prompts forbid giving final answers while the O-Advance rubric rewards them. These issues undermine the reliability of the benchmark.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Insufficient details regarding data construction, annotation process, and dataset statistics. The domain is limited to middle school science problems in Chinese, raising concerns about generalization.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of evaluation rigor issues (inconsistent scoring criteria, missing reliability statistics), not because the three-phase tutoring framework lacks merit or significance.

paper_title: SpecPrune-VLA: Accelerating Vision-Language-Action Models via Action-Aware Self-Speculative Pruning

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Limited technical novelty (method relies on multiple heuristic strategies without significant breakthrough) and technical errors in presentation, combined with sensitivity to numerous hyperparameters

main_rejection_cause.reason: The method combines existing techniques (attention entropy, token importance scoring, layer selection) that have appeared in other contexts. The training-free design and two-level pruning are well-engineered but do not represent a fundamentally new modeling paradigm.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: The paper contains technical errors and ambiguous statements (e.g., incorrect attention mechanism descriptions, undefined variables, incorrect FLOPs calculation). The velocity-based controller is heuristic with constants chosen empirically.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of limited novelty and technical clarity issues (heuristic approach, technical errors), not because the acceleration results are fundamentally uninteresting or the experiments are completely inadequate.

paper_title: Differential Gated Self-Attention

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Marginal advancement over existing Differential Transformer with modest performance gains, and undertrained baselines on standard benchmarks raising questions about evaluation validity

main_rejection_cause.reason: Replacing DT's static lambda with an input-dependent sigmoid gate is a reasonable modification but represents only a marginal advancement from Ye et al. (2024). The gains are consistent but marginal, especially on saturated or simple benchmarks.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: CIFAR-10 baselines are undertrained (75% accuracy is super low), making comparisons unreliable. ImageNet performance is well below prior work that trains from scratch (e.g., Tokens-to-Token ViT achieved 82.6% four years ago). The limited training time and from-scratch initialization may be undermining the evaluation.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because the novelty is marginal (incremental modification of Differential Transformer with modest improvements), not because the concept of input-dependent gating is fundamentally flawed or the evaluation methodology is completely invalid.

paper_title: Guaranteed Jailbreaking Defense via Disrupt-and-Rectify Smoothing

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Limited methodological novelty (direct extension of SmoothLLM with known techniques), high computational overhead (7.7s vs 0.7s baseline), and significant accuracy degradation compared to original model

main_rejection_cause.reason: DR-Smoothing is not substantially different from SmoothLLM. The two-stage design integrates existing techniques (spell-checking and paraphrasing) that SemanticSmooth already introduced. The theoretical contribution is a trivial application of Hoeffding's inequality, similar to existing random smoothing work.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: High computational overhead: N=10 increases runtime to 7.7s compared to baseline 0.7s. The additional inference cost of majority voting and paraphrasing is huge, making the approach less practical for real-time or API-limited deployment scenarios.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of limited novelty (straightforward extension of existing smoothing methods) and impractical feasibility (high latency overhead), not because the jailbreak defense problem is unimportant or the empirical results are completely negative.

paper_title: PhysTTT: Accurate and Lightweight Cross-Domain Heart Rate Measurement with Test-Time Training

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Double-blind policy violation detected in code repository (name 'YanchengYao' in LICENSE file), combined with insufficient cross-domain generalization evidence despite rebuttal adding MMPD dataset experiments showing significant performance degradation under challenging conditions (walking motion, natural light, darker skin tones).

main_rejection_cause.reason: Code repository contains author name 'YanchengYao' in LICENSE file, violating double-blind review policy

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Cross-domain evaluation limited to UBFC-rPPG and VIPL-HR with only three illumination conditions; MMPD results show significant degradation under challenging conditions (walking motion, darker skin tones); PURE and COHFACE datasets not evaluated

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of a double-blind policy violation in the code repository and limited cross-domain generalization evidence, not because the underlying method (Test-Time Training for rPPG) lacks merit.

paper_title: Characterising Overprecision in Black-Box LLMs: A Cognitive Science Inspired Framework

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Methodological contribution is largely descriptive and incremental, merely repackaging existing uncertainty evaluation ideas under the 'overprecision' terminology without novel methodological contributions; combined with limited evaluation scope (only GPT models tested) and insufficient empirical rigor.

main_rejection_cause.reason: Contribution is mostly descriptive/formalization of existing uncertainty evaluation ideas; cognitive science framing is decorative rather than explanatory; no theoretical development beyond restating overprecision paradigm; refinement strategies are ad hoc

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Only GPT-3.5-turbo and GPT-4o-mini tested; no comparison to open-source models, white-box methods, or different model families (Llama, Claude, Gemini); multiple reviewers remain unconvinced about generalization to 'LLMs'

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because the contribution is largely descriptive and uses terminology borrowed from cognitive science without novel methodological development, not because the problem of LLM calibration is unimportant.

paper_title: Multimodal Cancer Survival Analysis with Learnable Queries

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Conceptually incremental contribution that adapts learnable query ideas from prior works (DETR, BLIP-2, PIBD) to multimodal survival analysis without sufficient theoretical analysis explaining why the approach works without explicit constraints; missing key experimental evidence.

main_rejection_cause.reason: Core idea (learnable query-based token compression) is conceptually incremental relative to PIBD and query-based attention work (G-HANet, Learned Queries for efficient local attention); no theoretical or information-theoretic analysis explaining why the approach improves generalization or reduces redundancy

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: No ablation experiment on number of queries; no ablation with fixed/random query baselines; missing computational cost/FLOPs analysis; baselines not from recent years (2024-2025)

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because the technical novelty is limited (adapting learnable queries from prior works), not because the empirical results on TCGA datasets are weak.

paper_title: Leave No Observation Behind: Real-time Correction for VLA Action Chunks

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Experimental evaluation still inadequately convincing despite rebuttal adding physical robot experiments and Pi0.5 comparisons; lacks real-world validation on challenging tasks, comprehensive baseline comparisons (temporal ensemble, BID, RTC on LIBERO), and quantitative results on physical task.

main_rejection_cause.reason: No real-world experiments on challenging tasks (cube pick-and-place is simple); no quantitative results on physical task provided; Pi0.5+RTC not evaluated on all environments; missing comparison to temporal ensemble and BID baselines; no confidence intervals for success rates

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: No comparison against RTC on LIBERO Spatial despite using much larger correction head (32M params); residual correction head architecture varies across environments (MLP vs transformer) without justification or ablation

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because the experimental evaluation is insufficient (no real-world experiments on challenging tasks, missing baselines, no quantitative physical results), not because the underlying A2C2 idea is conceptually flawed.

paper_title: Decoupling The "What" and "Where" With Polar Coordinate Positional Embedding

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Critical practical barrier unresolved: PoPE implementation doubles K/V cache memory footprint, making it a serious obstacle for training and deploying large-scale models despite conceptual elegance and strong empirical results.

main_rejection_cause.reason: Current PoPE implementation doubles K/V cache memory footprint, described by reviewer as 'serious practical barrier for training and deploying large-scale models'; authors argue FlashAttention-style kernel could mitigate this but provide no implementation, runtime measurements, or memory benchmarks

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Long-context evaluation relies primarily on perplexity on PG-19 without testing functional capabilities (retrieval, QA); lacks comparison to ALiBi and other strong length-extrapolatable positional encodings; no efficiency benchmarks (TFLOP/s comparison)

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because the practical efficiency concern (doubled K/V cache memory) was not resolved despite rebuttal claims, not because the core diagnosis of RoPE's entanglement problem or the PoPE method is fundamentally flawed.

paper_title: Are You Getting What You Pay For? Auditing Model Substitution in LLM APIs

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The paper's main contributions are limited: evaluating existing methods is not sufficient novelty for ICLR, and the proposed TEE solution is impractical for real-world API deployment due to multi-GPU complexity, open-sourcing requirements, and need for provider cooperation.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The paper is described by reviewers as more of a position/survey paper with limited methodological contribution. The main contribution is arguing for TEE-based auditing and measuring overhead, which is valuable engineering but methodologically thin for ICLR. Prior work (Gao et al. 2024) already studied model substitution auditing with rigorous statistical methods.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: The TEE solution requires significant implementation changes, open-sourcing of inference code (unacceptable for providers), and is impractical for multi-GPU setups, pipeline parallelism, and complex routing strategies common in production LLM inference.
