overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The paper's evaluation is severely limited (only 2 models tested), quality of auto-generated benchmark data is unverified, and difficulty modeling methodology has critical flaws.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The evaluation is severely limited with only GPT-4.1 and DeepSeek-V3 tested, cannot reflect capability boundaries of diverse AutoML agents. Additionally, the automatic benchmark construction lacks quality inspection, raising reliability concerns about the synthesized data.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: The difficulty modeling method via leaderboard structure has critical flaws: (1) no filter mechanism on participants to avoid distribution shift, (2) participant count can be misleading for tasks with varying computational demands, (3) the mean score-based difficulty interpretation is flawed.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of severely limited experiments with only two models and unverified benchmark quality, not because the underlying benchmark construction concept lacks significance.

paper_title: Reinforcement Learning Agents in Quantum Code Discovery with Argmax-Preserving Quantization

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Limited novelty (incremental extension of quantization to RL-for-QEC), weak motivation for quantization in this niche setting, and insufficient experimental scale for broader impact.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The contribution appears incremental—the argmax-preserving quantization concept is a specific application to a niche scenario (RL-for-QEC) without theoretical justification of the observed effects. Reviewers note the novelty is limited and the method does not extend significantly beyond prior quantization work.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: The motivation for policy quantization in this narrow RL-for-quantum-code-discovery setting is not convincingly established, and applicability beyond this specific domain remains unclear.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of limited novelty and significance in the niche RL-for-QEC setting, not because the experimental validation was fundamentally flawed.

paper_title: Lightweight Detection of Silent Data Corruption in Distributed Deep Learning

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Flawed experimental evaluation (non-realistic fault injection), missing comparison with prior art on fault tolerance, and limited theoretical guarantees for detection reliability.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The fault injection experiments are flawed: only flipping highest exponent bits is not realistic (bit error rates are uniformly distributed across entire IEEE754 words per prior work); 300 faults total with 5 seeds is statistically insufficient; no comparison with established hardware fault tolerance methods (algorithmic checksums, ECC) that are standard in production.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Missing comprehensive related work: linear algorithmic checksums from the 1980s, Ozen et al's work on DNN resilience, and other hardware-focused fault tolerance mechanisms are not discussed or compared against.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because the fault injection experiments are not realistic and lack comparison with prior art, not because the underlying statistical detection concept is fundamentally unsound.

paper_title: DeepCritic: Deliberate Critique with Large Language Models

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Limited novelty (application of established SFT+RL framework to critique task) and prohibitive computational cost that hinders scalability.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The underlying framework (SFT + RL) is well-established in the reasoning domain; this work is primarily an application of existing paradigms to the critique capability task. Reviewer PU76 explicitly noted the framework is well-explored, and while meta-critique data construction is innovative, it lacks breakthrough innovation at algorithmic or architectural level.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: The data curation pipeline entails prohibitive computational costs—multiple long-sequence inference passes from a 72B teacher model per data point. Reviewer y2i7 identified this as a major scalability bottleneck, which the rebuttal did not convincingly resolve.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of limited novelty (application of established framework) and high computational cost, not because the empirical validation was insufficient.

paper_title: Exact Rates and Saturation Effect of Kernel Ridge Regression over Unbounded Input Space in Large Dimensions

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Insufficient novelty—the proof techniques and main results are nearly identical to prior work (Zhang et al. 2024), with only minor modifications that don't warrant a separate publication.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The AC found that the proof of Theorem 3.4 is almost identical to Zhang et al. 2024—the only difference is an additional assumption to control eigenfunctions in Eq. (22). Similarly, the bias proof and exact rates in Theorems 4.8, 4.10, 4.13 are identical to prior work, with the same phenomenology (plateaus, multiple descent) unaltered from the spherical case.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: No clear secondary rejection cause is supported by the reviews.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of insufficient novelty (proof techniques and results nearly identical to Zhang et al. 2024), not because the theoretical exposition lacks clarity or rigor.

paper_title: RobustVLA: Robustness-Aware Reinforcement Post-Training for Vision-Language-Action Models

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The paper lacks real-world validation and relies on oversimplified Gaussian noise assumptions that don't match complex real-world robotic perturbations. Additionally, the contribution is incremental as adding noise to training is a well-explored technique.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The paper's contribution is incremental - adding noise to training to improve evaluation robustness is a well-explored technique in visual reinforcement learning. The specific novelty for VLAs beyond standard regularization was not convincingly argued.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: The paper lacks real-world validation - all experiments are conducted in simulation (LIBERO) rather than on physical robots, which is critical for validating claims of 'real-world robustness' for VLA models designed for robotic manipulation.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because it makes an incremental contribution and lacks real-world validation, not because the problem of VLA robustness is unimportant.

paper_title: Learning Deep Modality-Shared Self-Expressiveness for Image Clustering with Textual Information

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The paper has unclear motivation and theoretical foundations, with insufficient hyperparameter analysis and missing ablation studies that prevent full assessment of the method's validity.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The paper's motivation is unclear - the term 'unclear distribution of aligned representations' is not sufficiently defined, and the rationale behind why the deep modality-shared self-expressive model works remains unexplained.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Missing ablation studies for the transformation f, g and insufficient hyperparameter sensitivity analysis across all datasets.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of unclear motivation and theoretical foundations, not because the clustering problem is unimportant.

paper_title: RAPTORGraph: Graph-Based Pathway Modeling for Causal Discovery in Single-Cell Perturbations

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The paper has significant methodological concerns including lack of identifiability guarantees, model rigidity with unrealistic assumptions, and insufficient biological validation of learned causal graphs.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The paper lacks identifiability guarantees - the theoretical conditions that guarantee unique causal factors are not formally justified, and the assumption that each gene maps to a single latent factor does not hold in practice for biological pathways.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: All evaluations are performed on a single dataset (Norman-CPA), limiting generalization claims, and no biological validation confirms that learned edges correspond to known gene interactions.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of theoretical gaps and single-dataset evaluation, not because the causal representation learning problem lacks significance.

paper_title: PartInfer: Enabling LLM Inference On Edge Devices

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The paper has insufficient experimental evaluation with weak baseline comparisons and missing key ablation studies for accuracy-efficiency trade-offs.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The paper lacks key ablation studies showing accuracy-efficiency trade-offs, missing comparisons to standard quantization methods (GPTQ/AWQ), and evaluations limited to Llama 3.2 family only without testing on other architectures like Gemma, Qwen, or MoE models.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Baseline comparisons are weak - the claimed 13× speedup is measured only against disk offloading, and the paper omits comparisons with popular edge frameworks like llama.cpp or TensorRT-LLM that practitioners actually use.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of insufficient experimental validation and weak baselines, not because the edge LLM inference problem lacks importance.

paper_title: HAM: Hierachical Adapters Merging for Scalable Continual Learning

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The paper has unclear novelty compared to existing methods like TreeLoRA, limited experimental scope with only synthetic image datasets, and comparisons against outdated baselines.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The paper's novelty is unclear - the hierarchical adapter merging approach appears similar to prior work like TreeLoRA, and the authors do not adequately distinguish their contributions from existing hierarchical/grouping/merging LoRA approaches.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: The paper evaluates only on synthetic image datasets (CIFAR-100, CUB-200, Tiny-ImageNet) without LLM experiments, and comparisons are made against outdated baselines with only marginal improvements.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of unclear novelty and limited experimental scope, not because the continual learning problem lacks significance.

paper_title: Off-Policy Learning in Large Action Spaces: Optimization Matters More Than Estimation

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The paper was rejected primarily due to limited methodological novelty - the proposed PWLL objectives are mathematically equivalent to reward-weighted regression (RWR) or established offline RL methods like CRR/AWAC/AWR, making this an incremental application rather than a fundamental methodological advance.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The proposed PWLL objectives (LPI, cLPI, RegKL) are mathematically equivalent to reward-weighted regression or bandit counterparts of established offline RL algorithms like CRR/AWAC/AWR. The paper fails to clearly position itself as an adaptation of existing methods, overstating its novelty as an 'optimization-centric' discovery when this trade-off is precisely why advantage-weighted methods became standard in offline RL.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: No clear secondary rejection cause is supported by the reviews.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of limited methodological novelty (the PWLL approach is an incremental application of existing offline RL techniques), not because of experimental deficiencies.

paper_title: A Hybrid Feature Tree-Based Approach for Explainable LLMs in Domain-Specific Knowledge Management

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The paper was rejected primarily due to fundamental evaluation gaps: lack of accuracy evaluation against external ground truth (trees could be coherent but factually incorrect) and no evaluation of explanation faithfulness, combined with severely limited experimental scope (single domain, single model, underpowered human evaluation).

main_rejection_cause.reason: The paper lacks evaluation against external ground truth and no faithfulness evaluation. The generated feature trees could be coherent and self-consistent but factually incorrect, and without faithfulness analysis, we cannot determine whether explanations accurately reflect the model's reasoning process. Additionally, experiments are limited to a single domain (mortgage compliance), single proprietary LLM (GPT-4.1), and human evaluation with only 3 experts on 30 instances lacks statistical power.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Human evaluation is severely underpowered (3 domain experts, 30 instances) and lacks statistical power for generalizable conclusions. The paper does not evaluate explanation accuracy against any external ground truth, weakening claims about audibility.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of fundamental evaluation gaps (missing ground truth and faithfulness evaluation, limited scope), not because of core method issues.

paper_title: HexFormer: Hyperbolic Vision Transformer with Exponential Map Aggregation

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The paper was rejected primarily due to limited technical novelty (the main innovation is replacing centroid aggregation with exponential map aggregation in hyperbolic attention, which is a natural extension of prior hyperbolic ViTs), combined with marginal empirical improvements that do not convincingly demonstrate the method's effectiveness.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The main innovation is replacing centroid aggregation with exponential map aggregation in hyperbolic attention, which is a natural and incremental extension of prior hyperbolic ViTs such as HVT, LViT, and HypFormer. Other model components (topological encoding, residual design, normalization) largely follow existing approaches without exploring integration with diverse Transformer improvements.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: The experiments are limited to small image classification datasets (CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, Tiny-ImageNet) without verification on more challenging downstream tasks like object detection or segmentation. No runtime, FLOPs, or efficiency analysis is provided despite hyperbolic operations adding computational overhead. The performance improvements are marginal (0.2-1%), failing to convincingly demonstrate the method's benefit.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of limited methodological novelty (incremental extension of existing hyperbolic ViTs) and marginal empirical improvements, not because of theoretical soundness issues.

paper_title: FlexiFlow: decomposable flow matching for generation of flexible molecular ensemble

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The paper was rejected primarily due to marginal performance improvements over saturated benchmarks (QM9, GEOM-Drugs) and a concerning validity drop on GEOM-Drugs, combined with the lack of empirical justification for why joint generation is superior to simpler sequential pipelines.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The QM9 and GEOM-Drugs benchmarks are over-saturated, with FlexiFlow providing marginal improvement over existing approaches. Reviewer LbWw noted 'no significant improvement' between Tables 1 and 2 compared to SemlaFlow. Additionally, the paper shows a concerning validity drop on GEOM-Drugs and lacks comparison with simpler sequential pipelines (graph generation followed by conformer sampling). The fundamental motivation for joint generation remains not empirically justified.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: The definition of 'representative conformer' as the average structure rather than lowest-energy state lacks chemical significance. The paper admits inability to perform computationally expensive fine-tuning to close the validity gap with SemlaFlow, leaving a slight performance deficit in final results.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of marginal performance improvements over saturated benchmarks and lack of justification for joint over sequential generation, not because of theoretical or methodological problems.

paper_title: Beyond Tokens: Enhancing RTL Quality Estimation via Structural Graph Learning

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The paper was rejected primarily due to limited technical novelty from an ML perspective - the method largely integrates existing techniques (graph masked autoencoding, GNNs, knowledge distillation) with domain-specific adaptations without introducing fundamentally new learning principles.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The work demonstrates limited technical novelty from an ML perspective, primarily integrating existing techniques such as graph masked autoencoding (GraphMAE, MaskGAE) and fine-grained knowledge distillation (VeriDistill) into the RTL quality estimation context without introducing fundamentally new learning principles. The paper lacks discussion of transferable insights or contributions to the general ML community.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Dataset realism and representativeness remain a concern - experiments rely on a newly curated, mostly small-scale and non-industrial dataset. All experiments are confined to OpenABC-D dataset with no evaluation on truly independent/industrial benchmarks or real-world proprietary designs.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of limited methodological novelty (integration of existing techniques without fundamental ML advances), not because of weak experimental validation.

paper_title: Debate with Image: Detecting Deceptive Behaviors in Multimodal Large Language Models

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The core conceptual definition of deception is blurry and subjective. The operationalization using CoT/internal reasoning as a proxy for intention collapses deception into reasoning-answer misalignment, failing to clearly distinguish genuine AI deception from unfaithful reasoning, strategic framing, or other misalignment phenomena.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The definition of deception is blurry and subjective. The paper uses chain-of-thought or internal reasoning as a proxy for intention, which ultimately collapses deception into a class of reasoning-answer misalignment. The benchmark fails to clearly distinguish genuine 'AI deception' from unfaithful reasoning, strategic framing, or other misalignment phenomena.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: The benchmark curation loop (testing on 10 MLLMs until target behaviors emerged) risks distribution overfitting to today's models and prompting style. Inter-annotator agreement statistics are missing, and the line between persuasion and deception remains partly subjective despite rebuttal efforts.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because its core method fails to operationally distinguish genuine deception from reasoning-answer misalignment, not because its experimental evaluation was insufficient.

paper_title: Mitigating Over-Refusal in Adversarial Tuning via Subspace-guided Sample Selection

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The core premise relies on a strong assumption that complex behaviors like 'refusal' and 'robustness' can be captured by single, linear directions in the activation space without sufficient theoretical backing or sensitivity analysis across layers.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The approach assumes a linear correspondence between activation-space projections at a single layer and subsequent parameter-space updates, using one-dimensional directions per behavior to rank samples. There is no sensitivity analysis across layers, pooling choices, or multi-dimensional subspaces, and no theoretical or empirical justification that a single direction captures over-refusal vs robustness without leakage.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Comparison baselines are mostly defense mechanisms at inference or full training, not data curation approaches. The incremental value of subspace-guided selection over simpler active learning methods is not decisively proven.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because its theoretical soundness is weak (single linear direction assumption lacks justification), not because its empirical results were invalid.

paper_title: Discovering and Leveraging Entropy-Complexity Relationships for Efficient Large Language Model Reasoning

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The contribution is primarily empirical and incremental. The relationship between entropy, problem difficulty, and overthinking is validated empirically but lacks strong theoretical grounding, and the evaluation is confined to mathematical reasoning benchmarks.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The entropy-difficulty-overthinking connection remains correlational with limited theoretical justification. The paper does not provide sufficient analysis or theoretical proofs addressing these interconnections.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Evaluation is largely confined to mathematical reasoning tasks (MATH500, AIME24, GPQA); applicability to broader reasoning domains such as commonsense reasoning is not demonstrated. The method also relies heavily on distilled DeepSeek-R1 models.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because the entropy-difficulty-overthinking relationship lacks theoretical grounding, not because the empirical validation on math benchmarks was flawed.

paper_title: Federated Recommendation with Reinforcement Learning based Knowledge Distillation

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The claimed novelty is overstated. Bidirectional KD in FL, multi-teacher KD for FL, mixed-label distillation, and RL-based teacher weighting are all established in prior work. The actual contribution is applying existing techniques to federated recommendation.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The claimed novelty is overstated. Bidirectional KD in FL is not new (FedKD, Nature Comm 2022), multi-teacher KD is well-established (2022-2025), mixed-label distillation is standard practice, and RL-based teacher weighting exists (Yang et al., AAAI 2025). The actual contribution is applying these existing techniques to federated recommendation as an application.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: The paper compares against only one KD-based FR baseline (PTF-FedRec) from 2024 while others are before 2022. Missing critical baselines from recent venues damages the credibility of performance claims.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because its claimed novelty is incremental (applying existing techniques), not because its application to federated recommendation is poorly executed.

paper_title: Causal Effect Identification in the Presence of Latent Confounding with a Single Imperfect Proxy Variable

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The method relies on cross-cumulant estimators with high variance in small samples, leading to poor performance. Additionally, the linear non-Gaussian assumption may be too restrictive and limits applications.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The method requires large sample sizes to achieve satisfactory performance due to high variance of cross-cumulant estimators. This limits utility in data-scarce scenarios and raises practical deployment concerns.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Experimental evaluation lacks robustness checks under noisy proxies, weak confounding, or varying non-Gaussianity strength. The method's behavior with near-Gaussian noise or weak nonlinearity is not tested.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because its practical feasibility is limited by large sample requirements, not because its theoretical contributions to causal identification are weak.

paper_title: Mini-batch Submodular Maximization

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Limited novelty in method contribution combined with unclear presentation of the smoothing model

main_rejection_cause.reason: The theoretical contribution is limited. The paper largely builds on the sparsification framework of Rafiey-Yoshida with the main innovation being application of smoothed analysis. Reviewers noted the method should be compared against stochastic submodular maximization literature where uniform sampling is already a baseline approach.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: The smoothing model definition is unclear - the source of randomness is not explained (whether from f^i being random or from sampling e*). Multiple reviewers expressed confusion on this point, and the authors did not adequately clarify during rebuttal.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of limited method novelty and unclear presentation of the theoretical framework, not because the experiments were insufficient or the problem was unimportant.

paper_title: Transfer Bound of Graph Convolutional Networks across Arbitrary Sparsity

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Incremental contribution with limited experimental validation for the theoretical claims

main_rejection_cause.reason: The stretched graphon approach is an incremental contribution over existing graphon/GNN transferability work. The technical novelty is limited compared to prior works by Ruiz et al., and the generalized graphon concept is known as graphex in the literature. The authors themselves stated they adopt the existing framework with minor modifications.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Experiments use only one dataset (Cora) and one architecture (GCN), which is insufficient to validate transferability claims across arbitrary sparsity levels. The paper should include larger and structurally diverse datasets, different GNN architectures (GAT, GraphSAGE), and synthetic graphon-generated graphs.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of limited novelty compared to existing graphon/GNN transferability literature, not because the theoretical framework was fundamentally flawed.

paper_title: To Trust Or Not To Trust Your Vision-Language Model's Prediction

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Novelty concerns and fundamental method limitations regarding data requirements

main_rejection_cause.reason: The method combines known components (image-text similarity from CLIP, image-to-image similarity via NCM classifier) which have been explored in prior few-shot CLIP adaptation work. The improvement appears to stem from model ensembling rather than a genuinely novel contribution. Multiple reviewers pointed out existing works on CLIP + external vision encoders and visual verification strategies.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: The method fundamentally requires image samples for each class (real or generated). While the rebuttal showed synthetic image generation works, this depends on StableDiffusion being trained on similar web data as the test distribution. On datasets with larger distribution gaps (ImageNet-A, ImageNet-R), the method loses its advantage over baseline zero-shot approaches.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because the novelty was limited and the method still requires in-domain image samples regardless of source, not because the experimental validation was insufficient.

paper_title: Personalized Vision via Visual In-Context Learning

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Limited generalization to truly novel tasks and concerns about method novelty compared to existing visual ICL works

main_rejection_cause.reason: The four-panel visual ICL format and image-to-image task unification have been explored in prior works such as Analogist and ImageBrush. The attention-guided seed scorer is also not novel. The paper largely combines existing ideas (visual ICL format + diffusion transformer) rather than introducing fundamentally new methodological contributions.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Most evaluation tasks have corresponding task types in the VisRel training set, meaning evaluations measure generalization to new instances rather than novel task types. The paper should include ablation studies removing entire task categories to demonstrate true cross-task generalization. Additionally, only one dataset (Cora) and standard GCNs were used in the sparse graph experiments.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of limited novelty compared to existing visual ICL literature and concerns about whether evaluations truly test novel task generalization, not because the overall framework was fundamentally unsound.

paper_title: Unpacking In-Context Learning: Underlying Mechanism and Out-of-Distribution Generalization via Blended Training on Function Mixture

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Poor presentation, lack of theoretical analysis, and insufficient technical depth for a conference publication

main_rejection_cause.reason: The paper is difficult to read with vague terminology, long unfocused paragraphs, undefined terms like 'lowest-error preference', and ambiguous phrases. The blended training setup description is inadequate - it is unclear whether task identity information is provided. Key experimental protocols are vague (e.g., how points are chosen, context length determination).

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: The paper largely extends an existing idea from Li et al. (2024b) on blended training with mechanistic analysis, but lacks clear differentiation. The related work section misses major ICL mechanism papers (function vectors, in-context gradient descent). The proposed masking-based diagnostic is described as 'too naive' by reviewers and lacks theoretical analysis.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of poor presentation, unclear terminology, and lack of theoretical analysis, not because the underlying research question about blended training for ICL was unimportant.

paper_title: ExplicitLM: Decoupling Knowledge from Parameters via Explicit Memory Banks

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The paper lacks critical experimental comparisons and clear experimental methodology. It compares only against a vanilla transformer baseline without comparing to RAG, MemoryLLM, or other relevant memory-based methods. Key claims about updatability (core to the paper's contribution) are not experimentally demonstrated. Missing standard benchmarks and clear evaluation protocols.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The paper only compares against a vanilla transformer baseline and does not include RAG, RETRO, MemoryLLM, or other relevant memory-based methods. Core claims about updatability are not demonstrated through experiments. No standard benchmarks like SimpleQA or NaturalQA are used, and the evaluation data and queries are not clearly described.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Key implementation details are missing, including how memory embeddings are fused into transformer layers, the query network design, and parameter settings. These missing details make reproduction difficult.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of severely insufficient experiments with missing critical baselines and benchmarks, not because the underlying problem of knowledge staleness is unimportant.

paper_title: Latent Reasoning with Recurrent Depth for Sequential Recommendation

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The paper overclaims the 'reasoning' capability without proper semantic guidance signals, and reviewers remain unsatisfied after rebuttal. The term 'reasoning' in recommendation is not well-defined, and the iterative refinement of hidden representations lacks clear semantic supervision comparable to LatentCoT.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The paper overclaims 'reasoning' capability without semantic guidance signals. Unlike LatentCoT which uses semantic supervision for chain-of-thought reasoning, LARES lacks such signals, making the 'reasoning' claim overstated. Reviewers suggest renaming to 'iterative self-refinement process' rather than 'reasoning'.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: The theoretical justification is weak and it is unclear what intermediate reasoning states actually capture. The paper lacks formal definition of 'reasoning step' for recommendations.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because the reasoning claim is overblown and lacks semantic grounding, not because the empirical gains on recommendation tasks are insufficient.

paper_title: Negatives-Dominant Contrastive Learning for Generalization in Imbalanced Domains

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The paper combines existing techniques (SupCon, reweighted cross-entropy, hard-negative mining) in an incremental manner rather than introducing a conceptually new approach. The theoretical bound is not empirically validated and the connection to NDCL's design is described as more rhetorical than principled.

main_rejection_cause.reason: NDCL appears to be an incremental combination of existing techniques: negative-dominant contrastive loss is a simple reformulation of InfoNCE/SupCon, reweighted CE is standard practice in long-tailed learning, and prototype alignment is a standard multi-domain contrastive technique. The paper lacks clear differentiation from existing work.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: The paper does not evaluate on large-scale DomainNet dataset. Performance gains over strong baselines are often within 1-2% without statistical significance tests. The theoretical bound is not quantitatively validated.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because the method is viewed as an incremental combination of existing techniques rather than a novel contribution, not because the problem of Imbalanced Domain Generalization is unimportant.

paper_title: A Universal Self-Supervised Paradigm via 3D Gaussian Splatting

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The paper's novelty is limited to replacing NeRF with 3D Gaussian Splatting in a rendering-based SSL framework. The 'universal' claim is overstated since 2D and 3D branches are trained with different assumptions (RGB-D vs RGB) and indoor-only data. Core design choices are not fully specified or ablated.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The paper largely repackages existing ideas (multi-view feature alignment, rendering-based supervision, masked modeling) within a Gaussian Splatting pipeline. Beyond replacing NeRF with tile-based splatting, no new learning principle or representation insight is introduced. This is an engineering improvement rather than a conceptual advance.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: The method is evaluated only on indoor scenes (ScanNet v2), with no experiments on outdoor or less controlled settings. Gains over strong baselines are modest and sometimes uneven, with notable per-class regressions. The 2D comparison relies on an in-house NeRF baseline whose competitiveness is unclear.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of limited conceptual novelty (primarily engineering adaptation of existing ideas), not because the efficiency gains via 3DGS are not meaningful.

paper_title: On the Convergence of FedProx with Extrapolation and Inexact Prox

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The paper provides incremental convergence analysis for FedExProx under inexact proximal solves, but the novelty is limited to handling an additional bias term. The scope is narrow (only strong convexity with interpolation), and the practical relevance is questioned by reviewers.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The convergence analysis is incrementally novel, extending existing proof techniques without new tools. The main contribution is handling an additional bias term from inexact proximal steps. FedExProx can be reformulated as standard GD with biased gradient, and the analysis follows prior work almost directly.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: The paper addresses a practical gap by removing the unrealistic exact proximal operator assumption, but this concern was partially addressed by prior work (FedNova) and the scope remains narrow. Reviewers found the theoretical contribution incremental and the assumptions (global strong convexity, interpolation) overly restrictive for real-world FL scenarios.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because the theoretical contribution is viewed as incremental without novel proof techniques or broadly applicable insights, not because the problem of inexact convergence analysis is unimportant.

paper_title: Personalized Federated Adaptation via Prototype–Text Contrastive Alignment

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The paper has poor presentation quality and unclear problem motivation (introduction reads as solution searching for problem), with critical claims about data heterogeneity handling not adequately justified and conflation of hyperparameter robustness with ablation studies.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The paper suffers from poor presentation quality and unclear problem motivation. The introduction lacks proper problem framing and critical jargon definitions. Additionally, claims about handling data heterogeneity better than other methods lack granular analysis, and the paper confuses hyperparameter robustness testing with ablation studies.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Despite claiming reduced communication and computational costs, the paper provides no actual evidence comparing these metrics against baselines. The computational overhead and scalability evidence are missing.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of poor presentation and unclear problem framing, not because the core method is fundamentally flawed.

paper_title: SelfCAD: Protecting Your Efficient Reasoning Capabilities via Self Cautious Insertion

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The core technique is essentially a heuristic text augmentation (inserting self-cautious sentences), lacking algorithmic or theoretical depth beyond the problem framing.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The core method is a simple text augmentation heuristic (inserting templated self-cautious phrases) without adaptive components, learning mechanisms, or optimization objectives. The strongest contribution is the problem framing rather than technical depth.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: The defense can be bypassed via simple text preprocessing (filtering, paraphrasing) or alternative distillation pipelines (logits, hidden states). The evaluation remains limited to black-box, text-trace distillation threat model.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of shallow methodological depth and insufficient novelty, not because the problem framing lacks significance.

paper_title: GeneLLM: Inheriting 1.25% of MoE-LLMs to Build Models of 8% Size that Retain 80% Performance

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The title is misleading (80% retention is against an undertrained baseline with mediocre performance), and the claims lack theoretical grounding and practical significance.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The title is misleading as 80% performance is measured against an undertrained baseline. Achieving ~80% of a weak baseline's performance with small models is not significant since 0.6-1B models already achieve similar ratios to 7B models in widely available open-source models.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Distillation baseline is under-specified and performs worse than or similar to scratch training on multiple tasks, suggesting a sub-optimal implementation. All models appear undertrained with only 2B-5B tokens.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of limited practical significance and weak baselines, not because the core approach is entirely without merit.

paper_title: Towards Federated Reinforcement Learning Free of Problem-Parameter-Based Tuning

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The main algorithmic contribution is largely a recombination of known components (control variates, momentum, variance reduction) with an adaptive stepsize mechanism, and the convergence bounds still hide problem-specific parameters.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The algorithm recombines known components already explored in FRL/RL (client momentum, control variate corrections, variance reduction, Hessian-aided updates). The headline rates (sample O(ε^-3), communication O(ε^-2)) are the same as prior work, with the main novel bit being tuning-free hyperparameters.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: The ablation study shows removing control variates results in only marginal performance differences. No reward heterogeneity experiments are provided despite claiming robustness to arbitrary environment heterogeneity.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of limited novelty beyond combining existing components, not because the theoretical results are incorrect.

paper_title: Motion-Aware Concept Alignment for Consistent Video Editing

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The momentum-corrected DDIM scheduler is presented as a heuristic without theoretical grounding, and the contribution appears incremental relative to existing image mixing and video editing methods.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The core ingredients (DDIM inversion plus masked latent injection and consistency propagation) are similar to image mixing (MagicMix, FreeBlend) and video editing propagation methods. The difference from training-free region-aware video editing is unclear and questionable.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Inference time is extremely slow (45 minutes for 147 frames on V100), significantly limiting practical utility and scalability despite being a training-free approach.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of incremental novelty and high computational overhead, not because the task definition lacks merit.

paper_title: Controlling Video Generation with Vision Language Models

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The paper lacks critical quantitative evaluation of visual quality, computational cost analysis, and video results, making it difficult to assess the practical viability of the proposed Ask-A-Video method.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The paper is missing quantitative visual quality metrics, video results, ablation studies, and comparisons with RL-based VLM-judge methods. No computational cost analysis is provided.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Missing concrete training time, optimization steps, and memory requirements make it difficult to assess practical feasibility.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of incomplete experiments (missing visual quality metrics, video results, ablations), not because of fundamental flaws in the novel VQA-based video control approach.

paper_title: Mitigating Fine-tuning Risks in LLMs via Safety-Aware Probing Optimization

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The Safety-Aware Probing method lacks clear theoretical justification for why the probing mechanism is necessary or beneficial over simpler approaches, and the method's scalability and computational overhead remain significant concerns.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The theoretical justification for why probing is needed or beneficial is unclear. The area chair questions why the sophisticated probing approach is necessary when simpler objectives could be tried first.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: No clear secondary rejection cause is supported by the reviews.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of weak theoretical justification for the probing mechanism and computational overhead (2x-3x), not because of experimental design issues.

paper_title: POET: Partially Observed Earth Transformer with High-Dimensional Position Embedding

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The proposed HiPE positional encoding and POET architecture appear largely incremental over existing spatio-temporal transformers and location encoding methods, with insufficient theoretical justification for why the proposed design is fundamentally required.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The contribution appears largely incremental and engineering-driven. The area chair finds the methodological novelty insufficient for ICLR-level publication, and prior work on location embeddings and spatio-temporal encoding is not adequately engaged.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Motivation for the proposed architecture and distinction from existing methods remain unclear, and the 'partially observed' framing is misleading.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of insufficient novelty and unclear methodological motivation, not because of weak experimental validation.

paper_title: A Single Character Can Make or Break your LLM Evals

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The paper demonstrates a clear phenomenon but fails to validate its key claims under generation-based evaluation, which is the dominant real-world evaluation protocol for instruction-tuned models.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The evaluation relies on next-token probability scoring rather than generation-based evaluation, which is the dominant protocol for instruction-tuned models. This limits real-world relevance of the conclusions.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Two reviewers view prompt sensitivity as well-established, and the specific delimiter variance issue may not represent a fundamentally new insight.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of evaluation protocol concerns (prob-based vs generation-based scoring) that limit real-world relevance, not because the underlying phenomenon is unimportant.

paper_title: When Can You Get Away with Low Memory Adam?

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The proposed SlimAdam method significantly overlaps with Adam-mini and other recent memory-efficient optimizers, and lacks clear theoretical justification for why SNR is superior to simpler metrics for compression decisions.

main_rejection_cause.reason: Significant overlap with Adam-mini (same block-wise mean compression framework) and other methods like SMMF and APOLLO. The contribution appears incremental rather than novel.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Missing key comparisons with Adam-mini, SMMF, APOLLO, and other memory-efficient optimizers. The 99% memory saving claim is misleading (actual savings are ~50% of total memory).

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of significant overlap with Adam-mini and insufficient novelty over existing work, not because of weak experimental evidence.

paper_title: Geo-Mamba: Dual-Path Riemannian State-Space Models for Functional Dynamics

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The paper combines multiple existing ideas (SSM, SPD manifold, dual-path architecture, GeoMix) without sufficient novelty or clarity on which components drive performance gains. Ablation studies show minimal impact from individual components, and the complexity of the pipeline is not justified.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The method combines multiple existing ideas (geometric SSM on SPD manifolds, dual-path architecture, pyramid-based feature extraction, GeoMix operator) without sufficient novelty. Reviewers noted that components like the GeoMix operator, distillation path, and geometric SSM have been proposed before. The paper does not clearly identify what is the central novel contribution.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Ablation studies show minimal performance degradation when removing key components, making it unclear which parts of the architecture are actually necessary. Baselines were not properly tuned with optimal hyperparameters, and the comparisons between Geo-Mamba and vanilla Mamba are unclear.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because it combines existing techniques without clear novelty or empirical demonstration of component necessity, not because the problem of geometric deep learning for fMRI is unimportant.

paper_title: Forecasting-Conditioned Reinforcement Learning: Embedding Forecastability as an Inductive Bias

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: While the paper addresses an important problem (forecastability in RL), the method is not sufficiently principled. The conceptual alignment between internal self-predictability and external predictability is unclear, and convergence issues with the forecastability objective were not adequately addressed.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The method is not sufficiently principled. External action predictability (what observers can predict) does not necessarily align with internal self-predictability (aligning executed actions with self-predicted actions). The effects of policy stochasticity and environmental dynamics are tightly coupled in the formulation, limiting optimal trade-offs between predictability and reward performance.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: The contribution appears incremental. Multiple reviewers noted that incorporating forecastability into the policy objective via reward or loss conditioning is relatively straightforward to conceive, and existing techniques like action chunking and options provide similar predictability benefits.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because the method lacks theoretical depth and principled design for the forecastability objective, not because the problem of predictable RL agents is unimportant.

paper_title: WAN3DNS: WEAK ADVERSARIAL NETWORKS FOR SOLVING 3D INCOMPRESSIBLE NAVIER-STOKES EQUATIONS

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The theoretical analysis assumes periodic boundary conditions while all numerical experiments use Dirichlet boundary conditions, creating a critical mismatch. Additionally, the paper lacks comparisons to classical solvers, making it unclear why the neural network approach is advantageous for low-Reynolds laminar flows.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The theoretical error analysis in Theorem 1 assumes periodic boundary conditions (explicitly stated in line 671), but all numerical experiments (Kovasznay, Beltrami, LDC) use Dirichlet boundary conditions. The proof techniques for handling boundary terms via integration by parts are fundamentally incompatible between these boundary conditions, undermining the relevance of the theoretical contribution.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: The paper does not compare WAN3DNS against classical numerical solvers for Navier-Stokes equations. For low Reynolds number laminar flows on simple domains like the lid-driven cavity, classical methods are highly efficient. Without this comparison, the practical value of the neural network approach for the specific test cases is unclear.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because the theoretical claims are misaligned with experimental conditions and the practical necessity of the method for simple laminar flows was not demonstrated, not because the weak-form adversarial approach lacks merit.

paper_title: HashPose: Memory-Efficient Human Pose Estimation via Progressive Hash Codes

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The paper contains calculation errors in memory savings claims and relies on unfair comparisons using stronger backbones and acceleration techniques for HashPose versus non-accelerated baselines.

main_rejection_cause.reason: Comparisons are unfair - HashPose uses ConvNeXt-v2 backbone while baselines use weaker backbones; HashPose is benchmarked with TensorRT and BF16 acceleration while baselines are not; timing comparisons use different GPUs (RTX 3090 vs A100). Additionally, memory calculations contain a unit error (KB vs MB confusion in Appendix C).

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: The paper reports only AP50 metrics while standard COCO benchmarks use full AP metrics. Fine-grained localization (AP75) shows HashPose significantly lags behind state-of-the-art heatmap methods. Ablation study shows counterintuitive results (label smoothing provides +2.8% AP75 improvement without explanation).

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of unfair experimental comparisons and calculation errors, not because the progressive hash code representation lacks novelty or theoretical merit.

paper_title: Inferring Capabilities from Task Performance with Bayesian Triangulation

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The method requires manual construction of measurement layouts, making it difficult to scale to real-world AI agents like LLMs. The identifiability conditions for triangulation are not formally addressed, and the predictive improvements on real data are weak.

main_rejection_cause.reason: Constructing measurement layouts requires substantial domain expertise and manual design by humans, limiting scalability. For powerful AI agents like LLMs, it is unclear what meaningful and measurable task meta-features would capture their diverse capabilities and weaknesses. The paper does not provide a systematic procedure for layout construction.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: The paper lacks a systematic framework for constructing measurement layouts. Robustness levels, stated as a core component of cognitive profiles, are not addressed in the construction methodology. The predictive evaluation on real data (Figure 8) shows weak improvements compared to the synthetic agent setting.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because the manual construction requirement limits practical applicability to powerful AI agents, and the identifiability conditions for triangulation were not formally addressed, not because the Bayesian triangulation concept lacks novelty or importance.

paper_title: LLM-Based Social Simulations Require a Boundary

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The paper primarily summarizes existing work without introducing novel theoretical or methodological contributions, with substantial overlap with prior position papers and no empirical validation.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The paper fails to acknowledge or differentiate itself from prior work (arXiv:2501.08579) which identified the same LLM-inherent limitations. The 'boundary problem' framework does not offer a new conceptual leap beyond existing frameworks like 'LLM-inherent vs Design.' As a position paper where the idea is the main contribution, this overlap is a critical flaw.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: No original simulations are conducted to illustrate the proposed boundaries. The proposed 'boundary checklist' remains conceptual and is not validated through case studies or quantitative analysis, limiting the ability to verify the framework's practical utility.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because it lacks novel intellectual contribution beyond prior work and offers only conceptual discussion without empirical validation, not because the writing is unclear or the core idea lacks significance.

paper_title: Advancing LLM Safe Alignment with Safety Representation Ranking

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The paper presents a simple inference-time approach but fails to convincingly demonstrate practical safety improvements due to weak baselines, indirect evaluation metrics, and missing key ablations.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The evaluation relies on ranking accuracy rather than direct safety outcomes like attack success rate. Baselines are far too weak (only GPT-2 reward model), failing to compare against state-of-the-art methods like ARGS, SafeDecoding, or Llama-Guard. Critical ablations comparing internal vs final representations are missing.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: No systematic layer-wise analysis validates the key design choice of using intermediate representations. Over-refusal evaluation is completely missing despite claims about preserving helpfulness. The method's robustness under high-pressure jailbreak attacks (PAIR, PAP, AutoDAN-Turbo) is not validated.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because the experimental evidence is insufficient to support practical safety claims with weak baselines and indirect metrics, not because the core idea of using intermediate representations for ranking is fundamentally flawed.

paper_title: BM-CL: Bias Mitigation through the lens of Continual Learning

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The paper offers an interesting conceptual framing but provides limited algorithmic innovation and marginal empirical improvements that do not justify the added complexity.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The proposed BM-CL primarily combines existing techniques (GroupDRO, ReSample with LwF, EWC) without fundamental algorithmic innovation. The conceptual framing is novel but the actual method is incremental, combining off-the-shelf components rather than introducing a new mechanism for bias mitigation.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Performance gains over strong baselines are marginal (~1-2% balanced accuracy), potentially within noise margins. The framework requires two-stage pipeline, group identification, and additional hyperparameters (p, λ) making the complexity vs benefit trade-off unfavorable. Statistical significance across seeds and datasets is not established.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because the novelty is limited to combining existing techniques and empirical improvements are marginal, not because the conceptual framing of bias mitigation as continual learning is without merit.

paper_title: Scaling Image and Video Generation via Test-Time Evolutionary Search

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: While the evolutionary framing for test-time scaling is novel, the practical advantages are not convincing due to small improvements over baselines and high computational costs.

main_rejection_cause.reason: EvoSearch requires thousands of NFEs (up to ~5000) to outperform baselines, resulting in 20+ minutes per image generation on a single GPU. This dramatically limits real-world usability. The paper lacks thorough runtime and computational overhead analysis compared to standard sampling methods.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: The evaluation is incomplete as it lacks comparisons with gradient-based optimization methods (ReNO, D-Flow) and the recent state-of-the-art Rollover Budget Forcing (RBF) method. Without these comparisons, it is unclear if the gradient-free evolutionary approach offers any advantage over simpler gradient-based approaches that can achieve results in ~50 iterations.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because the computational cost makes it impractical for real-world use and key baseline comparisons are missing, not because the evolutionary framing of test-time search is fundamentally uninteresting.

paper_title: What are Key Factors for Updates in RL for LLM Reasoning?

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The paper provides an interesting theoretical perspective but lacks rigorous justification for key assumptions and shows only marginal empirical improvements.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The theoretical analysis has critical flaws: normality assumptions for importance sampling ratios and advantages lack empirical justification; the analysis is conducted on logit gradients rather than model parameter gradients; key approximations lack quantified error bounds. The claim that low-probability tokens provide dominant gradient signal lacks both theoretical and empirical support.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Performance improvements are marginal (1-3%) and may fall within noise margins. Critical experiments on hard benchmarks (AIME24, AIME25) are missing. Training dynamics curves on harder math benchmarks are not shown. Direct comparison baselines for emphasizing high vs low entropy tokens are absent.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because the theoretical analysis lacks rigor and empirical improvements are marginal, not because the research direction of adaptive clipping for RLVR is unpromising.

paper_title: SIM-Shapley: A Stable and Computationally Efficient Approach to Shapley Value Approximation

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The paper's method was considered incremental over prior work, with concerns about novelty of applying stochastic optimization to Shapley values and incomplete theoretical analysis. Additionally, experiments suffered from inconsistent baseline comparisons and missing recent state-of-the-art methods.

main_rejection_cause.reason: Reviewers consistently noted that the core of SIM-Shapley relies on stochastic optimization techniques, which the paper overstates as fundamentally novel. The method reformulates KernelSHAP as an optimization problem using EMA updates, but this is an incremental combination of existing techniques rather than a new conceptual framework.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: The paper selectively compares to baselines (sometimes ignoring LeverageSHAP or FastSHAP) and fails to include recent state-of-the-art methods such as ProxySPEX and RegressionMSR. Additionally, concerns about unfair comparisons (different number of function evaluations per algorithm) were not adequately addressed.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because the novelty of its stochastic optimization approach to Shapley values was questioned as incremental, not because the underlying problem of efficient Shapley value computation is unimportant.

paper_title: SALSA-V: Shortcut-Augmented Long-form Synchronized Audio from Videos

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The paper presents a well-engineered video-to-audio system but was rejected primarily due to limited technical novelty - its main contributions (masked training, shortcut loss, synchronization features) are adapted from prior work without significant new insights or fundamental concepts.

main_rejection_cause.reason: Reviewer jLCz noted that 'the paper, while presenting a well-engineered system, suffers from several weaknesses that question the significance and novelty of its contribution.' The core components (architecture from MMAudio, masked training from AudioX/MultiFoley, batch size insights from Synchformer) are all adapted from prior work without fundamental new concepts.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: The experimental comparison is narrow with only two baselines (FoleyCrafter, MMAudio). Key recent methods including V-AURA, AudioX, Frieren, and CAVP are missing. Additionally, the human evaluation shows SALSA-V's audio quality (2.96) is lower than MMAudio (3.16), contradicting claims of outperforming existing methods.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because its technical novelty was considered incremental, not because the practical problem of video-to-audio generation lacks importance.

paper_title: Bandit Learning for Online Scheduling with Immediate Decision

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The paper was rejected due to lack of technical novelty (theoretical contributions are incremental extensions of prior bandit scheduling work), insufficient comparison with related literature, and weak motivation for the model's strong assumptions.

main_rejection_cause.reason: Reviewer NiFr noted that 'the main theoretical contributions feel incremental and can be viewed as extensions of prior work in bandit scheduling.' The MRDF algorithm is described as 'essentially a length-partitioned greedy heuristic' and S-UCB is 'just a direct plug-in of the classic UCB index into MRDF.' The paper failed to compare with related literature on 'admission control with reusable resources' as requested.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: No clear secondary rejection cause is supported by the reviews. While reviewers noted limitations (no buffer, preemption assumption, synthetic-only experiments), these were secondary to the novelty concerns. The authors also failed to update the manuscript despite promising to do so in the rebuttal.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because its theoretical contributions were considered incremental over prior bandit scheduling work, not because the online scheduling problem lacks theoretical or practical interest.

paper_title: Understanding Private Learning From Feature Perspective

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The paper was rejected due to concerns about the connection between noisy gradient descent and formal differential privacy guarantees (no gradient clipping, data-dependent sensitivity bounds) and concerns about novelty relative to prior work (Cao et al., 2022).

main_rejection_cause.reason: Reviewers raised concerns about the privacy guarantee: 'In your analysis, you assume no gradient clipping which, paired with ReLU activation, leads to unbounded L2 sensitivity' (dP2q). The bound on gradient sensitivity 'depends on the norm of the noise term which is unbounded and data dependent' making formal DP guarantees unclear. Additionally, 'it is difficult to follow the (ε,δ)-DP guarantees throughout the proofs.'

paper_title: Next-Token Gradient Sensitivity Probing for LLM Hallucination Detection

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The paper was rejected primarily due to limited evaluation scope (only QA tasks, missing strong baselines) and practical deployment concerns (dependence on labeled reference sets), despite having a novel method and addressing an important problem.

main_rejection_cause.reason: Reviewers noted 'missing strong baseline methods for comparison' (8sjc), 'limited evaluation scope - only QA tasks and small datasets' (bbKK), and lack of 'gray-box experiments on closed-source models such as GPT-4 or Gemma-2' to verify model-agnostic nature (U7zH). The evaluation did not include long-text scenarios or diverse hallucination types.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: The method requires pre-constructed NGS reference distributions for real and hallucinated tokens, which 'may be difficult to obtain in certain domains or low-resource settings' (UFQk). Multiple reviewers questioned practical deployment without access to labeled reference sets.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because its experimental evaluation was limited in scope and baselines, not because the NGS-based hallucination detection method lacked novelty or theoretical soundness.

paper_title: Variance Reduced Distributed Non-Convex Optimization Using Matrix Stepsizes

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The paper lacks sufficient experimental validation and practical feasibility due to reliance on knowing/estimating matrix L, combined with limited technical novelty in the theoretical synthesis.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The method's reliance on knowing or accurately estimating the matrix L (or local Li) is a major practical limitation. The paper acknowledges this but lacks a convincing practical strategy or robustness analysis regarding estimation errors, significantly undermining the applicability of the results.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: The experiments are insufficient. Evaluated on small logistic regression problems on LibSVM datasets neither reflecting moderate-scale non-IID federated benchmarks nor including ill-conditioned settings. CIFAR-10 results show low accuracy (~0.4), offering limited empirical justification for the added complexity.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of the method's impractical reliance on estimating matrix L and insufficient experiments with real-world federated learning tasks and realistic settings, not because the theoretical convergence results are incorrect.

paper_title: Bridging Local Divergence in Federated Learning via Personalized Adjustment Matrix

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The paper has limited novelty relative to existing personalized federated learning methods and shows significant performance degradation in large-scale settings that remains unresolved.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The proposed personalization via client-specific transform is incrementally positioned relative to existing works like FedRod and FedNH. The claim on superiority of keeping the decision space global is not fully justified, and the novelty of personalization as a small client-specific transform in feature space is not significant.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Performance degradation in large-scale settings (double-digit drop as N increases in Table 2) remains unresolved. The critical comparison against FedPAM on CIFAR-100 and Tiny-ImageNet with 500 and 1000 clients was requested but not provided.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of limited novelty relative to existing personalized federated learning methods, not because the approach lacks conceptual merit.

paper_title: Efficient Multi-View 3D Representation via Fusion of View-Agnostic Transformations

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The paper has unclear motivation regarding the claimed limitations of prior methods and insufficient experimental comparisons with current state-of-the-art approaches.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The motivation overstates limitations of prior VT methods. The claim that BEVFormer uses global cross-view attention is inaccurate as it uses deformable (sparse) cross-attention. The heterogeneity issues are not quantitatively demonstrated, and the assumption that cross-view interaction is not important may not hold for camera systems with significant FoV overlap.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Limited comparison coverage - excluding modern SOTA methods like Far3D, BEVNeXt, and GeoBEV on grounds that they are not standalone VT modules significantly limits the practical relevance of the empirical validation.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of unclear and overstated motivation regarding prior method limitations, not because the core technical approach of per-camera processing with polar coordinates lacks merit.

paper_title: M$^2$GenCO: Multi-task Meta Learning for Generative Combinatorial Optimization

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The paper's meta-learning framing is fundamentally misleading (closer to transfer learning), baseline comparisons are unfair due to evaluation protocol issues, and the core algorithmic novelty is incremental.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The one-step inner loop adaptation mechanism for consistency models is theoretically surprising and counter-intuitive. Vanilla MAML is used without addressing well-documented issues including task conflict, negative transfer, and gradient pathology. The framing as meta-learning is misleading since pretrain and test use completely different distributions, violating core meta-learning assumptions.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Baseline comparisons are fundamentally unfair - comparing greedy decoding for baselines versus MCTS for the proposed method creates a double standard. The claimed speedup compares one-shot greedy against iterative/autoregressive methods. No statistical significance testing is provided for any results.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of misleading framing (transfer learning presented as meta-learning), unfair baseline evaluations (greedy vs MCTS), and theoretical concerns about the one-step inner loop adaptation, not because the comprehensive benchmark contribution lacks value.

paper_title: CAT: A Metric-Driven Framework for Analyzing the Consistency-Accuracy Relation of LLMs under Controlled Input Variations

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The paper suffers from poor presentation/organization, limited novelty in the proposed metrics, and insufficient experimental scope focusing only on answer-order perturbations.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The paper is difficult to follow due to figures and metrics introduced out of order (Figures 1-2 appear before definitions). There is limited motivation and intuition for proposed metrics - MCA(c) generalizes majority voting with a threshold but this relationship is not clearly explained, and the DTW component in CORE is mathematically redundant with AUC.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: The evaluation focuses exclusively on answer-order permutations, which limits the generalizability of conclusions. No analysis of semantic, instructional, or contextual variations in perturbations. This single perturbation family makes results potentially permutation-set dependent rather than revealing general consistency properties.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of poor presentation/organization and limited novelty in the proposed evaluation framework, not because the underlying idea of studying consistency-accuracy trade-offs lacks merit.

paper_title: A purely Quantum Generative Modeling through  Unitary Scrambling and Collapse

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The paper was rejected because of fundamental scalability concerns with amplitude encoding and measurement shot requirements, as well as misleading claims about being a 'purely quantum' framework when it includes classical components like projective measurements and classical noise addition.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The paper claims a 'purely quantum' generative model but requires exponential measurement shots for amplitude encoding and readout, making scalability to realistic problem sizes questionable. The combination of deep amplitude encoding circuits with exponential measurement requirements creates fundamental bottlenecks for near-term hardware viability.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Experiments are limited to low-resolution grayscale images (MNIST 16x16) with no validation on higher-dimensional data or real quantum hardware, leaving uncertainty about whether the method can scale beyond toy problems.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because its feasibility claims are undermined by exponential measurement overhead and amplitude encoding bottlenecks, not because the underlying quantum scrambling-collapse concept lacks novelty.

paper_title: A Set-Sequence Model for Time Series

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The paper was rejected primarily due to insufficient experimental comparison with recent state-of-the-art methods, combined with limited methodological novelty.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The paper compares against outdated baselines (early Transformers, S4, LongConv) but omits recent state-of-the-art cross-sectional and time-series architectures such as iTransformer, TimeMixer, PatchTST, and Mamba, making it impossible to assess whether the method is competitive with current advances.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: The proposed Set-Sequence model combines existing permutation-invariant set encoders with standard sequential backbones following Deep Sets and Set Transformer design principles, representing an incremental engineering integration rather than a novel modeling paradigm.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because it lacks comparisons to modern time-series architectures, not because the efficient cross-sectional modeling problem it addresses is unimportant.

paper_title: Discrepancy-Aware Knowledge Distillation for Large Language Models

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The paper was rejected because it combines established distillation techniques with limited novelty and lacks a compelling theory-to-algorithm connection.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The method is perceived as an incremental combination of established importance reweighting and curriculum-style weighting techniques, with discrepancy signals added as an auxiliary signal rather than introducing fundamentally new algorithmic mechanisms.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: The theory section does not clearly compel the specific design choices including two discrepancy sources, the exact weighting form, and their combination, leaving the theory more motivational than determinative of the algorithm.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because its conceptual novelty is incremental and the theory does not clearly determine the algorithmic form, not because the empirical results are weak.

paper_title: RIFT: Group-Relative RL Fine-Tuning for Realistic and Controllable Traffic Simulation

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The paper was rejected because while the overall pipeline is interesting, both the algorithmic novelty and empirical validation of the realism/controllability claims fall short of the expected bar.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The RL fine-tuning component is largely an incremental variant of existing GRPO/PPO-style methods, lacking substantial algorithmic innovation beyond applying established techniques to a specific architecture.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Traffic realism is supported mainly by low-dimensional distributional distances and safety statistics without comprehensive analysis of multi-agent interaction patterns, and key controllability baselines (CTG, LCTGen, SMART) are missing.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because its algorithmic novelty is incremental and key baseline comparisons are missing, not because the closed-loop driving evaluation results are weak.

paper_title: PointLAM: Local Attentive Mamba for Efficient Point-based 3D Object Detection

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The paper was rejected because while it achieves competitive empirical results, the technical novelty is limited and several reviewers raised concerns about clarity of differentiation from prior work.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The key contributions are efficient implementation details rather than fundamental innovations; Deviation Network resembles feature difference operations, DSS is similar to F-FPS, and Bi-directional Mamba follows standard axis-based serialization without clear differentiation from prior Mamba adaptations for 3D data.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: No clear secondary rejection cause is supported by the reviews.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because its technical novelty is limited to efficient implementation details rather than fundamental algorithmic contributions, not because the empirical validation is insufficient.

paper_title: Error Analysis of Discrete Flow with Generator Matching

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The paper claims novelty for a Girsanov-type theorem for CTMCs that was already established in prior work (Pham et al.), and the actual novel contribution (Section 5 error bounds) is presented in a dense, hard-to-follow manner without adequate sampling complexity analysis or sufficient experimental validation.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The claimed main contribution of a Girsanov-type theorem for CTMCs was already established in prior work (Pham et al., ICML 2025). The actual novel contribution lies in Section 5, but this section is only 2.5 pages, extremely dense, and insufficiently explained.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: The paper lacks experiments; numerical experiments added during rebuttal are small and inconclusive in demonstrating practical applicability or sampling complexity.
