secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Distortion metrics in Tables 2 and 3 are often comparable to or worse than XAtlas (a purely geometric non-learning baseline) on multiple test cases, undermining claims of overall superiority. The evaluation lacks rigorous statistical analysis and significance testing.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of limited technical novelty (adapting existing sequence modeling components without substantial innovation), not because the problem framing or experimental evaluation was fundamentally flawed.

paper_title: Agent-Centric Personalized Multiple Clustering with Multi-Modal LLMs

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Insufficient methodological novelty - the approach relies heavily on GPT-4 for supervisory signals and MLLM feature extraction rather than innovative algorithm design

main_rejection_cause.reason: The method relies heavily on GPT-4 supervisory signals and MLLM feature extraction capabilities rather than achieving performance through innovative algorithm design. The core components build on existing paradigms (agent-based graph traversal, LoRA fine-tuning) without novel contributions to the algorithmic framework.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Missing critical comparisons with most relevant state-of-the-art methods, specifically recent works leveraging pre-trained models for interactive clustering such as 'Interactive Deep Clustering via Value Mining' (NeurIPS 2024). Without this comparison, performance gains cannot be attributed to the proposed framework design versus merely employing a large MLLM backbone.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of insufficient methodological novelty (heavy reliance on GPT-4 supervision and MLLM features rather than algorithmic innovation), not because the personalization clustering problem itself lacks significance.

paper_title: Examination Feedback Simulation: Beyond Static and Unique Clinical Trajectories

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Concerns about experimental validity - evaluation relies on proxy metrics and same SimScore is used both for optimization (RL) and evaluation, increasing overfitting risk

main_rejection_cause.reason: The main evaluation is a proxy: models are judged against held-out events that actually happened, while the stated goal is off-path plausibility. Without large-scale clinician validation of true counterfactuals, the central claim remains partially untested. Additionally, the same SimScore metric is used both for optimization (RL training signal) and evaluation, increasing the risk of reward hacking and overfitting to metric quirks.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: The architecture change is minimal - ClinSim is based on Qwen3 with only specialized data curation contributing to performance. No new training paradigm is proposed; the paper only validates contributions of existing paradigms (SFT, CoT, GRPO). The main contributions are the dataset (ClinTrack) and evaluation metric (SimScore), not novel model architecture.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of experimental validity concerns (proxy evaluation for off-path plausibility and dual use of SimScore for training and evaluation), not because the problem of examination feedback simulation lacks importance.

paper_title: Combinational Backdoor Attack against Customized Text-to-Image Models

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Limited methodological novelty - the training losses for text encoder and UNet appear highly similar to key losses in prior works, and the main contribution is identifying a new attack surface rather than a novel attack mechanism

main_rejection_cause.reason: The training losses (Section 4.3 and 4.4) appear highly similar to prior works [Struppek et al. 2022, Zhai et al. 2023]. While the paper identifies a new attack surface in customized T2I pipelines, the approach represents a compositional extension of established techniques rather than a fundamentally new attack mechanism. The main distinction is applying existing loss formulations across modular components.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: The attack coverage is narrow: it requires users to employ two specific compromised components simultaneously (backdoored text encoder + backdoored diffusion model + specific trigger prompt). This substantially reduces the probability of practical impact, raising questions about real-world significance. Attack effectiveness only emerges under very specific conditions.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of limited methodological novelty (similarity to prior backdoor attack works and compositional rather than fundamentally new attack mechanism), not because the identified supply-chain vulnerability in modular T2I pipelines lacks significance.

paper_title: Confounding Robust Meta-Reinforcement Learning: A Causal Approach

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Scalability and practical applicability concerns - the Counterfactual Bootstrap step requires MCMC sampling from posteriors over all possible MDPs, which is computationally infeasible for non-trivial environments

main_rejection_cause.reason: The proposed algorithm (Algorithm 1) relies on Counterfactual Bootstrap using MCMC sampling from posteriors over all possible MDPs. This computational requirement is infeasible for any non-trivial environment, making the proposed algorithm impractical for real-world applications despite theoretical soundness.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: No qualitative analysis demonstrates that the learned latent variable U actually captures the true confounding information. The experimental section only reports final task rewards without any visualization or analysis of the learned latent confounder, despite ground truth being available in controlled environments. Additionally, the experiments are confined to simplified toy domains (Windy Gridworld, Causal Pendulum) with low-dimensional state spaces.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of feasibility concerns (MCMC sampling from posteriors over all MDPs is computationally infeasible for real-world settings), not because the theoretical framework for confounding-robust meta-RL lacks merit.

paper_title: InteractScience: Programmatic and Visually-Grounded Evaluation of Interactive Scientific Demonstration Code Generation

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The evaluation metrics (VLM-as-Judge reliability, metric alignment with task) are problematic and the dataset quality is questionable

main_rejection_cause.reason: VLM-as-Judge reliability is questionable with insufficient human validation. Metrics are counterintuitive (higher OPR on harder questions) and don't align with the critical capability of models in performing scientific demonstration code generation. Dataset quality is questionable with unit test correctness at 4.1-4.2 and faithfulness at 4.4-4.5 on a 1-5 scale.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Human evaluation is minimal for validating VLM-as-Jge and test case verification. Only 10 synthesized instances were randomly sampled for manual inspection, which is insufficient for validation.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because the evaluation methodology (VLM-as-judge reliability, metric design) is unsound and not sufficiently validated, not because the underlying problem of scientific demonstration code generation is unimportant.

paper_title: Gradient Clipping Accelerates Saddle Avoidance in Distributed Optimization

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The contribution is incremental compared to prior literature and the complexity is not competitive with centralized settings

main_rejection_cause.reason: The paper's contribution is incremental. The achieved complexity O(epsilon^-3) is worse than centralized settings and not a significant advancement over prior work. The paper lacks comparison with relevant distributed nonconvex optimization literature (Sun et al. 2020, Pan et al. 2020, Xin et al. 2021). The technical extension from semi-distributed to fully distributed setting is not sufficiently novel.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: No clear secondary rejection cause is supported by the reviews.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because the technical contribution is incremental and the complexity does not advance the state-of-the-art, not because the problem of decentralized saddle point avoidance is unimportant.

paper_title: Towards the Explainability of Temporal Graph Networks via Memory Backtracking

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Computational cost and scalability are not adequately addressed, and improvements over baselines are marginal with insufficient statistical significance

main_rejection_cause.reason: The paper lacks critical experiments including: harder benchmarks (datasets with low repetition rates), ablations for topology attribution and memory backtracking components, and sensitivity analysis. The improvements over baselines are marginal (less than one standard deviation) and lack proper statistical significance testing details.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Computational cost is not adequately addressed. The memory backtracking process has exponential complexity in memory horizon and cubic complexity in number of events. No empirical runtime comparisons against baselines are provided to assess practical feasibility in large-scale scenarios.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because the experiments lack completeness (missing harder benchmarks, ablations) and feasibility evidence (unresolved computational cost concerns), not because the explanation method for temporal graph networks is conceptually unsound.

paper_title: CoSteer: Collaborative Decoding-Time Personalization via Local Delta Steering

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The method has limited novelty as it mainly extends existing context steering methods to cloud-edge collaboration without sufficient algorithmic innovation

main_rejection_cause.reason: The core contribution is limited - the method mainly extends existing context steering approaches (He et al., 2025) to a cloud-edge collaboration setting. The algorithmic innovation is minimal; the FTRL optimization algorithm is adopted directly from previous work (Zhang et al., 2025b). Three out of four reviewers raised novelty concerns, and the rebuttal did not adequately address this issue.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Baselines are compared only for a single model pair (Qwen7B-1.5B), and performance is mixed for other model combinations. More comprehensive baseline comparisons across different model pairs would strengthen the evaluation.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because the technical novelty is limited (mainly extends existing context steering to cloud-edge), not because the privacy-preserving personalization problem is unimportant.

paper_title: Learn to Merge: Meta-Learning for Adaptive Multi-Task Model Merging

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Limited comparisons with state-of-the-art methods and marginal performance improvements over existing approaches

main_rejection_cause.reason: The paper lacks comparison with important SOTA baselines (Twin-Merging, WeMoE, ProDistill, ProbSurgery). The evaluation is limited to 8 tasks when more comprehensive task suites (14 or 20 tasks) would strengthen the findings. NLP experiments use relatively small GPT-2 without LLM-scale validation.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: The meta-learning contribution is relatively incremental - mainly adapting MAML to merging coefficient optimization. It is unclear why meta-learning is necessary compared to simpler adaptive methods or coefficient search. The unified model without adapters underperforms, raising questions about the intrinsic generalization benefit.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because the experiments are incomplete (missing SOTA comparisons and limited scale), not because the meta-learning approach to model merging is conceptually flawed.

paper_title: Variance-Reduced Reinforcement Learning for Large Reasoning Models via James-Stein Baselines

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The paper's novelty is limited as it is primarily a direct application of classical James-Stein shrinkage to RLVR, with minimal performance improvement over RLOO and experiments restricted to math/logic reasoning tasks.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The contribution is primarily a direct application of classical James-Stein shrinkage (James et al., 1961; Stein et al., 1956) to RLVR policy gradient baselines. While the leave-one-out adaptation preserves unbiasedness, the core idea does not introduce fundamentally new mechanisms beyond adapting established statistical techniques to a new domain.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Experiments are limited to math and logic reasoning tasks, with no evidence of generality across different RLVR domains such as instructions, summarization, or control tasks. Ablations on key parameters and robustness to non-i.i.d. rollouts are also missing.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because its novelty is limited to adapting classical James-Stein shrinkage to RLVR, not because the underlying variance reduction concept lacks merit.

paper_title: Spiking Brain Compression: Post-Training Second-order Compression for Spiking Neural Networks

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The paper's novelty is largely incremental (extending OBS/OBC from ANNs to SNNs) and lacks deeper theoretical analysis regarding convergence, optimality, and stability of the compression procedure.

main_rejection_cause.reason: SBC extends existing second-order post-training compression frameworks (OBS/OBC) to the spiking domain. While the integration of spike-train similarity via Van Rossum Distance and the surrogate Hessian is elegant, the contribution is incremental rather than fundamentally new.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: The paper does not provide formal analysis or guarantees regarding convergence, optimality, or stability of the proposed compression procedure. The theoretical depth is limited to derivations without deeper guarantees.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because the core novelty is incremental, extending ANN compression to SNNs rather than introducing new theoretical paradigms, not because the empirical results are weak.

paper_title: Follow the MEP: Scalable Neural Representations for Minimum-Energy Path Discovery in Molecular Systems

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The paper contains fundamental theoretical defects: the loss function relaxation from absolute difference of potential energy to absolute value is logically unsound, and the loss does not enforce continuity of the resulting transition pathway.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The loss function relaxation is fundamentally flawed. Replacing the penalty on absolute difference of potential energy with absolute value of potential energy fundamentally alters the behavior and may lead to collapse of molecular conformations. Reviewer scTv pointed out that the independence assumption underlying the loss does not hold for states in MEP which must form a continuous trajectory.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: The loss function L = (1/B) sum U(phi_theta(s_j)) assumes independence of states which clearly does not hold for minimum energy paths that must be continuous trajectories. The authors failed to address this fundamental issue in their rebuttal.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because the theoretical foundation of the loss function is unsound due to unreasonable relaxation and failure to enforce path continuity, not because the experimental results are unimpressive.

paper_title: Provable Weak-to-Strong Generalization via Overspecified Students and Underspecified Teachers

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The paper lacks sufficient differentiation from the closely related Medvedev et al. (2025) work, with unclear novelty and some potentially incorrect claims about the ReLU network analysis.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The setting closely mirrors Medvedev et al. (2025) with insufficient clear distinction in technical challenges, core insights, or main takeaways. Many findings (e.g., early stopping enabling weak-to-strong generalization) overlap with prior work. Reviewers note that some claimed contributions are already in Medvedev et al. 2025.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Reviewer DZyZ identified potentially incorrect citation and application of Lemma C.4 for the ReLU network section. The claim that weak-to-strong generalization provably occurs for ReLU relies on Gaussian Universality Ansatz which remains unproven for this case. Some statements are incorrectly phrased compared to existing literature.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because its novelty is insufficiently differentiated from Medvedev et al. (2025) and contains technical correctness concerns, not because the general direction lacks importance.

paper_title: Delta-Triplane Transformers as Occupancy World Models

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The method exhibits significant performance degradation in camera-based settings compared to ground-truth occupancy, visible visual artifacts from delta-accumulation, and lacks strong theoretical justification for delta learning.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The theoretical validity of delta learning is questionable. Reviewers raised concerns that sparse targets do not necessarily equate to easier optimization, and that delta prediction can hinder error correction mechanisms found in full-state prediction methods. The claim that occupancy deltas are inherently easier to learn lacks rigorous justification.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: The method shows significant performance degradation when transitioning from ground-truth occupancy to practical camera-based inputs. DOME-F outperforms DTT-F at 0s and 1s, indicating lack of robustness in the triplane encoder for noisy inputs.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because the theoretical foundation for delta learning is insufficiently justified and camera-based performance shows significant gaps, not because the overall approach lacks merit.

paper_title: Rethinking Fair Anomaly Detection From The Group Imbalance Perspective

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Method motivation is confusing and not well-aligned with target problem; the rationality of the second component (fairness-aware contrastive learning) is unclear; theoretical analysis is fragmented and does not cover the full objective function

main_rejection_cause.reason: The method's motivation is confusing as it claims existing fairness-aware methods 'overlook group imbalance' when in fact they do consider imbalance. The AC notes the second component (fairness-aware contrastive learning) lacks clear rationale for how it addresses the target challenge. The theoretical analysis is fragmented with the second part failing to cover the full objective function.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: No clear secondary rejection cause is supported by the reviews.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because its method motivation is misaligned with the problem and lacks clear rationale for key components, not because of experimental issues.

paper_title: ResCast: Enhancing Global Medium-range Precipitation Forecasting with Residual Diffusion Model

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Questionable positioning versus prior ML weather models; missing important baselines (GenCast, NeuralGCM); ERA5 precipitation data has known biases making evaluation validity questionable; insufficient justification for key components

main_rejection_cause.reason: Evaluation relies on ERA5 precipitation data which has known biases and is not appropriate for precipitation evaluation. Important baselines (GenCast, NeuralGCM) are missing or inadequately compared. The paper makes incorrect claims about prior ML weather models and their precipitation capabilities.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Key components lack clear justification: the diffusion process description is unclear, the 'Conservation Law Loss' reduces to L2 on residuals and doesn't encode physical constraints as claimed, and 'global trend knowledge' is vaguely defined.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because its evaluation methodology is flawed (ERA5 precipitation biases, missing baselines), not because the core two-stage forecasting idea lacks merit.

paper_title: Memory-Efficient LLM Pretraining via Minimalist Optimizer Design

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Theoretical analysis is suboptimal and potentially misleading; the paper claims momentum parameters are inherently beneficial based on convergence analysis that conflicts with established results; limited novelty as method recombines existing techniques

main_rejection_cause.reason: The theoretical justification for the optimizer design is suboptimal. The paper claims larger momentum parameters are inherently beneficial, but this conclusion conflicts with established results (Liu et al., NeurIPS 2020) showing SGD with momentum achieves the same asymptotic convergence rate as SGD regardless of beta. The main theoretical motivation for the proposed design appears to rely on incomplete analysis.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: The method combines existing techniques (gradient normalization and momentum) rather than introducing new algorithmic concepts. The contribution is primarily empirical and organizational rather than algorithmically new.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because its theoretical analysis for the optimizer design is flawed and conflicts with established convergence results, not because the experimental results are weak.

paper_title: SpaceR: Reinforcing MLLMs in Video Spatial Reasoning

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Incremental novelty - primarily extends existing GRPO framework with spatial rewards and map imagination; map imagination mechanism shows marginal improvement (1.6%) with insufficient validation; dataset concerns with potential data leakage from ScanNet

main_rejection_cause.reason: The paper primarily adds spatial rewards and a map imagination module to the existing GRPO framework. The overall framework uses existing reward designs with task-level adjustments, making it more of an engineering extension than a theoretical breakthrough. The map imagination mechanism shows only marginal improvement (~1.6%) in ablation studies.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: The SpaceR-151k dataset is constructed from ScanNet, which is also used as a benchmark, introducing potential data leakage risks. The think mode approach decreases performance on general video understanding benchmarks, suggesting the model learns task-specific reasoning that may introduce noise.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because its contribution is incremental (engineering extension of GRPO) and the map imagination mechanism lacks sufficient validation, not because the underlying problem of spatial reasoning in MLLMs is unimportant.

paper_title: Multi-Order Wavelet Derivative Transform for Deep Time Series Forecasting

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Limited novelty relative to DeRiTS; marginal performance gains (even in favorable conditions); poor writing that impedes understanding; insufficient ablation studies

main_rejection_cause.reason: The ablation section does not sufficiently isolate contributions of wavelet decomposition, derivative order, and fusion strategy. The backcast loss mentioned in line 302 lacks ablation study support. Performance gains are marginal even in favorable conditions (Strong-Trend-Weak-Seasonal).

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: The paper appears conceptually similar to DeRiTS, with the primary difference being the replacement of the Fourier-based derivative operator by a wavelet-based one. The overall framework and motivation seem closely aligned.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because the ablation studies are incomplete and performance gains are marginal, not because the theoretical wavelet derivative transform lacks merit.

paper_title: AXIOM: Learning to Play Games in Minutes with Expanding Object-Centric Models

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The paper was rejected primarily due to a self-serving benchmark (Gameworld-10k) that is tightly tailored to the method's inductive biases, failing to demonstrate generalization to standard benchmarks, combined with unresolved scalability concerns about the explicit mean-field inference approach.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The paper relies exclusively on a custom benchmark (Gameworld-10k) that is tightly tailored to the method's object-centric and locally linear priors. Reviewers explicitly requested experiments on standard benchmarks like Atari, DMControl, or Robosuite to assess generalization, but this was never provided. The benchmark appears self-serving and does not allow meaningful comparison with state-of-the-art MBRL methods that use neural networks and amortized inference.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Scalability concerns about the explicit mean-field variational inference and streaming updates remain unaddressed. No empirical measurements or complexity analysis were provided to demonstrate how the method scales to high-dimensional visual inputs or longer-horizon tasks beyond the simple Gameworld environments.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of its lack of evaluation on standard benchmarks, which prevented assessment of generalization beyond the tailored Gameworld-10k suite, not because the method's compositional variational inference framework was technically flawed.

paper_title: RelTopo: Multi-Level Relational Modeling for Driving Scene Topology Reasoning

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The paper was rejected due to unclear claims about joint optimization of perception and reasoning (which remain separately optimized with independent loss functions), insufficient clarification of novelty relative to contemporaneous works like TopoLogic and TopoFormer, and lack of theoretical justification for modeling choices.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The paper claims to achieve joint optimization of perception and reasoning, but the perception level and reasoning level are still implemented separately with independent loss functions for L2L and L2T. Reviewers consistently questioned how this constitutes joint optimization, and the rebuttal failed to provide convincing clarification. The term 'multi-level' was also questioned as the three levels represent different optimization perspectives rather than hierarchical levels.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: The paper lacks clear differentiation from contemporaneous works, particularly TopoLogic (which uses GDT for post-processing), TopoMLP, and TopoFormer. The Geometry-Biased Self-Attention and curve-guided cross-attention mechanisms are not sufficiently distinguished from prior art, and the overall approach still follows the two-branch architecture paradigm of TopoNet or LaneSegNet.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of unclear claims about joint optimization and insufficient novelty relative to existing works, not because its empirical performance on OpenLane-V2 was lacking.

paper_title: OpenHA: A Series of Open-Source Hierarchical Agentic Models in Minecraft

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The paper was rejected primarily because its evaluation is limited to Minecraft environments without demonstrating generalization to other domains, and the CoA framework lacks substantial architectural innovation beyond token-level decomposition inspired by Chain-of-Thought.

main_rejection_cause.reason: CoA is mainly a token-level decomposition inspired by Chain-of-Thought, with no new loss, optimization, or theoretical insight. The framework unifies high-level abstract actions and low-level control through intermediate 'thinking' tokens, but this represents incremental extension rather than fundamental innovation. Reviewers noted the model is still fundamentally based on Qwen2-VL without substantial architectural changes.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: The scope of validation is limited to Minecraft, raising questions about generalizability to other environments like GUI automation, robotics, or other complex games. This single-environment evaluation weakens the broader claims about action space design for generalist AI agents.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of limited novelty (CoA is primarily Chain-of-Thought style decomposition without new architectural contributions) and single-environment evaluation that prevents assessment of generalization to other domains.

paper_title: Controlling Structured Explanations via Shapley Values

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The paper was rejected primarily due to limited novelty (the proposed regularization closely follows Deng et al., 2022), weak theoretical justification for the claimed connection between explanation scale and interaction strength, and insufficient motivation for how controllability translates to practical benefits.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The proposed multi-order interaction regularizer completely follows Deng et al. (2022). The main contribution appears to be the empirical observation of differences in interaction structures between CNNs and Transformers, making this work essentially a combination of Jiang et al. (2024) and Deng et al. (2022) without substantial methodological innovation.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: The paper claims to 'establish a theoretical connection' between subexplanation counts and Shapley-based interaction strength, but the evidence presented is empirical and weak. The correlation between explanation scale and interaction strength is not quantified with proper statistical measures (Pearson, Spearman, Kendall's Tau). Reviewers noted internal inconsistencies in how interpretability benefits are framed.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of limited novelty (the regularization follows prior work closely) and weak theoretical justification for the claimed connection between explanation scale and interaction strength, not because the empirical observations about CNN vs Transformer reasoning patterns were uninteresting.

paper_title: Adversarial Policy Transfer in Mixed Cooperative-Competitive Games

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The paper was rejected primarily due to incremental novelty (combining existing techniques like adversarial training, policy distillation, and transfer learning without clear conceptual advance), lack of theoretical convergence guarantees for the bi-level optimization, and ambiguity in what makes the approach inherently adversarial versus general transferable strategy learning.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The paper lacks theoretical convergence guarantees for the bi-level optimization between adversary and learner. While the adaptive adversarial weight mechanism is justified locally via score disagreement, there is no global convergence or stability analysis. Reviewers noted the bi-level optimization is described conceptually and algorithmically but without theoretical analysis regarding convergence to equilibrium or stability of adversarial updates.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: The novelty is incremental as the framework combines known ideas—adversarial training, policy distillation, and transfer learning—into a coherent system. Reviewers explicitly questioned what distinguishes the method from previous combinations of adversarial training and transfer learning in MARL and single-agent RL.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of lack of theoretical convergence guarantees for the bi-level optimization and incremental novelty, not because the empirical results on MPE, Overcooked, and Atari were weak.

paper_title: DATE: Dynamic Absolute Time Enhancement for Long Video Understanding

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Limited technical novelty - TIM and TASS are closely related to existing works (Seed1.5-VL, BOLT, AKS), representing engineering repurposing rather than novel methodological contributions

main_rejection_cause.reason: All four reviewers unanimously agree that the Timestamp Injection Mechanism (TIM) closely resembles timestamp token injection already proposed in Seed1.5-VL and other prior works, while TASS closely mirrors BOLT and AKS with minor modifications. The contribution is characterized as 'engineering practice' rather than novel scientific insight, failing to meet ICLR's novelty bar.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Despite claiming to solve 'absolute time perception,' the method is not tested on any temporal grounding benchmarks (e.g., QVHighlights, Charades-STA, ETBench). The only baseline for TIM comparison is a weak 'timestamp-in-prompt' method, and comparisons with alternative interleaving variants are missing.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of limited technical novelty (TIM and TASS are repurposed existing ideas), not because the overall framework lacks practical value or clear presentation.

paper_title: When Glass Disappears at Night: A Novel NIR-RGB Multi-modal Solution

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Insufficient physical grounding for using NIR modality and lack of thorough analysis justifying the proposed RGB-NIR configuration over alternatives

main_rejection_cause.reason: Reviewer ysrH raised fundamental questions about why NIR information is necessary and what physical principles justify its use. The authors could not provide in-depth analysis comparing RGB-NIR with alternatives like RGB paired with flash or SWIR. The lack of clear physical grounding for the modality choice undermines the method's theoretical foundation.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: No clear secondary rejection cause is supported by the reviews. While some reviewers mentioned missing SAM2 comparisons, the AC noted most technical concerns were addressed during rebuttal.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of insufficient physical justification for the NIR modality choice, not because the empirical results or dataset contribution were fundamentally flawed.

paper_title: Do Neural Networks Learn Similar Subspaces? An Empirical Exploration of Joint Parametric Subspaces in Deep Neural Networks

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Unclear presentation, overstated universality claim, and insufficient methodological clarity despite extensive rebuttal addressing many concerns

main_rejection_cause.reason: Reviewer rMn9 identified critical unclarity: the theoretical hypothesis is nowhere explicitly stated, Algorithm 1 is poorly written with undefined notation, and experimental setup is opaque. While authors provided clarifications in rebuttal, AC noted plots remain not easily readable with unclear axis labels and annotations.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: The paper's central claim of 'universality regardless of initialization, task, or domain' is overstated. Experiments only use same-architecture families (ResNet, ViT, LLaMA/Mistral), supporting within-architecture similarity rather than true cross-domain universality as claimed in the abstract.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of unclear presentation and overstated universality claims, not because the underlying research direction or experimental breadth was inherently flawed.

paper_title: Never Skip a Batch: Continuous Training of Temporal GNNs via Adaptive Pseudo-Supervision

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Limited novelty compared to existing moving average methods in TGB benchmark and weak support for architecture-agnostic claim

main_rejection_cause.reason: Reviewer hhx9 identified that the proposed pseudo-labeling methods are similar to the 'Moving Average' method already mentioned in the Temporal Graph Benchmark paper. The contribution lies mainly in adding pseudo-label updates to existing TGNs without introducing new architecture, optimization mechanism, or learning paradigm.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: The architecture-agnostic claim is only validated on two closely related models (TGNv2 and DyRepv2). Stronger baselines like DyGFormer, NAVIS, TGAT, GraphMixer are missing. Reviewer WadU explicitly retained rejection noting the evaluation is limited and other models may collapse.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of limited novelty relative to existing TGB moving average methods and insufficient validation of the architecture-agnostic claim, not because the core problem of sparse supervision in temporal GNNs is unimportant.

paper_title: ProMoS: Prototype-Guided Distillation for Generalist Graph Anomaly Detection

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Unclear methodological design choices for the mixture-of-students architecture with no explicit diversity enforcement and limited standalone contributions from key components

main_rejection_cause.reason: Multiple reviewers raised concerns about the discrepancy-aware commitment and refinement mechanism being confusing. No concrete strategy enforces diversity among student models in the mixture-of-students. Notation errors (e.g., ei and ri in Eq.2) and unclear teacher pretraining across multiple graphs persist despite rebuttal explanations.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Ablation studies show limited improvement from modules PB, SB, and DIS, indicating their standalone contributions are not significant. Reviewer 6V1N questioned why Eq.9 measures reliability and noted missing routing regularization in Eq.11. The complexity of the commitment/refinement design undermines interpretability.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of unclear design choices and insufficient evidence for key component necessity, not because the problem of unsupervised generalist graph anomaly detection is unimportant or the overall framework lacks merit.

paper_title: DOES THE DEFINITION OF DIFFICULTY MATTER ? SCORING FUNCTIONS AND THEIR ROLE FOR CURRICULUM LEARNING

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Limited novelty and significance - the paper confirms prior work on curriculum learning without novel methodology, and its key claim about complementary curricula is weakly supported by indirect evidence only

main_rejection_cause.reason: The paper provides no novel methodology - it uses existing scoring functions and models in a purely empirical evaluation, confirming findings already in the literature (e.g., Wu et al., 2021) that curriculum learning is not a 'plug-and-play' solution

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: The experimental scope is narrow with only two mid-sized datasets (CIFAR-10, DCASE2020), outdated architectures, unexplained divergences between datasets, no statistical significance tests for ensemble effects, and limited exploration of key curriculum learning components like pacing functions

paper_title: Rethinking Graph Out-Of-Distribution Generalization: A Learnable Random Walk Perspective

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Limited novelty and incomplete experimental validation - the method is viewed as an incremental combination of known components rather than a paradigm shift, and the critical link between the KDE-based MI loss and actual invariance improvement was not convincingly demonstrated

main_rejection_cause.reason: The conceptual novelty is limited - reviewers view the learnable random walk formulation as a reformulation of existing ideas (adaptive sampling, mutual-information regularization) rather than a fundamental breakthrough, with insufficient discussion of how LRW-OOD differs from prior random-walk-based approaches

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: The validation is incomplete - missing recent strong graph OOD baselines (causal intervention, environment simulation methods), no empirical proof-of-concept linking the KDE-based MI loss to invariance improvement, and scalability to large graphs remains unvalidated

paper_title: Geometric and Information Compression of Representations in Deep Learning

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Incomplete theoretical framing and methodological concerns - the paper measures only NC1 for 'geometric compression' while ignoring the broader Neural Collapse definition (NC1-NC4), and relies on MI estimators whose reliability in high dimensions is questioned

main_rejection_cause.reason: The theoretical framing is incomplete - 'geometric compression' is reduced to only NC1 (within-class variance) while true Neural Collapse involves multiple properties (NC1-NC4). Additionally, the reliability of MI estimators (DoE, NPEET, variational bound) in high-dimensional regimes is insufficiently justified

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: The experiments present a null result rather than strong evidence - reviewers noted inconsistent MI estimator choices across figures, lack of ablation comparing multiple estimators, and the measurement only at end-of-training ignores potential compression phases that occur during training (as in Shwartz-Ziv & Tishby)

paper_title: BLISS: A Lightweight Bilevel Influence Scoring Method for Data Selection in Language Model Pretraining

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Overstated claims and limited theoretical grounding - the paper contradicts its 'from scratch' claim by requiring pretrained models for KL alignment, claims 'long-term impact' while only training 3000 steps, and lacks convergence guarantees or sample complexity analysis

main_rejection_cause.reason: The method makes overstated claims that contradict implementation details - despite claiming to operate 'from scratch', the KL divergence alignment requires a partially trained LLM. The claim to capture 'long-term impact' via training 'to convergence' is contradicted by only 3000 steps and parameter resets. No convergence guarantees, sample complexity analysis, or theoretical bounds on proxy approximation error are provided

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: While the rebuttal addressed some clarity concerns, core claims about independence from pretrained models and long-term impact remain misleading given the actual implementation details

paper_title: LEAN: Library-Based Adaptation for Continuous, Federated Fine-Tuning

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Limited novelty and lack of theoretical justification - LEAN is viewed as an incremental extension of FLoRA rather than a new paradigm, with no convergence guarantees or formal stability analysis, and missing critical baselines to isolate the library's contribution

main_rejection_cause.reason: The paper is described as an incremental step beyond FLoRA rather than a substantive new paradigm - its edge relies on reuse for communications, a proximal term, and native async, which are modest modifications rather than fundamental innovations. No theoretical justification explains why LEAN would converge better than stacking in weak federations

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Critical baselines are missing - no comparison with 'FLoRA + prox' to isolate whether gains come from the library or just the proximal term. No reuse vs. no-reuse ablation to understand drift. Missing recent LoRA-based federated learning methods (FedPEFT, FedPETuning, SLoRA, FedIT). No sensitivity analysis for key hyperparameters (library size n, checkout size m)

paper_title: Panorama: Fast-Track Nearest Neighbors

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Limited novelty (primarily engineering optimizations) and insufficient experimental comparisons to relevant prior work

main_rejection_cause.reason: The paper's primary contribution is identified as engineering optimizations (memory layout changes, batching, SIMD) rather than new algorithmic insight. Relevant prior work (Gao & Long 2023, Yang et al. 2025) that proposed similar ideas for lower bound-based refinement acceleration is missing from comparisons.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Missing comparison to prior work that uses similar lower bound mechanisms for verification speedup. Large-scale benchmarks (100M/1B vectors) are absent; current experiments only reach 1M scale.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of limited novelty (primarily engineering optimization without new algorithmic insight) and missing comparisons to relevant prior work, not because the underlying problem of ANNS refinement acceleration is unimportant.

paper_title: Scalable Option Learning in High-Throughput Environments

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Methodological novelty insufficiently motivated; contributions appear primarily as engineering optimizations rather than fundamental algorithmic advances

main_rejection_cause.reason: Multiple reviewers and area chair identify that SOL's innovations appear as engineering optimizations (unified network, environment wrapper, parallelized computations) rather than fundamental algorithmic advances. The core RL algorithmic advances are modest, reusing option-critic ideas.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: No clear secondary rejection cause is supported by the reviews.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because the methodological novelty is insufficiently motivated (contributions are primarily engineering optimizations), not because the throughput improvements or hierarchical RL approach are unimportant.

paper_title: Multi-Task Learning as Stratified Variational Inequalities

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Theoretical flaw in constraint design where 'loss <= historical average' can lead to degenerate solutions where dominated tasks never update, and insufficient experimental coverage across domains

main_rejection_cause.reason: The constraint 'loss <= historical average' is theoretically flawed. When one objective dominates, other objectives can never update and the constraint becomes meaningless. The constraint can lead to degenerate results even though it performs well in practice for tested experiments. Slater's condition may not hold.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Experiments focus almost exclusively on recommendation datasets with insufficient baseline coverage (missing OMoE, ESMM), no inverse-priority tests, and no runtime/training iteration details. Limited evidence for broader applicability.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because the theoretical constraint design is fundamentally flawed (can lead to degenerate solutions), not because the priority-aware multi-task learning framework lacks practical value.

paper_title: Self-adaptive Retrieval-Augmented Reinforcement Learning for Time Series Forecasting

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Unclear RL correction mechanism and inconsistent experimental results across tables raise concerns about reproducibility and correctness

main_rejection_cause.reason: The RL correction mechanism is unclear - it is not explained how the policy network learns mean and standard deviation from reference and initial predictions, and whether correction terms are generated per timestep or for entire time series. The mathematical details of the RL correction step are not fully elaborated.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Results are inconsistent between Table 1 and Table 2 for the same model (iTransformer+SRRF). Some baseline results are significantly worse than reported in original papers.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of unclear RL correction mechanism description and inconsistent experimental results, not because the idea of using RL to correct spectral bias in time series forecasting is unpromising.

paper_title: Reciprocal Label Diffusion for Learning with Noisy Labels

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Insufficient theoretical motivation for using diffusion models (simpler approaches may suffice), unaddressed stability concerns for reciprocal learning, and lack of mechanistic evidence for how diffusion captures and corrects label noise

main_rejection_cause.reason: The reciprocal learning framework lacks stability guarantees. If the prediction model produces biased logits early in training, the diffusion model guided by these may incorrectly denoise correct labels, creating a circular reinforcement of mistakes leading to system collapse or convergence to suboptimal solutions. The Gaussian noise assumption may not hold for complex real-world structured noise.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Insufficient theoretical motivation - the paper fails to clearly articulate why diffusion models are necessary compared to simpler label correction methods. The justification for why diffusion is essential rather than convenient is weak.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of unresolved stability concerns in the reciprocal learning mechanism and insufficient theoretical justification for why diffusion models are necessary over simpler approaches, not because the novel idea of using diffusion for label denoising lacks potential.

paper_title: Lightweight MSA Design Advances Protein Folding From Evolutionary Embeddings

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The main rejection reason centers on methodological soundness concerns: the paper relies on unverified AI-generated embeddings from ESM-2 treated as evolutionary data without sufficient justification or co-evolutionary validation, raising risks of propagating training-set biases.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The method uses ESM-2 embeddings as the only source of evolutionary signal, which are AI-generated unvalidated representations treated as if they contained true biological information. This undermines methodological soundness and risks propagating training-set biases without co-evolutionary metrics to confirm synthetic MSAs carry meaningful structure information.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Missing ablation studies on different loss functions, MSA selection module effectiveness, sensitivity analysis of conservation-diversity tradeoff, and proper baselines for comparison. The HiFiAD efficacy claim lacks sufficient evidence.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of methodological soundness concerns about using unverified ESM-2 embeddings as evolutionary data without co-evolutionary validation, not because the problem is unimportant or the general approach lacks novelty.

paper_title: Control Reinforcement Learning: Interpretable Token-Level Steering of LLMs via Sparse Autoencoder Features

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The main rejection reason is weak experiment evaluation: gains are modest, baselines are missing (no comparison to simple static/greedy heuristics), and statistical robustness is lacking (no confidence intervals, single-seed runs).

main_rejection_cause.reason: No proper experimental baselines exist. Results are not compared against simple static/greedy heuristics (e.g., top-k SAE features by activation), logit-space steering, or format-sanitizers. Also missing confidence intervals, multiple-seed runs, and bootstrap tests for stability of gains.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Missing ablation studies comparing CRL's PPO-based selection against cheap alternatives like always adding top-k features. The claim that CRL improves reasoning/knowledge rather than format adherence is weakened by the substantial portion of MMLU gains coming from eliminating invalid outputs.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of weak experiment evaluation with missing baselines and insufficient statistical robustness, not because the idea of learning to steer with SAE features lacks merit.

paper_title: TAH-QUANT: Effective Activation Quantization in Pipeline Parallelism over Slow Network

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The main rejection reason is limited experiment scale: evaluations are restricted to RTX 3090 GPUs, only 8 GPUs total, and models up to 3B (with 8B only in rebuttal), insufficient to justify claims about democratizing LLM training.

main_rejection_cause.reason: Experiments are limited to GPT-2XL (1.5B) and Qwen2.5-3B (3B) models, with 8 billion tokens maximum training. This is far below the scale expected for democratizing large-scale LLM training. The comparison with AQ-SGD lacks zero-shot evaluations, and backward pass uses naive quantization without justification or comparison.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: The setup (RTX 3090, 8 GPUs) is underpowered compared to cited works using A100/V100/H100 and 8-32 nodes. Without experiments on larger models or more participants, it's unclear how TAH-QUANT would perform in realistic decentralized training scenarios.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of limited experiment scale with small models and underpowered hardware setup that cannot justify claims about democratizing LLM training, not because the theoretical contributions or method design lack merit.

paper_title: Efficient AllReduce with Stragglers

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The main rejection reason is weak experiment scale: experiments only go up to 3B parameters on 8 GPUs, and 7B experiments were not provided despite being fine-tunable on the same hardware, raising concerns about performance consistency.

main_rejection_cause.reason: Experiments are limited to 3B models on 8 GPUs without 7B experiments despite 7B being fine-tunable on the same 8x80GB GPU testbed. The omission creates concern that 7B results may have been withheld because they were inconsistent with the 3B model performance.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: StragglAR benefits only when straggler delay is 6-8ms or more, but the max delay in realistic environments (e.g., Perlmutter) is around 8ms, leaving minimal room for speedup. The single-straggler assumption is brittle in real-world clusters where stragglers often appear in groups.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of missing 7B experiments that could be run on available hardware and concerns about real-world applicability given the narrow parameter regime for speedup benefits, not because the algorithmic design is fundamentally flawed.

paper_title: How to Teach Large Multimodal Models New Skills

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The main rejection reason is insufficient experiment completeness: missing comparisons with recent state-of-the-art continual learning methods, and conclusions may be biased by vision-language-only setting with limited benchmark diversity.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The paper lacks direct comparisons with recent state-of-the-art continual learning methods published in the last two years. Only traditional methods (LoRA, WiSE-FT, MoE) are compared, making it unclear how competitive the proposed approach is against current baselines.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: The fundamental rationale for selecting specific parameter subsets (attention projection, MLP gate and up layers) lacks theoretical justification. The approach may be largely empirical and engineering-driven without clear scientific guidance on when and why these parameter subsets should be selected.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of insufficient comparisons with recent state-of-the-art continual learning methods and lack of theoretical justification for parameter selection strategy, not because the empirical findings about fine-tuning attention/MLP layers are uninteresting.

paper_title: Reasoning to Regulate: Chain-of-Thought for Traffic Rule Understanding

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Limited novelty and questionable motivation - CoT reasoning is standard for reasoning LLMs, and the paper lacks baseline comparisons to justify the VLM-based approach over simpler alternatives like OCR-then-LLM for traffic sign understanding

main_rejection_cause.reason: The paper's core contribution involves applying Chain-of-Thought reasoning to traffic sign understanding, but CoT is a standard operation for reasoning LLMs. The novelty is limited to the specific pipeline design for the MapDR task, making the contribution incremental rather than fundamental.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Missing key baseline comparisons - reviewers noted absence of simple geometry-only lane nearest to sign baseline and sign text only baseline. The paper also lacks reporting on CoT filtering recall and noise rate, and training configuration details for reproducibility.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of limited novelty with Chain-of-Thought being standard for reasoning LLMs and questionable motivation for VLM-based approach, not because of poor experimental execution.

paper_title: Source Knowledge Anchored Regularization for Unsupervised Domain Adaptation

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Severe lack of novelty - the paper is primarily a combination of standard objective functions (SHOT, FixMatch, Label-Smooth) without introducing novel conceptual or technical contributions, and contains an illusory citation

main_rejection_cause.reason: The primary objective function is a straightforward combination of established methods: SHOT (source hypothesis transfer), FixMatch, and Label Smoothing. All three loss terms are routine in the literature with only minimal novelty in their combination.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Performance gains are marginal (0.6% on VisDA, 0.2% on Office-31) and not statistically significant. The benchmarks used (Office-31, VisDA) are considered saturated and outdated for 2026, failing to provide meaningful insights for the research community.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because it lacks novelty by simply combining existing techniques without new algorithmic contributions, not because of experimental soundness issues.

paper_title: T-VecTTS: Adding time-varying-emotion control to flow-matching-based TTS

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Limited conceptual novelty as an incremental extension of EmoCtrl-TTS - while the paper presents a practical engineering solution for time-varying emotion control on flow-matching TTS, the core ideas of where/when to inject control and scheduling are incremental and tied specifically to F5-TTS architecture

main_rejection_cause.reason: The proposed techniques are incremental over EmoCtrl-TTS - main innovations involve where (which transformer blocks) and when (emotion-specific flow-step interval) to inject emotion control via zero-convolution conditioning branch, which feels limited in transferability beyond F5-TTS and flow-matching paradigm.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: No clear secondary rejection cause is supported by the reviews.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because the core ideas of selective block conditioning and flow-step scheduling are incremental extensions of EmoCtrl-TTS with limited transferability to other TTS architectures, not because of experimental deficiencies.

paper_title: AutoPBO: LLM-powered Optimization for Local Search PBO Solvers

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Multiple fatal flaws including lack of source code and reproducibility details, confusing organization that obscures the relationship between AutoPBO and StructPBO, and limited technical novelty as the multi-agent framework follows established LLM interaction patterns

main_rejection_cause.reason: Confusing organization obscures the relationship between AutoPBO (the optimized result) and StructPBO (the baseline), with StructPBO mentioned before its introduction in Section 3.4. Many algorithmic details are missing including undefined terms in Algorithm 1 and unclear feedback loop formalization.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: No source code released, missing optimization cost analysis, incomplete appendix references, and hardware configuration issues (DeepSeek-R1 on CPU-only system raises feasibility questions). The LLM call counts, latency, and total wall-clock time are not reported.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of confusing organization with unclear AutoPBO/StructPBO relationship and missing reproducibility details including no released code, not because performance was insufficient.

paper_title: Resource-Efficient Model-Free Reinforcement Learning for Board Games

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Misleading narrative claiming model-free KLENT as a simple alternative to AlphaZero when the actual contribution requires test-time MCTS search to outperform AlphaZero with search, making the simplicity claim invalid

main_rejection_cause.reason: The paper's central claim that KLENT is a simpler model-free alternative to AlphaZero is misleading and scientifically incorrect. KLENT without search does not have competitive performance with AlphaZero, while KLENT with search outperforms AlphaZero but requires implementing MCTS, defeating the simplicity argument.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: No clear secondary rejection cause is supported by the reviews.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of its misleading narrative claiming model-free simplicity when the actual contribution requires test-time MCTS search, not because of lack of algorithmic innovation.

paper_title: On Uniformly Scaling Flows: A Density-Aligned Approach to Deep One-Class Classification

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Limited experimental validation and insufficient novelty; the paper lacks comparisons with non-flow baselines and only evaluates on image anomaly detection datasets.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The paper only evaluates on MVTec AD and VisA, both industrial image anomaly detection datasets, and lacks comparison with non-flow one-class or reconstruction baselines. The VAE-USF section is also under-evaluated with limited settings and ablations.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Constant-Jacobian/volume-preserving flows have long existed in the literature (NICE, FlowSVDD, OneFlow) and have already been applied to anomaly detection to avoid SVDD-style collapse. The primary novelty is the formal SVDD-USF MLE equivalence and controlled ablations, not the core idea of using constant-determinant flows.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because its experimental scope is limited to image anomaly detection datasets without comparison to non-flow methods, not because the theoretical contribution lacks value.

paper_title: Reasoning-Enhanced Large Language Models for Molecular Property Prediction

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Redundant multimodal design without ablation proving image utility, dataset quality concerns without expert validation, and unclear reward definitions affecting reproducibility.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The paper lacks clear justification for using 2D molecular images when SMILES already encodes the same structural information, and does not provide ablations demonstrating the visual modality's contribution. Additionally, reward definitions are not clearly specified.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Dataset correctness relies entirely on teacher models without expert annotations or validation. The reasoning dataset is not provided for evaluation, and no statistical tests are reported to assess significance of results.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because the multimodal design is unjustified and dataset quality is unverified without expert validation, not because the two-stage training pipeline is fundamentally flawed.

paper_title: Poisoning the Inner Prediction Logic of Graph Neural Networks for Clean-Label Backdoor Attacks

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Incremental contribution over prior clean-label graph backdoor attacks and insufficient positioning of novel components relative to existing methods.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The work builds incrementally on established ideas in trigger design and poisoned node selection. The paper did not clearly differentiate BA-LOGIC's logic-poisoning approach from standard clean-label backdoor attacks on graph models or position its components relative to prior methods like UGBA-C, ERBA, and ECGBA.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: No clear secondary rejection cause is supported by the reviews.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because its novelty over prior clean-label graph backdoor attacks is insufficient, not because the empirical validation is weak.

paper_title: Dummy Consistent Path Method for Robust Attribution with Irrelevant Features

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Confusion between category-1 and category-2 features in axiom treatment, questionable experimental results with large variance, and lack of clarity in motivation and formulation.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The paper confuses category-1 features (irrelevant to true label) with category-2 features (no effect on model categorization), leading to incorrect claims about dummy consistency violations. The axiom treatment does not properly distinguish whether an attribution method should satisfy dummy consistency based on feature irrelevance to the model vs. to the ground truth.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Table 1 shows DiffID results with standard deviations much larger than means (e.g., 0.978 ± 6.41), severely affecting interpretability. No sufficient statistical analysis supports the claims about enforcing dummy consistency through the proposed optimization.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because its axiom treatment is fundamentally flawed regarding the distinction between feature types, not because the path-based attribution idea lacks potential.

paper_title: Time Series Forecasting as Reasoning: A Slow-Thinking Approach with Reinforced LLMs

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Limited novelty over existing RFT-based CoT methods, insufficient reward design justification, and missing comparisons with time series foundation models and classical baselines.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The framework relies on the same CoT and RFT mechanisms as prior work (o1, DeepSeek-R1). The primary difference is the task-specific reward design for forecasting, making GRIP a modest variant of GRPO. The paper does not clearly articulate what is fundamentally new beyond applying existing slow-thinking paradigms to time series.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: The paper lacks comparisons with Time Series Foundation Models (TimesFM, Moirai, Moment) and classical statistical baselines (ARIMA, ETS). Additionally, evaluation is conducted on a single LLM backbone, and the reasoning evaluation metric is unclear as it may only measure numerical accuracy rather than actual reasoning quality.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because its novelty relative to existing RFT-based CoT methods is limited and its reward design is insufficiently justified, not because the slow-thinking paradigm for time series is unpromising.

paper_title: A Novel Query-Driven Multi-Stage Alternating Feature Extraction and Interaction Network for Image Manipulation Localization

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The method lacks novelty as it is primarily a refinement of the dual-branch + fusion paradigm, and the paper fails to explain why the complex early fusion mechanism helps for image tampering detection. The writing quality does not meet conference standards.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The approach is fundamentally a refinement of the dual-branch + fusion paradigm. The 'alternating' schedule does not constitute a paradigm shift, and the query-based decoding has been used in other domains (e.g., DETR, Visual Prompt Tuning, Mask2Former). Heavy reuse of ideas such as multi-scale or multi-modal feature extraction and fusion in existing literature weakens the novelty claim.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: The manuscript contains many places where it does not meet mature academic writing standards. Figure 1 is not self-contained (term 'HF' in 'OursHF' is undefined), and there are many similar instances throughout the paper. Additionally, critical design choices rely on empirical settings without quantitative analysis.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because the method lacks novelty as a refinement of existing dual-branch + fusion approaches and fails to motivate why the complex early fusion mechanism helps for tampering detection, not because the experiments are fundamentally flawed.

paper_title: Procedural Pretraining: Warming Up Language Models with Abstract Data

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The paper conflates task-specific training with pretraining. Different downstream tasks are associated with different model sizes, architectures, and configurations, which contradicts the standard definition of pretraining as producing a single general-purpose model transferable across tasks.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The paper does not align with the widely accepted definition of pretraining. The authors train separate models for different downstream tasks using task-specific procedural data and different model architectures (varying layers, attention heads, hidden dimensions, and vocabulary sizes). This is task-specific training, not pretraining. The claimed procedural pretraining cannot be fairly compared to standard pretraining paradigms.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: No clear secondary rejection cause is supported by the reviews.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because the methodology does not align with the standard definition of pretraining, as it uses task-specific model architectures and training procedures rather than producing a single general-purpose pretrained model transferable across tasks.

paper_title: Geometry & Optimization of Three-Layer Networks: Symmetry Breaking as a Unifying Principle

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The paper has fundamental theoretical issues including confusion between symmetry-induced degeneracies and optimization-relevant slow modes, and contradictions regarding flat minima claims. Additionally, the authors indicated they plan to resubmit.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The paper confuses symmetry-induced degeneracies (unimportant near-zero eigenvalues) with optimization-relevant slow modes (small but crucial eigenvalues). The claim that 'optimization happens in outlier subspaces' is backwards: gradient descent struggles with flat directions, not steep ones. Additionally, the paper shows flat minima have smaller maximum eigenvalues but claims large eigenvalues are important for optimization, creating an unresolved contradiction.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: The analysis requires exact or near-exact symmetries in the joint structure of loss, architecture, and data. The method breaks down when there are no symmetries. The restriction to three-layer fully-connected networks with specific synthetic targets (Gaussian inputs, identity-matrix teacher) makes it unclear how much insight transfers to practical deep learning.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of fundamental theoretical flaws including confusion between symmetry zero modes and optimization-relevant slow modes, and contradictions between optimization and generalization claims, not because the experiments are poorly conducted.

paper_title: Fixation-Driven Time-Aware 3D Human Motion Forecasting in Indoor Scenes

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The paper's core assumptions about fixation are fundamentally flawed according to vision science and psychophysics. The fixation definition based on proximity to target objects is arbitrary, and the assumption that gaze consistently remains fixed on a single target is unlikely to hold in practice.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The paper redefines fixation based on proximity to target objects (within 0.3m), which is arbitrary. Vision science defines fixation based on gaze velocity, not object proximity. This design biases the model toward localizing objects rather than identifying true fixations. Additionally, the assumption of a single, stable gaze target contradicts prior studies showing complex fixation patterns even during single-object interactions.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: The fixation labels for GIMO dataset require ground-truth object-of-interest locations, providing very strong supervision that may leak target location information. Performance gains on GTA-IM (using velocity-based thresholds) are less significant than on GIMO, questioning the method's generalizability.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because the core fixation definition based on object proximity is fundamentally at odds with established vision science, and the single-target assumption contradicts human gaze behavior research, not primarily because of engineering or experimental design issues.

paper_title: Training-Free Adaptive Frame Selection for Video-Language Understanding

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The paper's contribution is primarily engineering-level with limited methodological novelty. The main signals (text-frame relevance via embedding similarity and frame-frame similarity) are not new, and several reviewers questioned the fairness of comparisons against end-to-end trained systems.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The contribution is mainly engineering-level, lacking deeper methodological insight or theoretical advancement. Query-aware frame selection for Video-LLM has been explored in prior works (KeyVideoLLM, AKS, Q-Frame). The paper did not clearly explain how the method mitigates temporal information loss when modeling long videos despite claiming this motivation.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Reviewers questioned whether comparisons with training-based methods are fair. The method involves intermediate steps and introduces computational overhead but comparisons do not account for this. Questions remain about whether performance gains come from frame selection or adjusting token-per-frame settings. Lack of systematic evaluation of latency and computing consumption undermines the 'lightweight' claim.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because the contribution is primarily engineering-driven with limited methodological novelty since the frame selection signals are not new, not because the experiments lack comprehensiveness.

paper_title: EffSelect: Efficient Feature Value Selection for Deep Recommender Systems with Mini-Batch Training

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Experiment issues: narrow baseline selection (missing LPFS, MultiFS), base model selection questioned (MaskNet vs DeepFM), and concerns about experimental setup that were not fully resolved despite rebuttal.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The paper's baseline comparisons are narrow, missing important recent methods like LPFS and MultiFS. The base model selection (MaskNet instead of the more standard DeepFM used in prior feature selection work) was questioned but not adequately addressed in rebuttal.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: No clear secondary rejection cause is supported by the reviews.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of experiment issues (baseline selection and base model choice), not because of method problems.

paper_title: The Dual Power of Interpretable Token Embeddings: Jailbreaking Attacks and Defenses for Diffusion Model Unlearning

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Method novelty concerns: SubAttack and SubDefense essentially represent a linear orthogonal transformation, which reviewers found incremental rather than foundational; weak motivation for why interpretability matters in attacking unlearning models.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The attack and defense strategy essentially represents a linear orthogonal transformation. The remaining concern is that interpretability in attacking unlearned models does not advance the frontier of robustness since defense against interpretable attacks tends to be weak.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Missing comparison with strong non-linear defenses like AdvUnlearn, Receler, and STEREO. SubDefense fails to defend against its linear complement SubAttack on ESD dataset.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of method novelty issues (linear framework limits advancement), not primarily because of experiment issues.

paper_title: Verifying GNNs with Readout is Intractable

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Experiment issues: experiments are largely irrelevant to the theory and central claims. The paper provides only quantization effects on accuracy/size rather than actual verification performance, failing to support the theoretical contribution.

main_rejection_cause.reason: Experiments only test quantization effects on model accuracy and size, not actual verification performance. This setup is largely irrelevant to the theoretical results showing NEXPTIME-completeness of ACR-GNN verification.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: While significance is limited, this is more a consequence of the theoretical result being intractable rather than a distinct rejection cause.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of experiment issues (experiments tangential to theory), not because of method problems.

paper_title: Adaptive Preconditioners Trigger Loss Spikes in Adam

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Method novelty concerns: the core stability condition (η ≤ 2/λ_max(H_t)) is well-known from optimization theory; the paper provides new framing rather than fundamentally new mathematics. Also concerns about constant Hessian assumptions for non-convex deep networks.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The core stability condition is well-known from optimization and prior Adam/edge-of-stability analyses. The contribution appears incremental rather than foundational, providing new framing rather than fundamentally new mathematics. Also, constant Hessian assumptions are problematic for non-convex deep learning scenarios.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: The theoretical framework relies on strong and often unrealistic assumptions of a constant and positive-definite Hessian throughout the analysis, limiting generalizability to practical DNN training.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of method novelty issues (incremental contribution, problematic assumptions), not because of experiment problems.

paper_title: SpatialComposer: 3D Spatial Object Insertion via Image Gaussian Composition

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Method novelty concerns: SpatialComposer is primarily an engineering integration of existing components (Gaussian Splatting and pre-trained diffusion models) rather than introducing a substantive algorithmic contribution. The 'train-free' refinement critically depends on strong base models and inherits their limitations.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The method is primarily an engineering decision within existing frameworks. The refinement step uses existing models (FLUX-Fill-dev, LBM) without novel algorithmic contribution.
