secondary_rejection_cause.reason: The paper fails to adequately engage with existing literature on learning rate scaling for ResNets and CNNs (e.g., Feature Speed Formula by Chizat and Netrapalli, Tensor Programs series by Yang et al.). Additionally, the paper doesn't consider residual branch scaling known to be necessary for ResNets, questioning the validity of the derived learning rate scaling for this architecture.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of severe clarity issues making technical assessment impossible and limited novelty (incremental extension of MLP results), not because the experiments were poorly designed.

paper_title: Contrastive Conditional–Unconditional Alignment for Long-tailed Diffusion Model

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The paper proposes CCUA to improve diffusion models on long-tailed datasets. While the method shows empirical improvements, major concerns remain unresolved: high training cost (1.3x slower even after optimization), lack of theoretical grounding, unclear rationale for hyperparameter settings, insufficient justification for latent space selection, and limited performance analysis. Authors failed to fully assuage these concerns despite rebuttal.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The method requires 1.3x more training time even after optimization and demands more GPU memory. The high computational cost was raised by multiple reviewers (KAa1, yVZe, 2xLz) and despite the rebuttal's improved implementation, the concern remains unresolved.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: The paper lacks theoretical grounding for why the specific combination of UCL and AL is optimal. Reviewer yVZe noted insufficient justification and no deep mathematical analysis. The claim that L_al 'implicitly extends' UCL to conditional training is not sufficiently explained, and the theoretical analysis in Sec A.5 was considered too short and not thorough enough.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of high training cost (1.3x slowdown) and lack of theoretical justification, not because the empirical results were weak.

paper_title: rePIRL: Learn PRM with Inverse RL for LLM Reasoning

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The paper proposes rePIRL, an IRL-based method for learning process reward models. Major weakness identified by multiple reviewers is the lack of technical novelty compared to existing work (especially 'Getting More Juice Out of the SFT Data' from NeurIPS 2024). Reviewer TGya specifically questioned whether the theoretical results are genuinely novel or simply repackaged from existing literature (SAC, Infinite Time Horizon Maximum Causal Entropy IRL). Despite rebuttal, the technical similarity concern was not fully resolved.

main_rejection_cause.reason: Multiple reviewers (wZzT, TGya) identified that the method is too similar to existing work, particularly 'Getting More Juice Out of the SFT Data' (NeurIPS 2024). Reviewer TGya further noted that the theoretical results (Theorem 1, propositions) appear to be direct copies from existing literature (Soft Actor-Critic, Infinite Time Horizon Maximum Causal Entropy IRL) without proper attribution, giving a misleading impression of theoretical contribution.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Reviewer TGya identified a problematic definition of p(o_t|s_t,a_t) - it only depends on current reward r(s_t,a_t) rather than cumulative reward/Q-value. This makes the energy model 'myopic' and questionable for sequential decision-making problems. The concern was raised in post-rebuttal discussion but not adequately addressed.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of insufficient technical novelty compared to existing work and questionable attribution of theoretical contributions, not because of poor experimental evaluation.

paper_title: MeasureNet: Polyline Detection Based Measurement for Celiac Disease Identification and Grading

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: This paper proposes MeasureNet for villi/crypt detection in medical images. Major concerns include incremental methodological contribution (combining existing components), unclear rationale for component choices, potential unfair comparisons (using DINO-DETR pretrained backbone while baselines don't), and multiple presentation issues. The method is built from established components (SegFormer, DINO, inverted residual blocks) with limited novel technical contribution.

main_rejection_cause.reason: Reviewer TYqi and S26Q both identified that the methodological contribution is incremental. The proposed MeasureNet architecture is assembled from established components (SegFormer, DINO, inverted residual blocks from MobileNetV2) with various loss adaptations. Reviewer S26Q noted the combination of strong/weak segmentors and mixup strategy is conceptually similar to data augmentation.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: The comparisons may be unfair - MeasureNet uses DINO-DETR as a powerful pretrained backbone while competing baselines in Tables 1 and 2 do not seem to use such pretrained backbones. Reviewer S26Q raised concerns that performance gains may stem mainly from the backbone, not the proposed method.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of incremental methodological contribution (combining existing components without clear justification for choices), not because the experiments were incomplete.

paper_title: T2G-Reasoner: Deep Reasoning for Text-to-Gloss Translation

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Limited novelty and weak experimental validation; the method is essentially a direct application of GRPO to T2G translation without fundamental innovation, and performance is sub-SOTA with missing ablation studies.

main_rejection_cause.reason: Core novelty is limited; the method is essentially LLM + SFT on synthetic alignments + GRPO, a direct transplantation of existing techniques to T2G without fundamental technical departure from applying GRPO to any structured prediction task.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Missing ablation studies (e.g., applying GRPO to CV-SLT, C2RL baselines) and evaluation on gloss-free benchmarks like OpenASL; sub-SOTA performance (29.05 vs CV-SLT 29.27) suggests weak validation.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of limited novelty and weak experimental validation, not because the approach is fundamentally unsound.

paper_title: Two-Stage Voting for Robust and Efficient Suicide Risk Detection on Social Media

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Critical experiment issues: DeepSuiMind contains only positive cases violating binary classification principles, misleading high metrics (99.7% F1), and missing strong baselines like RoBERTa and DeBERTa.

main_rejection_cause.reason: DeepSuiMind dataset contains only suicidal posts (all positive class), violating basic binary classification principles and inflating performance metrics; no statistical significance analysis provided; cited paper incorrectly claims BERT as SOTA when RoBERTa performs better.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Missing strong baselines such as RoBERTa, DeBERTa, and recent suicide-specific models (e.g., PsyGuard); narrow baseline selection undermines novelty claims.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of critical experiment soundness issues (flawed dataset construction), not because the two-stage design concept lacks merit.

paper_title: Diffusion Posterior Sampling for Nonlinear Contextual Bandits

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Theoretical results are mostly sanity checks under ideal settings; practical algorithms rely on heavy approximations not covered by theory; regret bounds are loose and pessimistic with large gap between theory and practice.

main_rejection_cause.reason: Theoretical results are mostly sanity checks or loose bounds under ideal assumptions; practical algorithms rely on heavy approximations not covered by theory; regret bounds are pessimistic (implying linear regret under prior misspecification) with large gap between theory and practice.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Extension of prior work on diffusion-based Thompson sampling for GLM bandits to nonlinear rewards without clear differentiation; diffusion prior is treated as a plug-in and could be replaced by other generative oracles.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of weak theoretical foundations and limited novelty, not because the empirical results are poor.

paper_title: ArchPilot: A Proxy-Guided Multi-Agent Approach for Machine Learning Engineering

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Primarily combines existing components with incremental adjustments; agentic framing is misleading as there is no genuine action space or decision-making beyond tool invocation; weak experimental validation with missing ablation studies.

main_rejection_cause.reason: Primary novelty is combining existing components (MCTS/UCT, proxy training, ridge-fitting, LLM-based code generation, restart) with incremental adjustments; the agentic framing is misleading as there is no genuine action space or autonomous decision-making beyond tool invocation.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: No ablation studies for core designs (restart, proxy reweighting, multi-agent structure); missing classical NAS method comparisons (e.g., DARTS); only two baselines compared on single benchmark; only one LLM backbone tested.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of insufficient novelty and weak experimental validation, not because the overall approach is unpromising.

paper_title: Deliberation Meets Reaction: A Dual-Expert VLA framework for Autonomous Driving

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Inference latency remains prohibitively high (~543ms) for practical on-vehicle deployment; the fundamental performance-efficiency trade-off has not been thoroughly resolved; no real-world dataset validation raises generalization concerns.

main_rejection_cause.reason: Inference latency remains prohibitively high (~543ms even in simplest scenarios) for practical on-vehicle deployment; the fundamental trade-off between performance and efficiency has not been thoroughly resolved despite claims of efficiency improvement.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Missing comparison to efficiency-focused VLA baselines (e.g., FastDriveVLA, DriveMoE); no real-world dataset validation, only CARLA simulator; comfort score remains significantly lower than SOTA (17.61 vs 33.67) without systematic solution.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of feasibility concerns regarding practical deployment latency, not because the dual-expert design concept lacks merit.

paper_title: DevBench: A Realistic, Developer-Informed Benchmark for Code Generation Models

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The benchmark suffers from ceiling effects (84-90% Pass@1 for frontier models), insufficient challenge to differentiate state-of-the-art models, and lacks rigorous validation of the telemetry-driven data curation process.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The benchmark shows ceiling effects with 84-90% Pass@1 for frontier models, undermining its ability to differentiate state-of-the-art models. Additionally, LLM-judge evaluation lacks quantitative correlation with human ratings, inter-annotator agreement statistics, and clear failure analysis.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: The telemetry-to-benchmark distillation process is opaque and unreproducible, with vague sampling methodology from 1 billion interactions to 1,800 instances. Generator-induced bias from GPT-4o synthesis is not empirically excluded, and category taxonomy lacks orthogonality validation.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of ceiling effects in the benchmark that prevent discrimination between state-of-the-art models and insufficient validation of LLM-judge reliability and data curation methodology, not because the underlying motivation for a telemetry-driven benchmark is weak.

paper_title: Perturbed Flow Matching for Structure-Based Drug Design

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The method's intuition and theoretical justification for the perturbation term are unclear, and the paper lacks fair comparisons due to inconsistent application of guidance settings and missing important flow-matching baselines.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The paper is difficult to understand with unclear intuitive motivation for the perturbed conditional probability path. The theoretical justification for the perturbation term is missing, and the connection to self-conditioning (an established concept) is not properly articulated.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: The 21x speedup claim is confounded by different sampling hyperparameters (NFE=100 vs NFE=1000), not attributable to the model architecture alone. Fair comparisons are also undermined by reporting PFM with cfg/cg guidance while baselines lack these settings.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of unclear method explanation and weak theoretical justification for the perturbation approach, not because the overall direction of improving flow matching for drug design is unpromising.

paper_title: FlatLand: Personalized Graph Federated Learning via Tailored Lorentz Space

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The use of Lorentz transformations is only valid in flat Minkowski space but the paper applies them in curved Lorentzian space where global Lorentz transformations are not generally valid, questioning the theoretical soundness of the approach.

main_rejection_cause.reason: Lorentz transformations used in the fully Lorentz neural networks are only valid in flat Minkowski space, but the paper applies them in curved anti-de Sitter space where global Lorentz transformations are not generally valid. Lemma 8 and the correctness arguments in Section 5 are affected by this issue.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: The motivation for using Lorentzian space (with time-like dimension) over hyperbolic Riemannian space is not clearly justified. Physical interpretations like light-cones and causality are not explained, and the claim that time-like dimension captures heterogeneity is questioned given mutual information is coordinate-invariant.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of theoretical soundness issues with Lorentz transformations in curved spaces, not because the experimental results are weak or the problem motivation is flawed.

paper_title: LiveOIBench: Can Large Language Models Outperform Human Contestants in Informatics Olympiads?

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The benchmark's contamination mitigation is insufficient (no mechanism beyond post-2022 cutoff), and claims about being a 'live' benchmark and having 'private' test cases are not supported by the submitted draft.

main_rejection_cause.reason: Contamination mitigation relies only on 'post-2022' cutoff which is insufficient given training data can include these problems. The benchmark lacks decontamination pipelines or canaries found in prior work. No mechanism actually demonstrates the 'live' update capability in the submitted draft.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: The paper overclaims features (private test cases, live updates) that are not supported by the submission. Test cases are simply scraped competition materials, not privately designed, and the live update mechanisms (dynamic task injection, user feedback-driven iteration) are not implemented in the submitted draft.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of insufficient contamination mitigation and unsupported claims about being a live benchmark with private test cases, not because the dataset construction or evaluation methodology is fundamentally flawed.

paper_title: SAKE: Towards Editing Auditory Attribute Knowledge of Large Audio-Language Models

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The benchmark's scope is limited (only 2 LALMs, 4 attributes) and does not fully realize the 'continuous/abstract' auditory attribute motivation stated in the paper, as evaluation uses discrete labels.

main_rejection_cause.reason: Only 2 LALMs and 4 attributes are evaluated, which is insufficient for a benchmark paper positioning. The 'continuous/abstract' motivation in the paper's premise is not fully delivered, as evaluation largely uses discrete classification labels rather than truly continuous attributes like pitch or prosody.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Several SOTA knowledge editing methods (WISE, AlphaEdit, UltraEdit) are missing from the evaluation. The mechanistic analysis of why methods like IKE fail is shallow, lacking deeper investigation into whether the LALM fails to process in-context audio or apply textual instructions.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of limited scope (2 LALMs, 4 attributes) and incomplete realization of the continuous/abstract auditory attribute motivation, not because the benchmark design or problem framing is fundamentally weak.

paper_title: Domain Generalizable Person Re-identification via Adversarial Dual-Stream Strategy with Local Consistency

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The paper's core contribution narrative (emphasizing CILL) is inconsistent with experimental evidence showing DAPS is the primary performance driver. Additionally, the method has limited novelty as it combines existing techniques (adversarial training, memory-bank clustering, local features) in an incremental way.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The paper claims CILL is a core contribution but ablation studies show DAPS provides the vast majority of performance boost (M→D R1: 66.3%→67.7% for CILL vs 66.3%→70.3% for DAPS). The narrative does not match the experimental evidence, undermining the paper's core claim.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: The method is an incremental combination of existing techniques (adversarial training, memory-bank clustering, local part-based features) commonly used in DG Re-ID, with no clear algorithmic innovation beyond component integration.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because its core contribution narrative is inconsistent with experimental evidence and novelty is limited, not because the experiments lack completeness or the significance of the problem is low.

paper_title: Evaluating the Logical Reasoning Abilities of Large Reasoning Models

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The benchmark lacks novelty compared to existing logical reasoning evaluation benchmarks (e.g., JustLogic, LogicGame, MME-Reasoning) and evaluates only outdated LLMs, with concerns about potential data leakage.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The paper collects existing exam questions and evaluates LLMs, which is very similar to prior work (JustLogic, LogicGame, MME-Reasoning). The community already has many logical reasoning benchmarks, making the incremental contribution unclear.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: The evaluation uses outdated LLMs (DeepSeek-R1, Gemini 2.0) while newer versions (DeepSeek 3.2, Gemini 2.5) exist, and benchmarks may be saturated as models achieve 75%+ accuracy.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because it lacks novelty compared to existing benchmarks and evaluates outdated models, not because the evaluation framework is poorly designed or the experimental setup is unsound.

paper_title: Understanding the role of depth in the neural tangent kernel for overparameterized neural networks.

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The paper has insufficient experimental validation (only small-scale synthetic datasets with depth up to 10-30) and unclear novelty compared to prior work (Xiao et al. 2020) that addresses the same infinite-depth NTK limit problem.

main_rejection_cause.reason: Experiments only cover depth up to 10-30 with synthetic uniformly distributed data on a sphere, which is insufficient to demonstrate the 'extremely slow' convergence claim or quantify practical relevance for modern deep architectures.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: The main result (well-defined limit of mean predictor in ordered phase) appeared in Xiao et al. 2020), and the paper does not clearly improve upon or distinguish from prior work on the n→∞ then L→∞ regime.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because experiments are too limited to support theoretical claims and novelty is unclear relative to existing work, not because the theoretical analysis is fundamentally flawed or the problem is insignificant.

paper_title: A Benchmark and Pair-Level 4PL-IRT Framework for Reliable Evaluation of LLM Reasoning

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The paper submission is incomplete with large sections missing, making the proposed IRT-based evaluation framework and experiments unassessable.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The manuscript is incomplete with substantial sections missing, rendering the methodology, experiments, and contributions unassessable. Multiple reviewers noted missing paragraphs across many sections.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: No clear secondary rejection cause is supported by the reviews due to the incomplete submission preventing proper evaluation.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was rejected because the submission is incomplete with missing sections preventing assessment, not because the IRT-based evaluation concept (noted as promising by one reviewer) is fundamentally flawed.

paper_title: On Dataset Distillation with Two-fold Pseudo-Distribution Matching

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The paper has incremental novelty (PTM and PLM build heavily on existing work like DANCE and pseudo-labeling) and limited theoretical justification for the 'matching capacity' concept, with incomplete experimental analysis.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The two main components (PTM and PLM) are heavily inspired by or extensions of existing work: PTM is similar to DANCE and progressive training approaches, while PLM applies standard knowledge distillation with label smoothing. The combination is sensible but not particularly innovative.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: The 'matching capacity' concept lacks formal analysis or theoretical grounding. The fixed threshold α=50 is not justified and may depend on dataset size/class count without principled guidance for selection.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because novelty is incremental over existing methods (DANCE, pseudo-labeling) and theoretical justification is lacking, not because the experimental results are poor or the problem significance is low.

paper_title: Enhancing structural consistency of 3D Human Pose Estimation through Trainable Loss Function

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The paper was rejected primarily due to limited novelty beyond SEAL-pose, with reviewers concluding that the contribution represents incremental engineering rather than ground-breaking innovation. Training stability concerns and lack of cross-dataset generalization analysis further weakened the submission.

main_rejection_cause.reason: Limited novelty beyond SEAL-pose (ICCV 2025 Workshop). The primary modification is replacing the loss-net with a Graph Network to capture skeletal topology, which reviewers characterized as engineering-level innovation rather than conceptual or theoretical advancement. The systematic hyperparameter search protocol was deemed not well justified, reinforcing the impression of engineering rather than novel methodological contribution.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Cross-dataset generalization was not addressed in experiments, and direct comparisons with constraint-based approaches (kinematic tree priors, graphical model based pose estimators like Pose-GCNN) were missing. The temporal pairwise loss results in Table 5 showed only marginal improvement.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because it offers limited methodological novelty beyond prior SEAL work and relies on incremental engineering contributions, not because the experiments lacked rigor or the core idea lacked significance.

paper_title: CCKS: Cooperative CPU-GPU Scheduling for Fused Kernels on Coherent Architectures

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The paper was rejected because it remains unclear how much of the performance improvement stems from CCKS's scheduling algorithms versus the inherent advantages of Grace Hopper's cache-coherent shared-memory architecture. Missing Blackwell evaluation leaves an important generalizability gap.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The approach's applicability is narrow, only useful for fused persistent kernels on specific hardware. The promised Blackwell evaluation was missing from rebuttal, leaving generalizability to newer architectures undemonstrated. Additionally, concerns about whether the claimed improvements truly stem from CCKS or simply Grace Hopper's shared-memory architecture were not fully resolved.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Experiments were limited to Grace Hopper platform with no evaluation on other architectures including Blackwell. The missing hardware validation makes it impossible to determine what portion of the 77% throughput gains comes from CCKS versus the underlying shared-memory paradigm.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because the generalizability of CCKS beyond Grace Hopper architecture was not demonstrated, not because the engineering effort or motivation was inherently flawed.

paper_title: DSPO: Stable and Efficient Policy Optimization for Agentic Search and Reasoning

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The paper was rejected primarily due to incomplete experiments: missing direct comparisons with DAPO and GSPO, evaluation only on Qwen model family, and reliance on older benchmarks that may have data contamination concerns.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The paper does not compare against DAPO and GSPO directly despite building on their ideas. Ablation studies serve as proxies rather than full comparisons with fully-tuned implementations. Evaluation is limited to Qwen model family only, and benchmarks are relatively old with potential pretraining contamination.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: While the synthesis of sequence-level optimization with dynamic filtering is shown to be synergistic, the algorithmic novelty is limited as both components exist in prior work. The paper would benefit from clearer differentiation of its contributions.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of incomplete experimental comparisons and limited model diversity in evaluation, not because the algorithm design or theoretical foundation was fundamentally flawed.

paper_title: Incremental Learning in Transformers for In-Context Associative Recall

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The paper was rejected because while the theoretical contribution is strong, the empirical validation remains insufficient. The gap between the simplified model and realistic transformers is substantial, and quantitative matching between theory and experiments is lacking.

main_rejection_cause.reason: Inadequate empirical validation: experiments are on a tiny recall task with tiny vocab and are mostly qualitative. Missing ablation studies for assumptions (A1-A4), no quantitative matching between theoretical predictions (e.g., plateau duration scaling) and measured values. The gap between the stylized transformer and realistic models is substantial.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Limited quantitative validation of theoretical predictions. SGD/noise effects on dynamics are under-discussed despite being central to the staged-learning story. The analysis assumes deterministic gradient flow while practice uses SGD.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because the empirical validation of theoretical findings was insufficient and the gap to realistic models was not bridged, not because the theoretical contribution lacked merit.

paper_title: Distributional Reinforcement Learning for Large Language Models

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The paper was rejected because despite substantial improvements during rebuttal, the algorithmic novelty remains limited (similar to Mavrin et al. 2019) and the justification for transitioning from value-free methods to actor-critic is insufficient given the 65% computational overhead increase.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The core exploration mechanism (DLTV) is functionally analogous to Mavrin et al. (2019)'s LTV bonus with decaying schedule. Modeling state-value distribution is a common extension of distributional RL. The algorithmic novelty beyond prior work was not adequately justified, making it unclear why this method should be favored over existing approaches.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: The paper claims minimal overhead but shows a 65% increase in training time over DAPO. The justification for reintroducing a critic in a field that has moved toward value-free methods (GRPO, DAPO) for scalability remains insufficient, especially given the significant performance-compute trade-off.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because the algorithmic novelty is limited and the computational cost justification for actor-critic over value-free methods is insufficient, not because the core insight about deterministic LLM environments lacks value.

paper_title: FeatBench: Evaluating Coding Agents on Feature Implementation for Vibe Coding

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Limited novelty and insufficient new insights - FeatBench provides incremental value over existing benchmarks like SWE-Bench, which already contains feature-level evaluation. Additionally, concerns about input realism as LLM-generated prompts may not reflect real-world feature requests.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The paper primarily contributes dataset construction rather than novel technical methods. Reviewers noted that SWE-Bench already contains 18% feature requests and the benchmark lacks sufficient differentiation from existing approaches to provide new insights.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: No clear secondary rejection cause is supported by the reviews.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of limited novelty and insufficient differentiation from existing benchmarks, not because of methodological soundness or experimental execution.

paper_title: CRAG-MM: Multi-modal Multi-turn Comprehensive RAG Benchmark

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Insufficient methodological transparency in dataset creation, confusing evaluation pipeline (RAG vs long-context benchmark), and metric definition inconsistencies that affect the reliability of reported results.

main_rejection_cause.reason: Missing critical details about dataset creation: no annotation instructions, inter-annotator agreement metrics, validation stages, or bias mitigation strategies. Questions are semi-synthesized or fully LLM-generated without sufficient human verification.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Confusion between RAG benchmark vs long-context benchmark evaluation pipeline, and metric definitions (truthfulness, hallucination, incorrect) are inconsistent throughout the paper.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of insufficient methodological transparency in dataset construction and unclear evaluation protocol, not because the underlying benchmark concept lacks significance.

paper_title: HeLutNet: Extremely Fast Privacy-preserving Inference in Milliseconds via LUT-based Machine Learning Models

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Limited scalability demonstrated only on MNIST without CIFAR-10 results, unfair comparisons with prior work using drastically simpler model architectures, and novelty concerns relative to existing LUT-based FHE research.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The complete absence of CIFAR-10 evaluation (standard in FHE literature) represents a fundamental scalability limitation. The ultra-shallow 2-layer models sacrifice representational capacity needed for non-trivial tasks, undermining practical applicability claims.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: LUT operations in FHE have been standard in TFHE/FHEW schemes and prior work exists on LUT-based FHE inference. The paper's contribution is end-to-end LUT network architecture rather than novel LUT techniques.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of fundamental scalability limitations (missing CIFAR-10 results) and unfair comparisons, not because the BGV-based SIMD implementation approach is without merit.

paper_title: FedSumUp:Secure Federated Learning Without Client-Side Training for Resource-Constrained Edge Devices

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Lack of theoretical privacy guarantees, organizational issues impairing comprehension, and heavy reliance on pre-trained VAE with unclear privacy properties when the server has access to the decoder.

main_rejection_cause.reason: No formal privacy analysis or theoretical bounds (e.g., differential privacy guarantees, information-theoretic leakage quantification). Privacy benefits are only empirically validated through MIA accuracy, while the server has access to VAE decoder which could potentially decode latent codes to image-like content.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: The paper centralizes all optimization to the server, increasing computational load that scales with number of clients. This burden is not reported, making efficiency claims one-sided.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of missing theoretical privacy guarantees and unclear protection against server-side attacks with decoder access, not because the core idea of using VAE latent codes for privacy is conceptually flawed.

paper_title: The Reasoning Boundary Paradox: How Reinforcement Learning Constrains Language Models

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Limited novelty since pass@k degradation has been observed before, theoretical analysis errors identified by reviewers in Section 342 regarding gradient analysis and winner-take-all reinforcement.

main_rejection_cause.reason: Reviewer identified errors in the theoretical analysis - the claims about low-likelihood tokens providing less meaningful updates and winner-take-all effects do not follow from the presented equations. The analysis in section line 342 is flawed.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: The paper acknowledges that pass@k degradation has been studied in prior works. The per-step influence analysis, while insightful, builds on existing observations about RLVR limitations.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of flawed theoretical analysis in the gradient/influence section and limited novelty over prior work, not because the proposed SELF mitigation method is conceptually unsound.

paper_title: Probability-based Reward Value Combination Method for Multi-Objective Alignment

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The paper has a fundamental inconsistency between its stated goal (maintaining BT consistency) and the actual formulation in Equation 7, which the reviewers could not resolve. The authors did not submit a rebuttal.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The method claims to maintain Bradley-Terry consistency at the multi-objective level, but Equation 7 does not actually achieve this. Reviewer zcFE identified that p(y1>y2|x) != sum_i w_i * p_i(y1>y2|x) still holds, and this fundamental inconsistency was never resolved as the authors did not provide a rebuttal.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Experiments are limited to two objectives (harmlessness and helpfulness) and medium-scale models (LLaMA-2-7B, Qwen2.5-7B). Missing important baselines such as calibrated z-score/temperature methods, logit-space fusion, and multi-objective scalarizations like Chebyshev or epsilon-constraint.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because its core method has a fundamental inconsistency with the BT formulation it claims to preserve, not because the problem of multi-objective RLHF is unimportant.

paper_title: Memory-Augmented Large Language Model-Based Agent with Cross-Task Experience Learning

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The paper presents incremental improvements over existing memory-augmented agents with marginal gains (2% on WebShop), limited scope to a single benchmark, and lacks comparison to stronger recent baselines.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The proposed cross-task memory is essentially a pre-filled experience buffer, not a fundamentally new paradigm. Prior works like REMEMBERER, Reflexion, and GITM have already explored experience-based reuse. The 'dynamic retrieval' is claimed as benefit over REMEMBERER but is essentially adaptive weighting based on successful trajectories with no learned mechanism.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Evaluation relies exclusively on WebShop benchmark, which shares the same structured API and UI across tasks, undermining cross-domain generalization claims. No comparison to stronger recent baselines like MemGPT, Mem0, Zep, or MIRIX.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because it lacks conceptual novelty over existing memory-augmented agents, not because the problem of improving data efficiency in LLM agents is unimportant.

paper_title: What Shapes a Creative Machine Mind? Comprehensively Benchmarking Creativity in Foundation Models

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The paper's core metrics (Usefulness=correctness, Originality as cluster count, Surprise=1-confidence) are fundamentally flawed as measures of creativity. The LLM-as-judge approach is circular and the framing lacks novelty relative to existing HCI and creativity literature.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The metric definitions are fundamentally flawed: 'Usefulness=correctness' measures capability not creativity; 'Originality' is based on embedding cluster count which is representation-sensitive and measures sampling diversity not creative novelty; 'Surprise=1-confidence' conflates uncertainty with creative surprise. No validation with human experts or inter-annotator agreement provided.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: No clear secondary rejection cause is supported by the reviews.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because its creativity metrics lack construct validity and conflate capability/uncertainty measures with genuine creativity assessment, not because the problem of evaluating LLM creativity is unimportant.

paper_title: Expand Neurons, Not Parameters

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The paper remains at a proof-of-concept level with experiments limited to small MLPs (8-128 neurons) on toy tasks and frozen CLIP embeddings. It lacks related work positioning, clear theoretical grounding, and experiments on realistic architectures.

main_rejection_cause.reason: Experiments are limited to small MLPs (8-128 neurons) on toy Boolean tasks and image classification using frozen CLIP embeddings. Real-world applicability to larger models and end-to-end training is not demonstrated. No comparison to Sparse Autoencoders which are also based on superposition hypothesis.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: The paper lacks discussion on practical integration with modern architectures (Transformers, deeper networks) and does not demonstrate how FPE would interact with other optimization techniques like quantization or knowledge distillation.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because its experimental scope is limited to small toy scenarios and does not demonstrate scalability to practical model sizes, not because the underlying idea of addressing polysemanticity is uninteresting.

paper_title: ReplicationBench: Can AI Agents Replicate Astrophysics Research Papers?

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The paper's core contribution is seen as incremental over existing agent benchmarks like PaperBench and DiscoveryBench. The key finding that agents struggle with long-horizon scientific tasks is not new, and the novelty concerns were not fully resolved in rebuttal.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The paper's primary weakness is insufficient novelty relative to existing benchmarks. Works like PaperBench, DiscoveryBench, and CORE-Bench already evaluate agent capabilities on scientific tasks. The key finding that agents struggle with long-horizon, domain-specific tasks has been repeatedly shown in prior benchmarks.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: The benchmark covers only 19 papers with 107 tasks, leading to large error bars. The paper does not clearly position what unique challenges or new insights the astrophysics domain brings beyond existing benchmarks.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because it does not offer fundamentally new insights beyond existing agent benchmarks, not because the problem of evaluating AI agents on scientific research tasks is unimportant.

paper_title: Generalized Representation for Generalized Dynamics Generation

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Missing key baseline comparisons, insufficient visual results, and inability to demonstrate generalization to unseen scenarios undermines the paper's claims about a unified simulator.

main_rejection_cause.reason: Missing key baseline comparisons (SCD, ArtGS, Gen-3), only synthetic examples without real-world data validation, and insufficient visual demonstrations. The paper claims to be a unified simulator but cannot demonstrate generalization beyond observed training data.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: The method's inability to extrapolate to longer time horizons and generalize to unseen geometries defeats the fundamental premise of a 'unified simulator' framework.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of incomplete experiments (missing key baselines, no real-world validation, insufficient visual results), not because the underlying idea of unifying physics simulation paradigms lacks merit.

paper_title: CodeStructEval: A Holistic Evaluation Framework of Code Structure Generation and Comprehension

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Non-reproducible due to underspecified AST definition and StAR metric, limited scale (157 samples), and lack of comparison with current state-of-the-art LLMs.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The task design is underspecified: no formal AST definition provided, no explanation of the AST parser format used, and the StAR metric is completely underspecified with no algorithm for structural equivalence. The task evaluates LLM familiarity with a specific serialization format rather than general code structure ability.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Benchmark scale is too small (157 samples from Python only) with no multilingual or diverse programming language coverage. Additionally, the benchmark uses outdated models without evaluation of current state-of-the-art LLMs, making it irrelevant for future development.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of poor task design clarity (underspecified AST format and StAR metric making the work non-reproducible), not because evaluating code structure understanding is inherently uninteresting.

paper_title: SAGE: Sufficiency-Aware Implicit Graph Exploration for Long Context Reasoning

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Insufficient experiments (limited baselines, single model family, incomplete ablations) and unresolved contribution focus due to disconnected counting module.

main_rejection_cause.reason: Insufficient experimental validation: limited to only two baselines (MiniRAG, RAPTOR) without comparing against GraphRAG paradigm; experiments confined to LLaMA family with no baseline comparisons across model families; incomplete ablation studies missing iteration rounds analysis and importance score ablation under non-default parameters.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: The paper contains a disconnected 'counting module' that is not related to the main SAGE contribution, and ablation experiments do not reveal the gains from the main module versus this hand-tailored solution for counting problems.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of incomplete experiments (limited baselines, single model family, missing ablations), not because the implicit graph exploration idea lacks merit.

paper_title: UNISE: Unified Noise-Invariant Learning for Speech Enhancement toward Improved Content Preservation

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Weak experimental validation (task design issues on EARS dataset, missing baselines, no human subjective evaluation) and poor reproducibility (missing hyperparameters, model sizes).

main_rejection_cause.reason: UNISE performs worse than unprocessed noisy speech on EARS test set, indicating the method may degrade content preservation in certain conditions. This critical failure case is not explained. Additionally, the trade-off between WER improvement and DNSMOS degradation is not adequately justified.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Reproducibility is poor: missing hyperparameters (codebook size V=2048 justification, Sinkhorn params, temperature), no model size information in tables, and no human subjective evaluation conducted. The paper's claim about enhanced content preservation lacks proper validation.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of weak experimental validation (method fails on EARS dataset, unclear WER vs DNSMOS tradeoff), not because the idea of combining contrastive learning with generative speech enhancement lacks merit.

paper_title: Automated Architecture Synthesis for Arbitrarily Structured Neural Networks

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Fundamental theoretical concerns about backward gradient computation in non-DAG structures and prohibitive computational complexity O(N+E+s·NM²) that doesn't scale to large models.

main_rejection_cause.reason: Backward gradient computation in non-DAG structures is unclear and potentially problematic. Traditional backpropagation relies on layer-wise ordering which is lost in arbitrary cyclic graphs. Theorems 3.1 and 3.2 are oversold (one is trivial universal approximation, another is basic SGD formula). No convergence guarantees provided for gradient stability in cyclic structures.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Prohibitive computational complexity O(N+E+s·NM²) that scales poorly with large graphs. Memory usage is O(p²) for dense adjacency matrix, exhausting 40GB VRAM at p≈70K. The approach is impractical for modern large-scale NNs with billions of parameters.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of fundamental soundness concerns (unclear gradient computation in non-DAG structures, no convergence guarantees) and impractical scalability, not because the idea of moving beyond DAG constraints lacks conceptual novelty.

paper_title: Semantic World Models

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The paper's conceptual framing of world models as semantic predictors is novel, but the experiments lack rigorous validation due to unfair baseline comparisons and limited evaluation scope, preventing the claims from being adequately supported.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The AVD baseline comparison is not a fair apples-to-apples comparison as the SWM model was used to evaluate AVD's predicted frames via VQA, unfairly benefiting SWM's semantic reward structure. The comparison lacks rigor for the major claim that semantic models are better than pixel reconstruction.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Evaluation is limited to simple simulated tabletop tasks with short horizons, no real-robot trials, and missing comparisons to language-space/CoT-style planners or semantic reward models trained directly from pixels.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because the experimental validation is not convincing enough to back up its conceptual claims (unfair baseline comparisons, limited evaluation scope), not because the novel idea of semantic world models lacks merit.

paper_title: Radio Frequency Ray Tracing via Stochastic Geometry

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The paper presents an elegant theoretical framework combining stochastic geometry with neural ray tracing for RF propagation, but the experimental evaluation is critically inadequate with no analysis of learned fields, missing ablation studies, and narrow dataset coverage.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The paper lacks analysis of learned fields (material, attenuation, phase parameters), ablation studies for design choices like Laplacian regularization and anisotropy terms, and simulation experiments with ground-truth parameters to verify the theory.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: The exponential transport model borrowed from computer graphics is not adequately justified for RF propagation, which involves more complex scattering, diffraction, and frequency-dependent effects that violate the independence and smoothness conditions required for exponential attenuation.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because the experimental evaluation is insufficient (missing field analysis, ablations, and proper baselines), not because the theoretical framework combining stochastic geometry with RF propagation modeling is conceptually flawed.

paper_title: Multi-Cultural Preference Optimization of Reward Models

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The paper addresses an important problem in pluralistic alignment but suffers from logical inconsistencies in the method (filtering removes agreeing pairs while weighting rewards agreement), undefined key terms, and inadequate experimental validation without rebuttal response.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The core weighting mechanism contradicts the filtering step (filtering removes pairs that agree with global RM while weighting assigns higher weights to more similar preferences), and the key term 'extremeness' is never mathematically defined despite being central to the weighting objective in Eq. 4.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: The evaluation only assesses reward model accuracy without demonstrating downstream effects on policy alignment or generation quality, and lacks harm analysis to verify the method doesn't entrench harmful cultural norms.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because the method has logical inconsistencies (filtering vs weighting contradiction) and undefined key terms (extremeness), not because the problem of multi-cultural preference alignment is unimportant.

paper_title: Accurate Estimation of Mutual Information in High Dimensional Data

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The paper assembles existing techniques (early stopping, VSIB, subsampling-extrapolation) into a practical protocol, but three of four reviewers questioned whether this synthesis constitutes sufficient novelty, and theoretical foundations remain inadequately justified.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The individual components (early stopping, VSIB probabilistic critics, subsampling-extrapolation) are established techniques, and the synthesis while practically useful does not meet the threshold for methodological contribution expected at this venue.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Theoretical foundations are inadequate - the stopping heuristic and linear extrapolation lack formal guarantees, and reviewer concerns about these theoretical foundations were met with appeals to impossibility results rather than novel theoretical analysis.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because the contribution lacks sufficient novelty (assembling existing techniques rather than introducing new methodology), not because the practical protocol for MI estimation is without value.

paper_title: Scaling up Multi-Turn Off-Policy RL and Multi-Agent Tree Search for LLM Step-Provers

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The paper achieves strong SOTA results on theorem proving but fails to demonstrate that the substantial computational cost is justified by proportional benefits, and evaluation lacks sufficient ablation studies to isolate component contributions.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The computational cost of the method is extremely high (multi-turn expert iteration, pass@8192 evaluation), raising questions about scalability and practical utility without clear evidence that the improvements justify such costs.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Missing ablation studies to demonstrate the effectiveness of individual components (adaptive filtering, periodic retraining, planner), and evaluation limited to only two datasets (ProofNet and MiniF2F) without PutnamBench or other benchmarks.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because the experimental evaluation raises serious feasibility concerns (prohibitive computational cost) and lacks ablation studies, not because the technical approach to theorem proving lacks merit.

paper_title: Level Up: Defining and Exploiting Transitional Problems for Curriculum Learning

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The method has a chicken-and-egg problem requiring a pre-trained oracle model to define the curriculum, and the self-referential evaluation framework (training on level k problems makes you better at level k problems) is not a convincing demonstration of improved general task competence

main_rejection_cause.reason: The method requires an existing pre-trained oracle model to define the curriculum, creating an inherent paradox where one must first perform a less efficient stage of training to enable more efficient learning later. This limits practical applicability and has not been resolved despite rebuttal.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: The evaluation framework is self-referential: showing training on level k problems makes a model better at level k problems is an expected result and not a convincing demonstration of improved general task competence. No evidence that chaining local level-up steps leads to globally better training.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because the method has an inherent feasibility problem (requires pre-trained oracle model) and self-referential evaluation, not because of lack of conceptual novelty.

paper_title: Splines-Based Feature Importance in Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks: A Framework for Supervised Tabular Data Dimensionality Reduction

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The method lacks sufficient theoretical justification and fails to demonstrate clear performance advantages over existing feature selection methods, with inconsistent results across variants

main_rejection_cause.reason: Using KAN's interpretability for feature importance has been explored in prior work (GeKAN, Interpretable graph KANs for cancer classification), and the proposed methods do not demonstrate fundamentally new capabilities. The paper fails to convincingly differentiate from existing KAN-based feature selection approaches.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Experiments rely on outdated datasets (some from 1993) and fail to include comparisons with existing KAN-based feature selection methods. Performance gains are either inconsistent or fail to highlight advantages of using KANs for feature importance.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of limited novelty and outdated datasets, not because the experiments were poorly presented.

paper_title: Fuzzy-Gated Training for Transformers: Length-Aware Priors and Gain-Aware Control

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The paper has insufficient experimental validation (only WikiText-2), weak baseline comparisons, and poor presentation clarity despite the interesting late-phase optimization problem motivation

main_rejection_cause.reason: Experiments are restricted to only WikiText-2 with no tests on time-series or equities datasets mentioned in the paper. No quantitative ablations isolating RPA vs baselines, Guardian on/off, or context game on/off are provided.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Baseline comparisons use unoptimized baselines (SFT Pythia-70M) instead of SOTA small/medium LMs or late-phase optimization methods. The gains are marginal and could indicate meta-overfitting given the complex method with many hyperparameters.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of limited experimental scope and weak baseline comparisons, not because the underlying idea was uninteresting.

paper_title: RAMM: Robust Adversarial Multimodal Learning for Protein Stability Prediction

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The adversarial training effectiveness is questionable from ablations and mathematics standpoint, and performance relies on non-standard validation procedure rather than demonstrating clear superiority

main_rejection_cause.reason: When standard validation procedure is applied (cDNA117K and T2837 datasets), the proposed method is outperformed by baseline Stability Oracle (0.45 vs 0.61 Pearson). The comparison is also unfair as RAMM uses XGBoost head while baselines use MLP. The paper relies on non-standard validation procedure to show performance gains.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: The mathematical justification for adversarial training (key contribution) is not adequately addressed. The paper claims mutation-invariant features in abstract but mutation-aware latent space in text, which are contradictory claims. Key theoretical foundations like GAN equations are not properly cited.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of experimental soundness issues and unfair comparisons, not because the problem addressed was unimportant.

paper_title: Intra-Prompt Parallel Decoding for Common-Context Question Answering

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The method lacks novelty as it appears to be a special case of existing tree-based decoding methods, and direct comparisons to strong baselines are missing

main_rejection_cause.reason: IPPD is essentially a special case of tree-based decoding methods (SpecInfer, DeFT, FastTree, FlashForge), which already proposed parallel decoding of requests with shared context. The paper fails to convincingly demonstrate how IPPD is fundamentally distinct from these existing approaches.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Direct experimental comparisons with strong baselines (Cascade Inference, DeFT, FastTree) are absent despite these methods having similar objectives. This makes it difficult to assess the true novelty and relative advantages of the proposed approach.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of limited novelty relative to existing tree-based decoding methods, not because the method was poorly motivated or explained.

paper_title: Feature Augmentation of GNNs for ILPs: Local Uniqueness Suffices

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Theoretical results are contentious with proofs described as 'unreadable', and the paper's positioning remains unclear between general GNN contribution and L2O-specific application

main_rejection_cause.reason: The theoretical component remains contentious; one reviewer explicitly described the appendix proofs as 'unreadable', the expressivity argument glosses over critical steps by delegating to external references, and the generalization bound is misaligned with experiments (theory for graph-level binary classification vs. node-level solution prediction in ILP benchmarks)

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: The crucial d hyperparameter is not thoroughly tested (one reviewer noted experiments only tested d=1), and baseline comparisons are limited. Additionally, ZINC dataset was included despite having no relevance to the ILP motivation, and the coloring runtime is not contextualized against GNN inference time

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because the theoretical results are contentious with proofs described as unreadable and the method's positioning remains unclear, not because the core idea of local d-hop identifiers lacks merit.

paper_title: ProcessLID: Step-wise Internal Reward in LLM Reasoning via Local Intrinsic Dimension

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Incremental novelty extending existing LID techniques to step-level reasoning without fundamentally new principles, and limited inference-time evaluation scope

main_rejection_cause.reason: The contribution is described as an incremental extension of existing LID work to step-level reasoning rather than introducing fundamentally new principles; the paper adapts existing techniques without addressing the main challenge of handling long and unsegmented reasoning trajectories where step boundaries are ambiguous

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Inference-time experiments are limited to 150 MATH-500 questions and two generators, with no integration into generation processes like beam search or pruning. Additionally, out-of-domain generalization relying on in-domain reference trajectories remains untested, and the fixed 100-token step segmentation is not well justified

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because the novelty is incremental, extending existing LID techniques without fundamental new principles, not because the step-level correctness estimation problem lacks importance.

paper_title: On the Role of Preference Variance in Preference Optimization

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Theoretical claims about PVar determining DPO gradient upper bound are overstated and do not fully justify why high-PVar samples should be retained, plus marginal improvements over baselines

main_rejection_cause.reason: The theoretical upper bounds only explain why low-PVar samples should be filtered out but not why high-PVar samples should be retained; the paper presents faster loss convergence as empirical evidence but this cannot directly prove the claim since convergence is also influenced by gradient direction consistency and data distribution

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: No clear secondary rejection cause is supported by the reviews.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because the theoretical claims are overstated and do not fully justify the method, not because the PVar filtering idea lacks clarity or practical value.

paper_title: LieDynNet: Learning Lie Symmetries from Spatiotemporal Data

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Limited novelty with respect to prior work (closure loss from Forestano et al., flow-based loss from Ko et al.), and disputed prior-free claim since PDE surrogate requires equation residuals

main_rejection_cause.reason: The paper combines existing loss terms that were already proposed in prior work (closure loss by Forestano et al. and flow-based loss by Ko et al.), making the novelty incremental rather than introducing fundamentally new principles or mechanisms

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: The claim of being prior-free is disputed because the PDE surrogate is trained with equation residuals requiring prior knowledge of the governing equations; while the subsequent symmetry learning stage may be prior-free, this is not true for the entire method with all components combined

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because the novelty is limited to combining existing loss terms and the prior-free claim is disputed, not because the goal of discovering Lie symmetries from data lacks importance.

paper_title: Training Variable Long Sequences With Data-centric Parallel

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Only synthetic data used in experiments without real workloads, and insufficient novelty as the paper lacks comparisons to existing works on variable-length sequence training efficiency

main_rejection_cause.reason: All experiments rely solely on synthetic datasets without any results on realistic workloads such as text or video sequence data; the paper uses Panda-70M as motivation but does not include any experimental results on this dataset or any other real dataset

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: The paper lacks comparison to existing works on efficient computation of variable-length sequences including HotSPa, FlexSP, WLB-LLM, and ByteScale, despite these methods addressing similar problems with dynamic sequence/context parallel approaches

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because experiments only use synthetic data without real workloads and lack comparisons to existing work, not because the core idea of data-centric parallelism for variable-length sequences lacks merit.

paper_title: Agent-Chained Policy Optimization

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The paper was rejected primarily due to insufficient experimental comparisons (limited baselines, missing key MARL algorithms), not because of methodological concerns.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The paper only compares against on-policy methods (MAPPO/HAPPO), omitting key MARL algorithms such as VDN, QMIX, MADDPG, and COMIX. This makes it difficult to properly situate ACPO's contribution within the broader MARL landscape.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: ACPO is 3-4x slower than MAPPO, which is a significant practical drawback that limits the method's applicability in real-world scenarios.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of insufficient baselines and high computational cost in experiments, not because of its novel theoretical framework or convergence guarantees.

paper_title: Designing Observation and Action Models for Efficient Reinforcement Learning with LLMs

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The paper was rejected primarily due to insufficient theoretical grounding and dependence on detailed human specifications, not solely because of experimental limitations.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The framework's success heavily depends on access to pre-existing, human-engineered environment structure and well-defined reward signals. Reviewers felt the system acts more as a 'code translator' for detailed human specifications rather than performing autonomous conceptual design.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: No clear secondary rejection cause is supported by the reviews.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of insufficient theoretical grounding and the framework's dependence on detailed human specifications rather than autonomous design, not because of weak empirical results.

paper_title: Just Enough Thinking: Efficient Reasoning with Adaptive Length Penalties Reinforcement Learning

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The paper was rejected primarily due to limited novelty relative to existing difficulty-aware reward shaping work, not because of weak empirical performance.

main_rejection_cause.reason: ALP lies within a rapidly growing line of work on adaptive reasoning and difficulty-aware reward shaping (e.g., LASER, AdaptThink, R1-style approaches). The distinction—online continuous scaling versus precomputed targets—is incremental and not convincingly shown to yield fundamentally new capabilities.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: The paper lacks decisive ablation studies. Without controlled experiments removing the solve-rate term or comparing against simple uniform length penalties under identical training conditions, it remains unclear whether gains stem from the difficulty-aware design or general length regularization.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of limited novelty relative to prior difficulty-aware reasoning work, not because of poor empirical results.

paper_title: Beyond Loss Guidance: Using PDE Residuals as Spectral Attention in Diffusion Neural Operators

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The paper was rejected primarily due to soundness concerns about the physical residual calculation and unfair experimental comparisons, not because of lack of innovation.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The physical residual calculation for Navier-Stokes equations is flawed. Taking divergence of vorticity magnitude or other vector operations as implemented is incorrect, making all arguments for physical embedding questionable. Additionally, PRISMA uses more prior knowledge (PDE equations, noise types) during training compared to baselines that are truly data-driven.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: The comparison is unfair because PRISMA explicitly leverages prior knowledge of the governing PDE while baselines are purely data-driven. Without training baselines (e.g., FNO/PINO) with noise augmentation, claims of state-of-the-art performance on noisy observations are unproven.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of soundness concerns about the physical residual calculation and unfair experimental comparisons, not because of lack of innovation.

paper_title: Retina Vision Transformer (RetinaViT): Measuring the Importance of Spatial Frequencies in Vision Transformers

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The paper was rejected primarily due to limited novelty relative to existing multi-scale transformers and weak empirical validation, not because of unclear writing.

main_rejection_cause.reason: RetinaViT does not incorporate hierarchical or cross-scale attention mechanisms within transformer blocks, unlike prior multi-scale transformers (PVT, CrossViT, ResFormer). The architectural contribution is shallow, as it only adds multi-scale patch concatenation and a heuristic positional embedding scaling without clear advantages over existing approaches.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: The experimental evaluation is limited to ImageNet-1K classification only. No comparisons with standard ViTs or established multi-scale transformer baselines trained under identical conditions. The marginal performance gains (+0.1-0.2pp at standard depths) do not justify the approach without demonstrating clear benefits on dense prediction tasks where multi-scale processing is most critical.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of limited novelty relative to existing multi-scale transformers and incomplete experiments, not because of unclear presentation.

paper_title: First Things First: Teaching LLM-Based Agents to Prioritize Must-Haves before Nice-to-Haves

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Limited innovation and insufficient experimental comparisons; the core method is a combination of existing techniques without substantial conceptual advancement, and comparative experiments are weak with missing horizontal comparisons with other strategies.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The paper's core idea does not deviate from the existing benchmark paradigm of instruction following + multi-scenario verification, and the multi-objective reward function is primarily a combination of existing technologies without substantial conceptual advancement.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Comparative experiments are weak - only performance before and after using FTF-RL is compared without horizontal comparison with other strategies, and ablation experiments are incomplete (only demonstrating R_requirement's role).

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of limited innovation and weak comparative experiments, not because the requirement-aware reasoning concept lacks importance.

paper_title: VizAgentBench: Benchmarking Multimodal Agent Reasoning on Coordinated Multi-View Visual Analytics Tasks

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Insufficient benchmark scale, missing human baselines, potential GPT-4.1 question generation bias, and lack of detailed analysis and reproducibility - the benchmark lacks diversity and statistical robustness while reviewers question whether it provides clear methodological insights.

main_rejection_cause.reason: Only 192 dashboards and questions may not ensure sufficient diversity or statistical robustness; lack of human baselines makes it impossible to judge whether the 44% accuracy stems from AI limitations or benchmark complexity.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Question generation by GPT-4.1 may introduce bias favoring OpenAI models during evaluation; manual inspection lacks measurable inter-rater reliability.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of benchmark scale and evaluation design issues, not because the interactive multi-view visualization reasoning problem lacks significance.

paper_title: Representation Drift Compensation: A Zero-Cost Enhancement for LLM Decomposition

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Limited innovation relative to prior work (FLAP), theoretical analysis concerns (Proposition 1 correctness questioned), and incomplete experimental comparisons - the method appears incremental over existing bias-correction approaches for other compression types.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The core idea of learning bias corrections is incremental - FLAP already uses bias correction for pruning, and this work essentially adapts it for decomposition without substantial conceptual advancement.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Proposition 1's theoretical analysis has correctness concerns - a reviewer identified that the closed-form solution c* = Eμ always yields zero error, contradicting the claimed theoretical bound.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of limited novelty over FLAP and theoretical analysis issues, not because the representation drift concept lacks importance.

paper_title: Continuous Time Series Generation with Irregular Observations

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Unclear motivation for MoE in NCDE context, unjustified CDE choice over simpler alternatives (ODE/SDE), and limited innovation - the method appears to be an assembly of existing modules without clear theoretical or empirical justification for the specific design choices.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The overall framework is an assembly of existing modules (NCDE, MoE, decoupled training, diffusion models); the main novelty lies in combining them without introducing new theoretical mechanisms.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Unclear problem statement, understated components, missing explanation of pretraining and router training, and unjustified choice of CDE over ODE/SDE for continuous trajectory generation.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of limited innovation and unclear design motivations, not because the time series generation task lacks importance.

paper_title: Decoupling Planning and Control for Instructable Agents

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Limited conceptual novelty over prior hierarchical VLA/MARL frameworks (DEPS, LS-Imagine, JARVIS-1), insufficient baseline comparisons, and unquantified compute overhead in multi-agent settings - the paper emphasizes engineering integration without convincingly distinguishing conceptual novelty.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The proposed planner-controller architecture is not sufficiently novel; similar hierarchical designs have been explored in prior works (DEPS, LS-Imagine, JARVIS-1), and the contribution emphasizes engineering integration and plug-and-play flexibility over conceptual breakthrough.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Missing comparison with end-to-end VLA models (RT-2, RT-H) and centralized-training/decentralized-execution MARL methods (QMIX); multi-task generalization is not addressed despite being a key evaluation dimension.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of limited conceptual novelty and incomplete baseline comparisons, not because the decoupling of planning from control lacks significance.

paper_title: SymLight: Exploring Interpretable and Deployable Symbolic Policies for Traffic Signal Control

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: The contribution is primarily incremental, with core approach closely aligned with existing literature on MCTS-based traffic control and symbolic policy discovery; additionally, scalability to city-scale deployments and experimental breadth are insufficient.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The core approach of using MCTS to search for interpretable symbolic policies remains closely aligned with existing literature. The incremental contributions (encoding choices, PSR, adaptive reward normalization) do not clearly amount to a conceptual advance commensurate with ICLR expectations.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Evaluation is confined to a single simulator and six networks, insufficient to support broader claims about general deployability, robustness, and superiority over alternative learning paradigms.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of limited novelty relative to existing MCTS and symbolic policy works, not because the interpretability goal or empirical results on CityFlow are uninteresting.

paper_title: Leveraging MLLMs for Zero-Shot Action Recognition: Concise, Discriminative and anti-Hallucination Prompting

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Zero-shot generalizability is undermined by the confused-pair dictionary requiring test data access, and experiments lack testing on state-of-the-art video LLMs and complex video understanding benchmarks.

main_rejection_cause.reason: The evaluation lacks experiments on modern, stronger MLLMs (Qwen3-VL, InternVL2/3) and complex video understanding benchmarks (ActivityNet-QA, Something-Something V2).

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: The confused-pair dictionary requires access to test dataset for construction, undermining zero-shot generalizability when applied to new data distributions.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of insufficient evaluation on modern video LLMs and limited zero-shot generalizability due to test-data-dependent dictionary construction, not because the prompt design or hallucination detection ideas lack merit.

paper_title: INSEva: A Comprehensive Chinese Benchmark for Large Language Models in Insurance

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Only 20% of dataset is publicly available (up from 10%), creating significant reproducibility barriers; benchmark saturation with ~84% average scores limits long-term utility.

main_rejection_cause.reason: Only 20% of the benchmark is publicly available due to commercial constraints, creating a significant barrier to reproducibility and making the paper's main claims unverifiable.

secondary_rejection_cause.reason: Benchmark saturation with average scores reaching ~84% across most tasks indicates insufficient headroom for differentiating future, more capable models. Also lacks detailed error analysis and failure mode breakdowns.

final_one_sentence_conclusion: This paper was mainly rejected because of limited reproducibility due to only 20% dataset disclosure and benchmark saturation concerns, not because the taxonomy or evaluation framework lacks value.

paper_title: SplitQuant: Efficient Low-Bit Quantization for Diffusion Transformers via In-Channel Dimension Splitting

overall_summary.main_rejection_reason: Missing key experimental evidence (Wan2.1 results absent from main text), unclear efficiency claims without end-to-end evaluation, and limited baseline comparisons.
